docs.title: pyrox
docs.text:
Probabilistic modeling with Equinox and NumPyro: Bayesian neural networks, Gaussian processes, and composable GP building blocks.

pyrox bridges Equinox modules and NumPyro traces so one module class can host deterministic parameters, random sample sites, priors, guides, and mode switching — without duplicating inference logic. NumPyro owns inference; pyrox just makes modules visible to it.

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
• pyrox._core — the Equinox-to-NumPyro bridge. PyroxModule, PyroxParam, PyroxSample, Parameterized, pyrox_method.
  • pyrox_gp — Gaussian process building blocks: kernels, sparse/variational GPs, non-Gaussian inference, pathwise samplers, multi-output GPs.
  • pyrox_nn — Bayesian and uncertainty-aware NN layers: dense variants, spectral layers, SNGP, ensembles, the Bayesian Neural Field stack.
  • pyrox_lgm — latent Gaussian models in precision form: GMRF components, PC priors, inla().
  • pyrox_ssm — state-space models as NumPyro models, whose inference recurses in time: Markov (Kalman) GPs over SDE kernels, sparse and non-Gaussian Markov GPs, the normalizing Kalman filter.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pyrox is not on PyPI yet, and the name pyrox on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project, so pip install pyrox installs the wrong package. Install from GitHub with uv:

uv add "pyrox @ git+https://github.com/jejjohnson/pyrox.git#subdirectory=packages/pyrox"
uv add "pyrox-gp @ git+https://github.com/jejjohnson/pyrox.git#subdirectory=packages/pyrox-gp"

pyrox-gp, pyrox-nn and pyrox-lgm also need a geonnax v0.0.11 override until kernellib pins that version; the README has the details.

docs.title: Pattern A — pure Equinox module injected into a NumPyro model
docs.text:
import equinox as eqx
import numpyro
import numpyro.distributions as dist


def model(x, y=None):
    net = MLP(key=key)  # any eqx.Module
    W = numpyro.sample("W", prior)
    net = eqx.tree_at(lambda m: m.W, net, W)
    f = numpyro.deterministic("f", net(x))
    numpyro.sample("obs", dist.Normal(f, 0.1), obs=y)

docs.title: Pattern B — PyroxModule owns its probabilistic semantics
docs.text:
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro.distributions as dist
from pyrox._core import PyroxModule, pyrox_method


class BayesianLinear(PyroxModule):
    pyrox_name = "BayesianLinear"
    in_features: int
    out_features: int

    @pyrox_method
    def __call__(self, x):
        W = self.pyrox_sample(
            "weight",
            dist.Normal(0, 1).expand([self.in_features, self.out_features]).to_event(2),
        )
        b = self.pyrox_param("bias", jnp.zeros(self.out_features))
        return x @ W + b

docs.title: Pattern C — Parameterized for constrained params, priors, and guides
docs.text:
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro.distributions as dist
from pyrox._core import Parameterized, pyrox_method


class RBFKernel(Parameterized):
    pyrox_name = "RBFKernel"

    def setup(self):
        self.register_param(
            "variance",
            jnp.array(1.0),
            constraint=dist.constraints.positive,
        )
        self.register_param(
            "lengthscale",
            jnp.array(1.0),
            constraint=dist.constraints.positive,
        )
        self.set_prior("variance", dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0))
        self.autoguide("variance", "normal")

    @pyrox_method
    def __call__(self, X1, X2):
        v = self.get_param("variance")
        ls = self.get_param("lengthscale")
        sq = jnp.sum((X1[:, None] - X2[None, :]) ** 2 / ls**2, axis=-1)
        return v * jnp.exp(-0.5 * sq)

Switch kernel.set_mode("guide") to draw variational params instead of sampling the prior. "normal" autoguides respect the registered constraint via TransformedDistribution.

docs.title: Building with agents
docs.text: pyrox exists so that a model's random parameters live in the module that uses them, with stable site names, under every NumPyro handler. Coding agents tend to re-implement what they cannot see — a numpyro.sample wired into an Equinox module by hand, a GP marginal likelihood written out with cho_solve, a deep-ensemble loop — and each one loses scoping, caching or structure. pyrox ships three things that let them find it.

docs.title: The capability index
docs.text: The capability index lists every public name in the four packages, grouped by the module that defines it, with a one-line summary; then the public API of gaussx, kernellib and geonnax, which pyrox builds on. It is regenerated from the code and checked in the test suite, so it never drifts.

docs.title: The Claude Code plugin
docs.text:
The repository is a Claude Code plugin marketplace. In any project:

/plugin marketplace add jejjohnson/pyrox
/plugin install pyrox@pyrox

The plugin adds:

  • bayesian-models-with-pyrox (skill) — loads whenever a task puts priors on an Equinox module's parameters, writes a GP or Bayesian NN in NumPyro, or fits a latent Gaussian model: which package does what, the three modelling patterns, the rules (sites through the bridge, unique scopes, don't rebuild a Parameterized module), a worked example, and a "don't write it — use pyrox" table.
  • pyrox-reuse-reviewer (subagent) — a read-only check of a diff for modelling code pyrox already provides, and for bridge misuse.

docs.title: llms.txt
docs.text: For other agents and tools, the docs site serves llms.txt: a curated map of pyrox and its key pages.

docs.title: Rules for your project's AGENTS.md
docs.text:
Paste this into the agent instructions of a project that builds on pyrox:

## Probabilistic models: build on pyrox

This project uses pyrox (Equinox ↔ NumPyro bridge), pyrox-gp (GPs),
pyrox-nn (Bayesian layers) and pyrox-lgm (INLA). Before writing a module
with random parameters, a GP likelihood or prediction, a Bayesian layer, an
ensemble loop or a latent Gaussian model, search the capability index
(https://jejjohnson.github.io/pyrox/capabilities/) or the packages'
`__all__`, and compose what exists:

- Inside an Equinox module, register sites with `self.pyrox_sample` /
  `self.pyrox_param` in a method decorated with `@pyrox_method`
  (`from pyrox._core import PyroxModule, pyrox_method`), never
  `numpyro.sample` directly.
- Give two instances of one class in one model distinct `pyrox_name`s.
- Declare constrained parameters with priors and guides once, in a
  `Parameterized.setup()`; don't rebuild such a module with `eqx.tree_at` or
  pass it as a `jit` argument (close over it instead).
- GPs: `pyrox_gp.GPPrior` + `gp_factor` / `.condition(...).predict(...)`,
  the `pyrox_gp` kernels with `set_prior`; never `cho_solve` a Gram by hand.
- Check every model's site names under
  `numpyro.handlers.trace(numpyro.handlers.seed(model, 0))`, and that it
  recovers known parameters on simulated data.

docs.title: Working on pyrox itself
docs.text: Contributors (and their agents) follow AGENTS.md in the repository and the AGENTS.md of each package: the package map, what pyrox is built on, "reuse before you write", the contracts and the tests that enforce them, and recipe skills for adding layers, kernels, GP and LGM components.

docs.title: Capability index
docs.text: Every public name in the five pyrox packages (263 of them), each listed once at its public home and grouped by the module that defines it, with the first sentence of its docstring; then the public API of gaussx, kernellib, geonnax and functax, which the packages build on. Search this page before writing a helper: if what you need is here, compose it; if it is almost here, extend it where it lives. Regenerate with make capabilities after changing a public API (packages/pyrox/tests/test_capabilities.py checks it is current).

statistical_linear_regression function Moment-match a nonlinear conditional to a linear-Gaussian surrogate. submatrix function Sub-matrix A[I, J] of an operator, without forming the full matrix. sufficient_stats function Sufficient statistics (x, x xᵀ) of a Gaussian, over any batch axes. sum_of_kroneckers_sample function Sample from 𝒩(0, K) with a matrix-free Lanczos square root. sum_operator with structural dispatch. svd_low_rank_plus_diag function Build A = diag(a) + U diag(s) Vᵀ from a truncated SVD. svgp_variance_adjustment function SVGP variance adjustment operator Q = K_ℐℐ⁻¹ Σ_ℐ K_ℐℐ⁻¹ − K_ℐℐ⁻¹. symbolic_cholesky function Symbolic analysis of a sparse Cholesky factorisation (host, cached). symmetric_tag constant Re-exported from lineax. symmetrize function Symmetric part of the trailing two axes, removing round-off asymmetry. theta_design function Integration points and log-weights over hyperparameters θ. tikhonov_augment function Observation augmentation for tridiagonal_solve_batched function Solve independent tridiagonal systems over leading batch axes. tridiagonal_tag constant Re-exported from lineax. udl_decomposition function Factorise a symmetric block-tridiagonal precision as Λ_x = U D Uᵀ. udl_from_ssm_params function Build the UDLDecomposition of a Gauss-Markov chain's precision. udl_to_ssm_params function Read the equivalent Gauss-Markov docs.title: Upstream: kernellib
docs.text: Kernels (AbstractKernel, stationary and dot-product families), kernel operators and the pure kernel functions in kernellib.functional. pyrox-gp's kernels wrap these.

docs.title: kernellib
docs.text: Name Kind What it does AbstractEstimator class Configure, fit, predict. AbstractFeatureMap class A finite-dimensional approximation k(x, x') ≈ φ(x)ᵀ φ(x'). AbstractGraph class Weighted, undirected graph without self-loops. AbstractGreatCircleKernel class \(k(x, x') = \sigma^2\,\psi( heta(x, x') / c)\) on (lon, lat) inputs. AbstractKernel class Anything that produces a Gram matrix. AbstractMeshKernel class A kernel on a triangle mesh given by its Laplace-Beltrami spectrum. AbstractPointwiseKernel class A kernel defined by k(x, x'). AbstractSphereSeriesKernel class A kernel on \(S^2\) given by its Laplace-Beltrami spectrum \(\Phi(\lambda)\). AbstractStationaryKernel class k(x, x') = variance * shape(\|\|(x - x') / lengthscale\|\|²). ActiveDims class Apply a kernel to a subset of input dimensions. Advected class A frozen spatial field moving at a constant velocity. CKAAccumulator class Running mini-batch CKA (Nguyen, Raghu & Kornblith, 2021). Chordal class A Euclidean kernel on points of the sphere, \(k_0(R\,u(x), R\,u(x'))\). Constant class Constant kernel, k(x, x') = sigma^2. Cosine class Cosine kernel, sigma^2 cos(2 pi \|\|x - x'\|\| / p). Cubic class Cubic covariance model, compactly supported. CurlFree class Curl-free kernel: the covariance of a gradient field \(F = abla\Phi\). CurlFreeFeatures class Hilbert-space features of a curl-free 2-D vector field. Derivative class \(\partial_{x_i} \partial_{x'_j} k(x, x')\) for fixed input dimensions. DerivativeIndexed class Joint covariance of a GP's values and partial derivatives. Distance class Distance-induced kernel, k(x, x') = σ² (\|x\|^a + \|x'\|^a - \|x - x'\|^a) / 2. DivergenceFree class Divergence-free kernel: the covariance of a rotated gradient field. DivergenceFreeFeatures class Hilbert-space features of a divergence-free 2-D vector field. EARTH_RADIUS_KM constant Re-exported from builtins. EigenPro class Kernel regression by EigenPro-preconditioned SGD (Ma & Belkin, 2017). EigenProPreconditioner class Spectral correction state for EigenPro kernel SGD. Falkon class Nyström kernel ridge regression solved by Falkon (Rudi et al., 2017). FalkonInfo class Convergence report of a falkon_solve run. FalkonPreconditioner class The two upper-triangular Cholesky factors of the Falkon preconditioner. FastFoodFeatures class FastFood random features (Le, Sarlós & Smola, 2013) for any kernel with a spectral sampler. FastFoodParams class The random structure of a FastFood feature map. FeatureKernel class Inner product of features, \(k(x, x') = \langle \phi(x), \phi(x') angle\). GeneralizedCauchy class Generalized Cauchy covariance model. GeometricAnisotropy class A rotated, stretched stationary kernel: a correlation ellipse or ellipsoid. Gibbs class Gibbs kernel: a lengthscale that varies with location. Gneiting class Gneiting's non-separable space-time covariance. Graph class Sparse weighted graph: a static topology and traced edge weights. GraphEigenFeatures class Low-rank features of GraphMatern / GraphHeat from Laplacian eigenpairs. GraphHeat class Graph heat (diffusion) kernel on node indices. GraphMatern class Graph Matérn kernel on node indices (Borovitskiy et al., 2021). GraphTopology class Static, hashable edge list of an undirected graph without self-loops. GreatCircleAskey class Askey's truncated power kernel, \(\psi(t) = (1 - t)_+^ au\). GreatCircleCauchy class Generalized Cauchy kernel, \(\psi(t) = (1 + t^\alpha)^{- au/\alpha}\). GreatCircleExponential class Exponential kernel of the great-circle angle, \(\psi(t) = e^{-t}\). GreatCirclePoweredExponential class Powered exponential kernel, \(\psi(t) = e^{-t^\alpha}\). GreatCircleSpherical class The geostatistics spherical model of the great-circle angle. GreatCircleWendland class C²- or C⁴-Wendland kernel of the great-circle angle. GridGraph class Regular lattice graph that never stores its edges. Helmholtz class Helmholtz-decomposition kernel: curl-free plus divergence-free parts. HelmholtzFeatures class Helmholtz features: curl-free plus divergence-free columns. HoleEffect class Hole-effect (cardinal sine, "wave") covariance model. ImplicitCrossKernelOperator class Matrix-free rectangular kernel operator K(X, Z) \cdot v. ImplicitKernelOperator class Matrix-free kernel operator: (K + sigma^2 I) v via sequential scan. JunStein class Axially symmetric kernel of Jun & Stein (2008), \(L_x L_y k_0(x, y)\). KNNGraph class A directed k-nearest-neighbour graph, self excluded. KRR class Kernel ridge regression. KernelDensity class Weighted Parzen density \(\hat p(x) = rac1c\sum_i eta_i k(x, x_i)\). KernelLocalityPreservingProjections class Kernel locality preserving projections. KernelOperator class Kernel matrix operator with efficient first-order autodiff. KernelPCA class Kernel principal component analysis. KernelSchrodingerProjections class Kernel Schrödinger eigenmap projections. KroneckerFeatures class Features of a separable kernel \(k_s k_t\) as a product of two maps. LaplaceEigenfunctionFeatures class Hilbert-space (HSGP) approximation of a stationary kernel on a box. LaplacianEigenmaps class Laplacian eigenmaps (Belkin & Niyogi, 2003) of the k-NN graph of X. LatitudeScaled class Amplitude modulation by latitude, \(k(x, y) = s(\phi_x)\,s(\phi_y)\,k_0(x, y)\). LegendreLatitudeFn class A function of latitude, \(f(\phi) = \sum_{j=0}^{J-1} w_j\,P_j(\sin\phi)\). Linear class Linear kernel, k(x, x') = sigma^2 x^T x' + b. LinearTransform class A stationary kernel of a linearly transformed lag. LocalityPreservingProjections class Locality preserving projections (He & Niyogi, 2003). Matern class Matern kernel with closed-form nu in {0.5, 1.5, 2.5}. MeshHeat class Heat (diffusion) kernel on a triangulated surface. MeshLaplaceFeatures class FEM Laplace-Beltrami eigenvector features of a mesh kernel. MeshMatern class Matérn kernel on a triangulated surface (Borovitskiy et al. 2020). Modulated class A kernel with an input-dependent amplitude, \(k(x, x') = a(x)\, k_0(x, x')\, a(x')\). NystromFeatures class Nyström features (Williams & Seeger, 2001) for any kernel. OrthogonalRandomFeatures class Orthogonal random features (Yu et al., 2016). PaciorekSchervish class Paciorek-Schervish kernel: a location-dependent anisotropy matrix. Pentaspherical class Pentaspherical covariance model, compactly supported. Periodic class Periodic (MacKay) kernel on the Euclidean distance. PeriodicFeatures class Exact truncated Fourier features of a 1-D Periodic kernel. Periodised class Make any kernel periodic: apply it to inputs wrapped onto circles. PermutationTestResult class Outcome of permutation_test. Polynomial class Polynomial kernel, k(x, x') = sigma^2 (x^T x' + b)^d. Product class Elementwise product of kernels, k(x, x') = prod_i k_i(x, x'). RBF class Radial basis function (squared exponential) kernel. RandomAdvectionRBF class The frozen-field RBF averaged over a Gaussian velocity. RandomFourierFeatures class Random Fourier features (Rahimi & Recht, 2007). RationalQuadratic class Rational quadratic kernel, a scale mixture of RBFs. Residual class What an approximation misses, \(k(x, x') - ilde k(x, x')\). RootedTree class A tree with one root: every non-root node has exactly one parent. Scaled class A kernel times a scalar, k(x, x') = scale * k_0(x, x'). SchrodingerEigenmapProjections class Schrödinger eigenmap projections (SEP): linear Schrödinger eigenmaps. SchrodingerEigenmaps class Schrödinger eigenmaps (Czaja & Ehler, 2013) of the k-NN graph of X. Shift class Input warp x -> x - offset; offset is scalar or per dimension. SlepianFeatures class Features of a zonal kernel concentrated on a spherical cap. SphereHeat class Heat (diffusion, squared-exponential) kernel on the sphere. SphereMatern class Intrinsic Matérn kernel on the sphere (Borovitskiy et al. 2020). SphereSeries class A sphere kernel from any user spectrum \(\Phi(\lambda) \ge 0\). Spherical class Spherical covariance model, compactly supported. SphericalHarmonicFeatures class Weighted real spherical harmonics up to degree \(L\) for a zonal kernel. Stable class Stable (powered exponential) covariance model. Stretch class Input warp x -> x / scale; scale is scalar or per dimension. Sum class Sum of kernels, k(x, x') = sum_i k_i(x, x'). TailDown class Tail-down covariance on a rooted tree (Ver Hoef & Peterson, 2010). TailUp class Tail-up covariance on a rooted tree (Ver Hoef & Peterson, 2010). Tanh class Hyperbolic-tangent kernel, k(x, x') = sigma^2 tanh(gamma x^T x' + c0). Tapered class A covariance multiplied by a compactly supported taper. TaylorStatistics class The sides and angle of a kernel Taylor-diagram triangle. TreeSites class Pairwise geometry of N sites on a RootedTree (host-computed). Variogram class A binned empirical semivariogram. Warped class Apply a kernel to warped inputs, k(x, x') = k_0(w(x), w(x')). Wendland class Wendland covariance model, compactly supported. White class White-noise kernel, sigma^2 delta(x, x'). adjacency_matrix function Symmetric weighted adjacency matrix of a k-NN graph. barrier_potential function Diagonal potential that is strength at indices and 0 elsewhere. batched_kernel_matvec function Compute K(X, Z) @ v in memory-efficient batches. batched_kernel_rmatvec function Compute K(X, Z)^T @ u in memory-efficient batches. cka function Centred kernel alignment, \(\mathrm{HSIC}(x, y) / \sqrt{\mathrm{HSIC}(x, x)\,\mathrm{HSIC}(y, y)}\). combine_potentials function Several Schrödinger potentials as one: \(\sum_k \alpha_k c_k V_k\). commute_time_kernel function Commute-time kernel \(K = L^{+}\), the Laplacian's pseudo-inverse. cosine_graph_kernel function Inverse-cosine kernel \(K = \cos(\pi L / 4)\) (Smola & Kondor, 2003). curl function Per-point curl of a 2-D or 3-D vector field. delaunay_graph function The edge graph of the Delaunay triangulation of X. derivative_inputs function Rows [x, i] for DerivativeIndexed: values, then partials. diffusion_kernel function Diffusion (heat) kernel \(K = \exp(- eta L)\) (Kondor & Lafferty, 2002). distance_correlation_squared function Squared distance correlation (Székely et al., 2007), cka. distance_covariance_squared function Squared distance covariance (Székely et al., 2007), 4 * hsic. divergence function Per-point divergence \( abla \cdot F(x_n) = \operatorname{tr} J_n\). draw_rff_cosine_basis function Draw (variance, lengthscale, omega, phase, weights) for a kernel. edge_weights function Reweight a graph's edges by a kernel on the nodes' features. eigenpro_correction function Compute the EigenPro eigenspace correction for one SGD mini-batch. eigenpro_preconditioner function Build an EigenPro spectral preconditioner from a kernel operator. eigenpro_step_size function Return the EigenPro preconditioned step size for a batch size. empirical_variogram function Binned empirical semivariogram of y observed at X. energy_distance function Energy distance (Székely & Rizzo, 2004), 2 * mmd_squared. estimate_lengthscale function A data-driven lengthscale for an RBF-type kernel. evaluate_rff_cosine_paths function Evaluate the zero-mean RFF prior path(s) at inputs X. falkon_preconditioner function Build the Falkon preconditioner from the inducing-point kernel matrix. falkon_predict function Predict with Nyström KRR weights: \(f(x_*) = \sum_j \alpha_j\, Nearest class Nearest neighbour on every axis: one tap per target, weight 1. NearestBasis class Nearest neighbour: one tap, the closer of i and i + 1, with weight 1. NonlinearDerivativePlan class ∂ᵐf̂/∂xᵐ of a nonlinear series plan: it reads, but has no fixed operator. NonlinearPlan class A plan whose fit depends on y: no fixed operator or adjoint, but linearize. Pchip class Monotone piecewise cubic Hermite (Fritsch-Carlson), as SciPy's PCHIP. Plan class f̂(X*) = H 𝒮(y), fitted once, applied to many fields. Policies class Outside the domain, at missing samples, and at the edges. Polyharmonic class The polyharmonic spline φ(r) = ±rᵏ for odd k, ±rᵏ log r for even k. PosteriorCovariance class Σ*, the (M, M) posterior covariance of the field at M targets. RBF class Radial basis function interpolation: f̂(x) = ∑ⱼ cⱼ k(x, xⱼ) + ∑ₚ bₚ pₚ(x). RadialKernel class k(x, x′) = φ(‖x − x′‖), Euclidean in the coordinates as given. ReadGeometry class What a plan's stencil was built from, so Plan.derivative can rebuild it. Readout class c → f̂(X*): the read-out of a plan, from coefficients to target values. Scheme class An interpolation scheme: configuration, frozen into a Plan by plan. SeriesInterpolant class A 1-D series field f̂ read at targets chosen inside the trace. SeriesScheme class A scheme on one axis with a cubic Hermite read-out and its own slopes. Steffen class Steffen's monotone cubic: no overshoot between knots, by construction. Stencil class A sparse read-out H: row k reads S source values at flat indices. Tensor class One local scheme per source axis, as one tensor stencil. TransposedStencil class f̂ = diag(s) Hᵀ y: a sampling stencil H used backwards, scaled per cell. Wendland class The compact Wendland kernel φ(r) = ψ(r/ρ), zero for r ≥ ρ. WindowedPlan class plan[window]: the rows of a grid target inside a window, sources unchanged. bspline function The centred B-spline βᵏ of degree k at x. check_outside function Enforce outside="raise" on the host; no-op for every other policy. clenshaw function The Chebyshev series f(x) = ∑ₖ aₖ Tₖ(ξ(x)) by Clenshaw's recurrence. compose function H = H_outer H_inner: apply inner first, then outer, as one stencil. index_positions function The fractional index position u of each target, so node j sits at u = j. locate function The cell index i, the offset t ∈ [0, 1) and the inside flag of each target. locate_curvilinear function The cell (r, c), the offset (s, t) and the inside flag of targets on a swath. overlap_weights_1d function The (M, N) overlap lengths |cⱼ ∩ Cᵢ| of every target and source cell. plan_key function sha256 hex of the scheme, the policies and both geometries' bytes. remap_taps function Bring tap indices back onto [0, N − 1] by a boundary rule. spline_poles function The poles zₚ of the order-k B-spline prefilter, as in scipy.ndimage. tensor_stencil function H = H₁ ⊗ … ⊗ H_D: one local basis per source axis, read at the targets.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: This page documents the label taxonomy, epic model, and issue conventions used in this project.

docs.title: Label Taxonomy
docs.text:
Every issue carries exactly one type:*, one or more area:*, one pkg:* for each workspace package it touches (none for repo-wide work such as build, CI or the roadmap), at most one layer:*, one wave:*, and one priority:*.

Scope Labels Type type:epic-wave, type:epic-theme, type:feature, type:design, type:chore, type:docs, type:bug, type:research Area area:engineering, area:testing, area:docs, area:code — extend per project (e.g. area:algorithmic, area:integration) Package pkg:core (the pyrox core), pkg:gp, pkg:nn, pkg:lgm, pkg:ssm, so the issues of one package can be searched with label:pkg:ssm Layer layer:0-primitives, layer:1-components, layer:2-models — only if the project has a formal layer stack Wave wave:0, wave:1, wave:2, … — release-scoped phases (add wave:N-<slug> variants for descriptive labels) Priority priority:p0 (blocker), priority:p1 (high), priority:p2 (normal)

Bootstrap the standard set on a fresh repo:

make gh-labels

The script lives at .github/scripts/create-labels.sh. Edit the hard-coded create … entries in the script to customise area:*, layer:*, and wave:* for the project, then re-run — the script is idempotent.

docs.title: Two-Layer Epic Model
docs.text:
Work is organised as Wave → Theme → Issue:

[EPIC] Wave N   (L1)   —   release-scoped mega-epic, owns a milestone
  ├── [EPIC] <theme>   (L2)   —   parallel-safe group of issues
  │     ├── feature / design / chore / bug issue
  │     └── …
  └── [EPIC] <theme>   (L2)
        └── …
  • Wave epic (type:epic-wave) maps one-to-one with a milestone (vX.Y-<slug>). Groups several Theme epics that can run in parallel.
  • Theme epic (type:epic-theme) groups concrete issues that ship together as a coherent slice. Themes inside a wave are parallel-safe unless the body says otherwise.
  • Issue (feature / design / chore / bug) is the leaf — a single substantial deliverable that rolls up to a Theme epic.

Stragglers are discouraged: any type:feature issue should attach to a Theme epic. If no suitable theme exists, create one first.

docs.title: Issue Format
docs.text:
Issue templates live in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/:

Template When to use Epic — Wave (L1) Opening a new release-scoped wave Epic — Theme (L2) Grouping related issues inside a wave Feature / Enhancement One substantial deliverable Design / ADR Resolve an open design question for a new API Bug report Something isn't working Research / Comparative Analysis Study prior art (external repo, paper) and produce a prioritized roadmap of follow-up issues

Feature + Design templates include two optional sections for context-heavy issues:

  • Design Snapshot — paste API sketches, code examples, or excerpts from private / external design docs so the issue is self-contained.
  • Mathematical Notes — equations, sign conventions, numerical considerations.

Delete either section if not relevant. Both exist so that an implementer (human or AI agent) can work on the issue without opening other repos or channels.

docs.title: Creating issues
docs.text: New issues should use one of the templates in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ so that labels, required sections, and title conventions are consistent.

docs.title: From the UI
docs.text: Click New issue on the repo's Issues tab and pick a template. The body is pre-filled with the section scaffolding — fill in, apply labels and milestone, submit.

docs.title: From the CLI
docs.text:
For drafted content, write the body to a file (minus the template's YAML frontmatter), then:

gh issue create \
  --title "feat(primitives): diagonal BLR update step" \
  --body-file /tmp/issue-body.md \
  --label "type:feature,area:algorithmic,layer:0-primitives,wave:1,priority:p1" \
  --milestone "v0.1-diagonal"

To open the UI in a browser with a template pre-selected:

gh issue create --web

The web flow opens /issues/new/choose so you can pick the template in the UI. gh issue create does not support pre-selecting a template for the web path; the --template flag is only used as starting body text in the non-web flow.

After the issue is created, apply native parent / blocked-by links via the Makefile targets documented below in the Relationships section (or make gh-sub / make gh-block).

docs.title: From Claude Code
docs.text:
The create-gh-issue skill (at .claude/skills/create-gh-issue/SKILL.md) guides Claude through:

  • Picking the right template (decision tree covering feature / design / bug / research / epic-wave / epic-theme)
  • Drafting the body with required sections + rename guidance for optional sections (Design Snapshot → Demo To Implement, etc.)
  • Applying the correct label set (which type:* + area:* + layer:* + wave:* + priority:* combos are valid for each work type)
  • Setting the milestone (which vX.Y-<slug> corresponds to the wave)
  • Applying relationships (chains to link-gh-issues skill for native sub-issue + blocked-by links)
  • Style conventions — unicode math, text code fences, code-first-prose-last
  • Bulk workflow — publishing a .plans/<wave>-backlog.md file into real GitHub issues (multi-pass: wave epic → theme epics → leaf issues → relationships), with draft-ID → GH-number mapping

Example prompts:

  • "Open a feature issue for the diagonal BLR update step, child of theme epic #27"
  • "File a design issue for the per-parameter prior question"
  • "Publish the drafts in .plans/wave-1-backlog.md as real issues and wire up the sub-issue links"
  • "Open a research issue comparing pof vs this project, based on my notes in <path>"

docs.title: Drafting a wave backlog
docs.text:
For large planning exercises (new wave, new release, large refactor), draft the whole backlog as one markdown file before opening GitHub issues. A template lives at docs/templates/wave-backlog.md.

Why:

  • Review the whole wave in one scroll instead of clicking through 15 half-drafted issues
  • Share context once at the top (Shared Context · Design Snapshot · Intended Package Layout · Runtime Boundary) rather than duplicating across every child issue
  • Stable draft IDs (<PREFIX>-01, <PREFIX>-02, …) let child issues reference each other before GitHub issue numbers exist

Workflow:

  1. Copy docs/templates/wave-backlog.md into your project's .plans/ directory (gitignored). Rename to describe the wave — e.g. .plans/wave-1-backlog.md.
  2. Pick a short project prefix (e.g. PYX for pyrox, OBX for optax_bayes). Number drafts sequentially.
  3. Fill in shared context at the top, then draft each issue body.
  4. When the file is ready, open each draft as a real GitHub issue using the matching .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/. Copy the body verbatim.
  5. Record GitHub issue numbers next to draft IDs in the backlog file, or replace draft IDs throughout. Update cross-references.
  6. Either delete the backlog file or archive it in .plans/archive/.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Use an explicit ## Relationships block at the bottom of each issue / epic body:

## Relationships
- Parent: #<theme-epic>
- Blocked by: #
- Blocks: #
- Related: #

GitHub's task-list feature links bidirectionally from the parent, so checklist items in a Theme epic body auto-show in the referenced issues.

docs.title: Applying native GitHub relationships
docs.text:
The prose ## Relationships block above is a human-readable record. GitHub also exposes two native relationship features that power the UI sub-issue panel and the dependency graph — apply both:

Prose line Native feature Mutation Parent: / Theme Epics / Issues checklist Sub-issues (parent ↔ child hierarchy) addSubIssue / removeSubIssue Blocked by: Typed dependency addBlockedBy Blocks: Inverse — applied on the OTHER issue addBlockedBy (on the blocked side) Related: No native feature prose only

docs.title: From the UI
docs.text:
• Sub-issues — open the parent issue, side-panel → Sub-issues → Create sub-issue or Add existing sub-issue.
  • Blocked by — open the blocked issue, side-panel → Development → Mark as blocked by.

docs.title: From the CLI (Makefile targets)
docs.text:
For scripted work, the repo ships a helper script wrapped by three make targets:

# Link children as sub-issues under a parent
make gh-sub PARENT=7 CHILDREN="42 43 44"

# Mark issue 44 as blocked by 43
make gh-block ISSUE=44 BLOCKED_BY=43

# Inspect parent / sub-issues / blocking / blocked-by for an issue
make gh-show ISSUE=44

Direct script usage (same functionality plus unlink commands):

bash .github/scripts/link-issues.sh sub     <parent> <child> [<child> ...]
bash .github/scripts/link-issues.sh block   <issue> <blocker>
bash .github/scripts/link-issues.sh unsub   <parent> <child>
bash .github/scripts/link-issues.sh unblock <issue> <blocker>
bash .github/scripts/link-issues.sh show    <issue>

The script resolves issue numbers to GraphQL node IDs automatically, and treats "already linked" as a no-op so re-runs are safe.

docs.title: From Claude Code
docs.text:
The link-gh-issues skill (at .claude/skills/link-gh-issues/SKILL.md) guides Claude through the same operations — useful for bulk-applying relationships from a drafted wave backlog, parsing the Issues checklist out of a theme epic body, or verifying that the native links match the prose.

Example prompts:

  • "Apply the relationships from epic #29"
  • "Link #42, #43, #44 as sub-issues of #7"
  • "Mark #44 as blocked by #43"
  • "What's blocking #44?" (Claude runs make gh-show ISSUE=44 or the underlying GraphQL query)

docs.title: Raw GraphQL (for reference)
docs.text:
Under the hood the helper runs:

mutation { addSubIssue(input: { issueId: "<parent-node-id>", subIssueId: "<child-node-id>" }) { subIssue { number } } }
mutation { addBlockedBy(input: { issueId: "<this-node-id>", blockingIssueId: "<blocker-node-id>" }) { issue { number } } }

Issue node IDs are resolved via gh api repos/:owner/:repo/issues/<N> --jq .node_id.

docs.title: Pre-commit checklist
docs.text:
Run these locally before opening a PR:

make format       # ruff format . + ruff check --fix .   (applies changes)
make lint         # ruff check .                         (CI-style check)
make typecheck    # ty check
make test         # pytest

Note that make format mutates files — it formats and applies autofixes. make lint is the CI-parity read-only check. Run make format first, commit the result, then run make lint / make test to verify.

Pre-commit hooks run ruff on every commit, using the same locked version (lint dependency group in uv.lock) as CI. Run make precommit to apply them to all files manually.

Commit messages follow the Conventional Commits specification — enforced on PR titles by .github/workflows/conventional-commits.yml.

docs.text: The pyrox_nn.api subpackage exposes sklearn-style immutable estimator facades. Each estimator wraps a pyrox_nn model + the inference runners in pyrox.inference behind a one-call fit/predict ergonomic.

class EstimatorBase(eqx.Module):
    """Immutable configuration for a probabilistic regression model.

    Attributes:
        feature_cols: Names of the input columns, in the order they
            should be packed into the design matrix.
        target_col: Name of the target column.
    """

    feature_cols: tuple[str, ...] = eqx.field(static=True)
    target_col: str = eqx.field(static=True)

    def fit(self, df: pd.DataFrame, *, seed: PRNGKeyArray | int) -> FittedEstimator:
        """Fit and return a new `FittedEstimator`.

        Subclasses override; ``EstimatorBase.fit`` raises.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"{type(self).__name__}.fit must be implemented by subclasses"
        )

class FittedEstimator(eqx.Module):
    """Output of `EstimatorBase.fit`.

    Subclasses store fitted parameters as `equinox.Module`
    fields and implement ``predict``. The base class enforces only
    the immutable-PyTree contract.
    """

    config: EstimatorBase

    def predict(
        self,
        df: pd.DataFrame,
        *,
        quantiles: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    ) -> Float[Array, " N"] | tuple[Float[Array, " N"], tuple[Float[Array, " N"], ...]]:
        """Predict targets for ``df``.

        Subclasses override; ``FittedEstimator.predict`` raises.

        Args:
            df: Inputs (must contain ``feature_cols``).
            quantiles: If given, return ``(mean, (q1, q2, ...))`` where
                ``q_i`` is the per-row predictive quantile at level
                ``quantiles[i]``. If ``None``, return only the mean.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"{type(self).__name__}.predict must be implemented by subclasses"
        )

docs.title: BNFEstimator
docs.text:
Bases: EstimatorBase

MAP-fit Bayesian Neural Field estimator.

Composes the BNF layer (pyrox_nn.BayesianNeuralField) with pandas-side preprocessing (pyrox_nn.preprocessing.fit_spatiotemporal) and an ensemble-MAP inference loop (pyrox.inference.ensemble_map).

Attributes:

Name Type Description feature_cols tuple[str, ...]

Input columns (first one is time).

target_col str

Target column.

width int

Hidden MLP width.

depth int

Hidden MLP depth.

observation_model ObservationModel

"NORMAL" (currently only this is fully implemented). "NB" and "ZINB" raise NotImplementedError until gaussx.mixture_quantile ships.

seasonality_periods tuple[float, ...]

Periods for seasonal features. Empty ⇒ no seasonal features.

num_seasonal_harmonics tuple[int, ...]

Harmonics per period.

fourier_degrees tuple[int, ...]

Per-input dyadic Fourier degrees. Length must match feature_cols (or empty ⇒ no Fourier features).

interactions tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]

Pair-index list for interaction features.

encoder Callable[[Array], Array] | None

Optional single-example encoder (C,) -> (E,) whose output enters the network as one extra gated feature block (see pyrox_nn.BayesianNeuralField), for example geonnax.SphericalHarmonicEncoder(l_max=10, input_mode="lonlat"). It receives encoder_cols in the DataFrame's own units: the estimator undoes its standardization of those columns first (the time column arrives encoded, as in the design matrix).

encoder_cols tuple[int, ...] | None

Indices into feature_cols fed to encoder, in order; required exactly when encoder is given.

timetype Literal['int', 'datetime']

"int" or "datetime".

freq str | None

Optional unit string for datetime time columns.

noise NoiseModel

"fixed" (default) keeps the noise scale \(\sigma_0\) at sigma_obs; "learned" infers it through the sample site log_sigma_obs \(= \log \sigma_0 \sim \mathcal N(\log \sigma_{\text{obs}}, 1)\), which the MAP and VI ensembles treat like any other latent. With prior_weight=0 (MLE) and no sigma_col nothing bounds \(\sigma_0\) below, so that combination raises ValueError.

sigma_obs float

Observation noise std \(\sigma_0\) when noise="fixed" (with sigma_col, a floor for representativeness error), or the prior median of \(\sigma_0\) when noise="learned".

sigma_col str | None

Optional column of per-row noise stds \(\sigma_i > 0\), in target units. Each row's likelihood is \(\mathcal N(f(x_i), \sigma_i^2 + \sigma_0^2)\). The target is not rescaled by the estimator, so \(\sigma_i\) is used as given.

ensemble_size int

Number of MAP ensemble members.

num_epochs int

SGD-MAP iterations per member.

learning_rate float

Adam learning rate.

prior_weight float

1 ⇒ MAP, 0 ⇒ MLE, fractional ⇒ tempered.

Source code in packages/pyrox-nn/src/pyrox_nn/api/_bnf.py 
class BNFEstimator(EstimatorBase):
    r"""MAP-fit Bayesian Neural Field estimator.

    Composes the BNF layer (`pyrox_nn.BayesianNeuralField`) with
    pandas-side preprocessing (`pyrox_nn.preprocessing.fit_spatiotemporal`)
    and an ensemble-MAP inference loop
    (`pyrox.inference.ensemble_map`).

    Attributes:
        feature_cols: Input columns (first one is time).
        target_col: Target column.
        width: Hidden MLP width.
        depth: Hidden MLP depth.
        observation_model: ``"NORMAL"`` (currently only this is fully
            implemented). ``"NB"`` and ``"ZINB"`` raise
            ``NotImplementedError`` until ``gaussx.mixture_quantile``
            ships.
        seasonality_periods: Periods for seasonal features. Empty ⇒
            no seasonal features.
        num_seasonal_harmonics: Harmonics per period.
        fourier_degrees: Per-input dyadic Fourier degrees. Length must
            match ``feature_cols`` (or empty ⇒ no Fourier features).
        interactions: Pair-index list for interaction features.
        encoder: Optional single-example encoder ``(C,) -> (E,)`` whose
            output enters the network as one extra gated feature block (see
            `pyrox_nn.BayesianNeuralField`), for example
            ``geonnax.SphericalHarmonicEncoder(l_max=10, input_mode="lonlat")``.
            It receives ``encoder_cols`` in the DataFrame's own units: the
            estimator undoes its standardization of those columns first (the
            time column arrives encoded, as in the design matrix).
        encoder_cols: Indices into ``feature_cols`` fed to ``encoder``, in
            order; required exactly when ``encoder`` is given.
        timetype: ``"int"`` or ``"datetime"``.
        freq: Optional unit string for ``datetime`` time columns.
        noise: ``"fixed"`` (default) keeps the noise scale $\sigma_0$ at
            ``sigma_obs``; ``"learned"`` infers it through the sample site
            ``log_sigma_obs`` $= \log \sigma_0 \sim \mathcal N(\log
            \sigma_{\text{obs}}, 1)$, which the MAP and VI ensembles treat
            like any other latent. With ``prior_weight=0`` (MLE) and no
            ``sigma_col`` nothing bounds $\sigma_0$ below, so that
            combination raises ``ValueError``.
        sigma_obs: Observation noise std $\sigma_0$ when ``noise="fixed"``
            (with ``sigma_col``, a floor for representativeness error), or
            the prior median of $\sigma_0$ when ``noise="learned"``.
        sigma_col: Optional column of per-row noise stds $\sigma_i > 0$, in
            target units. Each row's likelihood is
            $\mathcal N(f(x_i), \sigma_i^2 + \sigma_0^2)$. The target is not
            rescaled by the estimator, so $\sigma_i$ is used as given.
        ensemble_size: Number of MAP ensemble members.
        num_epochs: SGD-MAP iterations per member.
        learning_rate: Adam learning rate.
        prior_weight: ``1`` ⇒ MAP, ``0`` ⇒ MLE, fractional ⇒ tempered.
    """

    width: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=64)
    depth: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=4)
    observation_model: ObservationModel = eqx.field(static=True, default="NORMAL")
    seasonality_periods: tuple[float, ...] = eqx.field(static=True, default=())
    num_seasonal_harmonics: tuple[int, ...] = eqx.field(static=True, default=())
    fourier_degrees: tuple[int, ...] = eqx.field(static=True, default=())
    interactions: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...] = eqx.field(static=True, default=())
    encoder: Callable[[Array], Array] | None = None
    encoder_cols: tuple[int, ...] | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)
    timetype: Literal["int", "datetime"] = eqx.field(static=True, default="int")
    freq: str | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)
    noise: NoiseModel = eqx.field(static=True, default="fixed")
    sigma_obs: float = eqx.field(static=True, default=0.1)
    sigma_col: str | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)
    ensemble_size: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=16)
    num_epochs: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=2000)
    learning_rate: float = eqx.field(static=True, default=5e-3)
    prior_weight: float = eqx.field(static=True, default=1.0)
    inference_kind: InferenceKind = eqx.field(static=True, default="map")
    standardize_columns: tuple[str, ...] | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)
    # Optional guide factory for the VI path. Takes the numpyro model
    # function and returns a guide. Defaults to AutoNormal at fit-time
    # (mean-field). Pass `AutoLowRankMultivariateNormal`, `AutoIAFNormal`,
    # `AutoBNAFNormal`, or any other AutoGuide constructor for richer
    # variational families that can represent posterior weight
    # correlations the mean-field guide cannot.
    guide_factory: Callable[[Callable], Any] | None = eqx.field(
        static=True, default=None
    )

    def fit(self, df: pd.DataFrame, *, seed: PRNGKeyArray | int) -> FittedBNF:
        if self.observation_model != "NORMAL":
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f"observation_model={self.observation_model!r} requires "
                "gaussx.mixture_quantile (tracked as gaussx#121). Use "
                "observation_model='NORMAL' for now."
            )
        if self.noise not in ("fixed", "learned"):
            # A BayesianNeuralField returns the field alone, so it cannot be
            # heteroscedastic.
            raise ValueError(f"noise must be 'fixed' or 'learned'; got {self.noise!r}.")
        # sigma_obs, the inference kind and learned noise under MLE are
        # validated by NeuralFieldEstimator.fit, after the preprocessing.
        # 1. Pandas-side preprocessing → SpatiotemporalFit bundle.
        fit_bundle = fit_spatiotemporal(
            df,
            feature_cols=self.feature_cols,
            target_col=self.target_col,
            timetype=self.timetype,
            freq=self.freq,
            seasonality_periods=self.seasonality_periods,
            num_seasonal_harmonics=self.num_seasonal_harmonics,
            fourier_degrees=self.fourier_degrees,
            interactions=self.interactions,
            standardize=self.standardize_columns,
        )
        # 2. Build the BNF layer template + design matrix.
        bnf = _build_bnf(
            fit_bundle, self.width, self.depth, self.encoder, self.encoder_cols
        )
        x_train = _df_to_design(df, fit_bundle, timetype=self.timetype, freq=self.freq)
        y_train = jnp.asarray(df[self.target_col].to_numpy(), dtype=jnp.float32)
        sigma_i = None
        if self.sigma_col is not None:
            sigma_i = _sigma_column(df, self.sigma_col)
        # 3. Run ensemble inference: a NeuralFieldEstimator on the BNF.
        fitted = NeuralFieldEstimator(
            model_fn=lambda: bnf,
            noise=self.noise,
            sigma_obs=self.sigma_obs,
            ensemble_size=self.ensemble_size,
            inference=self.inference_kind,
            num_epochs=self.num_epochs,
            learning_rate=self.learning_rate,
            prior_weight=self.prior_weight,
            guide_factory=self.guide_factory,
        ).fit(x_train, y_train, sigma=sigma_i, seed=seed)
        return FittedBNF(
            config=self,
            fit_bundle=fit_bundle,
            params=fitted.params,
            losses=fitted.losses,
            bnf_template=bnf,
        )

class FittedBNF(FittedEstimator):
    """Output of `BNFEstimator.fit`.

    Attributes:
        config: The `BNFEstimator` that produced this fit.
        fit_bundle: Pandas-side preprocessing record.
        params: Stacked per-ensemble-member parameter dict (each leaf
            has a leading ``(E,)`` axis for MAP, or an
            ``AutoNormal``-shaped variational-parameter dict for VI).
        losses: Per-member loss history, shape ``(E, num_epochs)``.
        bnf_template: The `BayesianNeuralField` layer instance
            used for inference (identical across members).
    """

    fit_bundle: SpatiotemporalFit
    params: Any
    losses: Float[Array, "E T"]
    bnf_template: BayesianNeuralField

    def predict(
        self,
        df: pd.DataFrame,
        *,
        quantiles: Sequence[float] | None = None,
        predict_seed: int = 0,
        num_posterior_samples: int = 32,
    ) -> Float[Array, " N"] | tuple[Float[Array, " N"], tuple[Float[Array, " N"], ...]]:
        r"""Posterior-predictive mean (and optional quantiles).

        For MAP fits the per-member predictions are point estimates;
        for VI fits we draw ``num_posterior_samples`` weight samples
        per member from the variational guide.

        The quantiles are those of the latent field plus the noise scale
        $\sigma_0$ (the fixed ``sigma_obs``, or each member's or draw's
        learned value): an equal-weight mixture of
        $\mathcal N(f_m(x), \sigma_{0,m}^2)$. Per-row $\sigma_i$ from
        ``sigma_col`` are not known at new points, so they are not added;
        add $\sigma_i^2$ yourself where you know it.

        Args:
            df: Inputs.
            quantiles: Optional levels. Returns ``(mean, (q_1, ..., q_K))``.
            predict_seed: PRNG seed for VI posterior sampling and
                quantile MC.
            num_posterior_samples: Per-member posterior draws used for
                VI predictive moments and quantile MC.
        """
        cfg = self.config
        assert isinstance(cfg, BNFEstimator)
        x_pred = _df_to_design(
            df, self.fit_bundle, timetype=cfg.timetype, freq=cfg.freq
        )
        return _predict(
            self.params,
            self.bnf_template,
            x_pred,
            encoder=None,
            noise=cfg.noise,
            sigma_obs=cfg.sigma_obs,
            has_sigma=cfg.sigma_col is not None,
            inference=cfg.inference_kind,
            guide_factory=cfg.guide_factory,
            quantiles=quantiles,
            predict_seed=predict_seed,
            num_posterior_samples=num_posterior_samples,
            # The BNF estimator keeps its published 200-draw floor, so its
            # quantiles are unchanged; NeuralFieldEstimator uses 2000.
            min_quantile_samples=200,
        )

docs.title: Neural fields on arrays and xarray
docs.text:
NeuralFieldEstimator fits any Bayesian neural field, a callable that maps (encoded) coordinates to a field while registering its weights as NumPyro sites (BayesianSIREN, SphericalHarmonicFeatures, BayesianNeuralField, …), with pyrox.inference.ensemble_map or ensemble_vi. It takes plain arrays with optional per-row noise and a validity mask, so padded batches fit exactly like their valid rows, or an xarray Dataset (fit_xarray, pip install pyrox-nn[xarray]) whose missing cells are masked; datetimes become days since the first timestamp (or time_origin=), and FittedNeuralField.predict_xarray maps a Dataset's grid the same way. Under MAP, pyrox_param sites and constrained latents (e.g. a LogNormal prior) are optimised in unconstrained space against the constrained-space density (no Jacobian), and fields that draw numpyro.prng_key() are rejected (use inference="vi"). The BNF estimators above are this estimator on a BayesianNeuralField.

import geonnax
from pyrox_nn import BayesianSIREN
from pyrox_nn.api import NeuralFieldEstimator

est = NeuralFieldEstimator(
    model_fn=lambda: BayesianSIREN.init(441, 128, 1, depth=4, first_omega=1.0),
    encoder=geonnax.SphericalHarmonicEncoder(l_max=20, input_mode="lonlat"),
    noise="learned", ensemble_size=8, num_epochs=2000,
)
fitted = est.fit(X, y, sigma=sig, valid=mask, seed=0)  # X (N, 2) lon/lat in radians
mean, (q05, q95) = fitted.predict(X_new, quantiles=(0.05, 0.95))

docs.text:
Bases: Module

Fit any Bayesian neural field with ensemble MAP or VI.

The field is built by model_fn(): a callable mapping a batch of (encoded) coordinates (N, D_enc) to the field (N,) or (N, 1) while registering its weights as NumPyro sample sites, usually a PyroxModule such as pyrox_nn.BayesianSIREN, pyrox_nn.SphericalHarmonicFeatures or pyrox_nn.BayesianNeuralField. Each ensemble member maximises (MAP) or approximates (VI) the posterior of

\[ y_i \sim \mathcal N\bigl(f_\theta(\gamma(x_i)),\ \sigma_i^2 + \sigma_0^2\bigr), \]

where \(\gamma\) is encoder (identity when None), \(\sigma_i\) the optional per-row noise passed to fit and \(\sigma_0\) set by noise. Rows with valid[i] = False contribute nothing to the log joint or its gradient, so padded batches fit exactly like their valid rows alone.

Sites: the field's own, plus log_sigma_obs with noise="learned"; the likelihood site y and the deterministic sites f (and log_sigma_f with noise="heteroscedastic").

Attributes:

Name Type Description model_fn Callable[[], Callable[[Array], Any]]

Zero-argument factory returning the field. Called once per fit; the returned module's sites must not depend on the data.

encoder Callable[[Array], Array] | None

Optional deterministic single-row encoder \(\gamma: (D,) \to (D_\mathrm{enc},)\) applied to every row before the field (vmapped), e.g. geonnax.SphericalHarmonicEncoder(l_max=20, input_mode="lonlat") (lon/lat in radians).

noise NoiseModel

"fixed" keeps \(\sigma_0\) at sigma_obs; "learned" infers it through the site log_sigma_obs \(= \log\sigma_0 \sim \mathcal N(\log\sigma_\mathrm{obs}, 1)\); "heteroscedastic" uses the field's own input-dependent scale: the field must return (mu, log_sigma), e.g. a trunk followed by pyrox_nn.GaussianRegressionHead, and \(\sigma_0 = \sigma(x_i)\). MAP members start from prior draws, and the head clips \(\log\sigma\) to \([-7, 3]\) with zero gradient outside, so keep its log_scale_prior_std small (the default 0.1): with 1.0 and a SIREN trunk, members start past the clip and never leave it. With prior_weight=0 (MLE), "learned" and no sigma, nothing bounds \(\sigma_0\) below, so fit raises.

sigma_obs float

\(\sigma_0\) for noise="fixed", or the prior median of \(\sigma_0\) for noise="learned"; unused when heteroscedastic.

ensemble_size int

Number of ensemble members \(E\).

inference InferenceKind

"map" (pyrox.inference.ensemble_map) or "vi" (pyrox.inference.ensemble_vi with guide_factory).

num_epochs int

Optimiser steps per member (full batch).

learning_rate float

Adam learning rate.

prior_weight float

1 ⇒ MAP, 0 ⇒ MLE, fractional ⇒ tempered (MAP only).

guide_factory Callable[[Callable], Any] | None

VI guide constructor taking the model function; None ⇒ AutoNormal.

Examples:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import geonnax
>>> from pyrox_nn import BayesianSIREN
>>> from pyrox_nn.api import NeuralFieldEstimator
>>> enc = geonnax.SphericalHarmonicEncoder(l_max=3, input_mode="lonlat")
>>> est = NeuralFieldEstimator(
...     model_fn=lambda: BayesianSIREN.init(16, 32, 1, depth=3),
...     encoder=enc, ensemble_size=2, num_epochs=10,
... )
>>> lonlat = jnp.stack([jnp.linspace(-3, 3, 20), jnp.zeros(20)], -1)
>>> fitted = est.fit(lonlat, jnp.sin(lonlat[:, 0]), seed=0)
>>> mean, (lo, hi) = fitted.predict(lonlat, quantiles=(0.05, 0.95))
>>> mean.shape, lo.shape
((20,), (20,))

class NeuralFieldEstimator(eqx.Module):
    r"""Fit any Bayesian neural field with ensemble MAP or VI.

    The field is built by ``model_fn()``: a callable mapping a batch of
    (encoded) coordinates ``(N, D_enc)`` to the field ``(N,)`` or
    ``(N, 1)`` while registering its weights as NumPyro sample sites,
    usually a `PyroxModule` such as `pyrox_nn.BayesianSIREN`,
    `pyrox_nn.SphericalHarmonicFeatures` or
    `pyrox_nn.BayesianNeuralField`. Each ensemble member maximises (MAP) or
    approximates (VI) the posterior of

    $$
    y_i \sim \mathcal N\bigl(f_\theta(\gamma(x_i)),\
        \sigma_i^2 + \sigma_0^2\bigr),
    $$

    where $\gamma$ is ``encoder`` (identity when ``None``), $\sigma_i$ the
    optional per-row noise passed to ``fit`` and $\sigma_0$ set by
    ``noise``. Rows with ``valid[i] = False`` contribute nothing to the log
    joint or its gradient, so padded batches fit exactly like their valid
    rows alone.

    Sites: the field's own, plus ``log_sigma_obs`` with
    ``noise="learned"``; the likelihood site ``y`` and the deterministic
    sites ``f`` (and ``log_sigma_f`` with ``noise="heteroscedastic"``).

    Attributes:
        model_fn: Zero-argument factory returning the field. Called once per
            ``fit``; the returned module's sites must not depend on the data.
        encoder: Optional deterministic single-row encoder
            $\gamma: (D,) \to (D_\mathrm{enc},)$ applied to every row before
            the field (vmapped), e.g.
            ``geonnax.SphericalHarmonicEncoder(l_max=20, input_mode="lonlat")``
            (lon/lat in radians).
        noise: ``"fixed"`` keeps $\sigma_0$ at ``sigma_obs``; ``"learned"``
            infers it through the site ``log_sigma_obs`` $= \log\sigma_0 \sim
            \mathcal N(\log\sigma_\mathrm{obs}, 1)$; ``"heteroscedastic"``
            uses the field's own input-dependent scale: the field must
            return ``(mu, log_sigma)``, e.g. a trunk followed by
            `pyrox_nn.GaussianRegressionHead`, and $\sigma_0 = \sigma(x_i)$.
            MAP members start from prior draws, and the head clips
            $\log\sigma$ to $[-7, 3]$ with zero gradient outside, so keep its
            ``log_scale_prior_std`` small (the default 0.1): with 1.0 and a
            SIREN trunk, members start past the clip and never leave it.
            With ``prior_weight=0`` (MLE), ``"learned"`` and no ``sigma``,
            nothing bounds $\sigma_0$ below, so ``fit`` raises.
        sigma_obs: $\sigma_0$ for ``noise="fixed"``, or the prior median of
            $\sigma_0$ for ``noise="learned"``; unused when heteroscedastic.
        ensemble_size: Number of ensemble members $E$.
        inference: ``"map"`` (``pyrox.inference.ensemble_map``) or ``"vi"``
            (``pyrox.inference.ensemble_vi`` with ``guide_factory``).
        num_epochs: Optimiser steps per member (full batch).
        learning_rate: Adam learning rate.
        prior_weight: ``1`` ⇒ MAP, ``0`` ⇒ MLE, fractional ⇒ tempered
            (MAP only).
        guide_factory: VI guide constructor taking the model function;
            ``None`` ⇒ ``AutoNormal``.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import geonnax
        >>> from pyrox_nn import BayesianSIREN
        >>> from pyrox_nn.api import NeuralFieldEstimator
        >>> enc = geonnax.SphericalHarmonicEncoder(l_max=3, input_mode="lonlat")
        >>> est = NeuralFieldEstimator(
        ...     model_fn=lambda: BayesianSIREN.init(16, 32, 1, depth=3),
        ...     encoder=enc, ensemble_size=2, num_epochs=10,
        ... )
        >>> lonlat = jnp.stack([jnp.linspace(-3, 3, 20), jnp.zeros(20)], -1)
        >>> fitted = est.fit(lonlat, jnp.sin(lonlat[:, 0]), seed=0)
        >>> mean, (lo, hi) = fitted.predict(lonlat, quantiles=(0.05, 0.95))
        >>> mean.shape, lo.shape
        ((20,), (20,))
    """

    model_fn: Callable[[], Callable[[Array], Any]] = eqx.field(static=True)
    encoder: Callable[[Array], Array] | None = None
    noise: NoiseModel = eqx.field(static=True, default="fixed")
    sigma_obs: float = eqx.field(static=True, default=0.1)
    ensemble_size: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=16)
    inference: InferenceKind = eqx.field(static=True, default="map")
    num_epochs: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=2000)
    learning_rate: float = eqx.field(static=True, default=5e-3)
    prior_weight: float = eqx.field(static=True, default=1.0)
    guide_factory: Callable[[Callable], Any] | None = eqx.field(
        static=True, default=None
    )

    def fit(
        self,
        X: Float[ArrayLike, "N D"],
        y: Float[ArrayLike, " N"],
        *,
        sigma: Float[ArrayLike, " N"] | None = None,
        valid: ArrayLike | None = None,
        seed: PRNGKeyArray | int,
    ) -> FittedNeuralField:
        r"""Fit the ensemble on arrays.

        Args:
            X: Coordinates of shape ``(N, D)`` (the encoder's input units).
            y: Targets of shape ``(N,)``.
            sigma: Optional per-row noise stds $\sigma_i$ of shape ``(N,)``,
                finite and > 0 on valid rows, in target units.
            valid: Optional boolean mask of shape ``(N,)``; rows with
                ``False`` (padding) are ignored, whatever their values.
            seed: PRNG key or integer seed.

        Returns:
            The fitted ensemble.

        Raises:
            ValueError: On a bad configuration, mismatched shapes, a mask
                with no valid row, or non-finite values (or $\sigma_i \le 0$)
                on a valid row.
        """
        _check_config(
            noise=self.noise,
            sigma_obs=self.sigma_obs,
            inference=self.inference,
            prior_weight=self.prior_weight,
            has_sigma=sigma is not None,
        )
        x_train, y_train = _pack_data(X, y, sigma, valid)
        if isinstance(seed, int):
            seed = jr.PRNGKey(seed)
        field = self.model_fn()
        model_fn = _field_model(
            _make_forward(field, self.encoder),
            self.sigma_obs,
            noise=self.noise,
            has_sigma=sigma is not None,
            has_valid=valid is not None,
        )
        params, losses = _fit_ensemble(
            model_fn,
            x_train,
            y_train,
            inference=self.inference,
            ensemble_size=self.ensemble_size,
            num_epochs=self.num_epochs,
            learning_rate=self.learning_rate,
            prior_weight=self.prior_weight,
            guide_factory=self.guide_factory,
            seed=seed,
        )
        return FittedNeuralField(
            config=self,
            field=field,
            params=params,
            losses=losses,
            has_sigma=sigma is not None,
        )

    def fit_xarray(
        self,
        ds: Any,
        *,
        coords: Sequence[str],
        target: str,
        sigma: str | None = None,
        time_origin: Any = None,
        seed: PRNGKeyArray | int,
    ) -> FittedNeuralField:
        r"""Fit on an xarray Dataset (``pip install pyrox-nn[xarray]``).

        Every variable named in ``coords``, ``target`` and ``sigma`` (a
        dimension, coordinate or data variable) is broadcast against the
        others and flattened, in the target's dimension order, to one row
        per grid point; ``coords`` become the columns of ``X`` in the order
        given. Rows where any of them is missing (NaN, NaT) are masked out,
        so a gappy grid needs no reshaping.

        A datetime coordinate becomes float days since ``time_origin``
        (default: its earliest timestamp), so the column starts near 0
        instead of at ~2·10⁴ days since 1970, which float32 would resolve
        only to minutes and a SIREN would see as a huge frequency. A
        timedelta coordinate becomes float days. The origins are stored on
        the fit; `FittedNeuralField.predict_xarray` applies the same
        mapping, and ``predict`` on arrays expects the same units.

        Args:
            ds: An ``xarray.Dataset``.
            coords: Names of the input variables, e.g. ``("lon", "lat", "time")``.
            target: Name of the target variable.
            sigma: Optional name of the per-row noise std variable.
            time_origin: Optional reference time for every datetime
                coordinate (anything ``numpy.datetime64`` accepts).
            seed: PRNG key or integer seed.

        Returns:
            The fitted ensemble, which remembers ``coords`` and the time
            origins.

        Raises:
            ImportError: If xarray is not installed.
            ValueError: If a name is not a variable of ``ds``, or as `fit`.
        """
        xr = _require_xarray("fit_xarray")
        names = [*coords, target, *([sigma] if sigma is not None else [])]
        _check_names(ds, names)
        # Flatten in the target's dimension order (C order), whatever the
        # order of ``coords``.
        arrays = xr.broadcast(*(ds[name] for name in names))
        dims = (
            *ds[target].dims,
            *(d for d in arrays[0].dims if d not in ds[target].dims),
        )
        arrays = [a.transpose(*dims) for a in arrays]
        origins = tuple(_time_origin(ds[name].values, time_origin) for name in coords)
        cols = [
            _numeric_column(a.values.ravel(), origin)
            for a, origin in zip(
                arrays, (*origins, *([None] * (len(names) - len(coords)))), strict=True
            )
        ]
        X = np.stack(cols[: len(coords)], axis=-1)
        valid = np.isfinite(np.stack(cols, axis=-1)).all(axis=-1)
        fitted = self.fit(
            X,
            cols[len(coords)],
            sigma=None if sigma is None else cols[-1],
            valid=valid,
            seed=seed,
        )
        return FittedNeuralField(
            config=fitted.config,
            field=fitted.field,
            params=fitted.params,
            losses=fitted.losses,
            has_sigma=fitted.has_sigma,
            xarray_coords=tuple(coords),
            time_origins=origins,
        )

def fit(
    self,
    X: Float[ArrayLike, "N D"],
    y: Float[ArrayLike, " N"],
    *,
    sigma: Float[ArrayLike, " N"] | None = None,
    valid: ArrayLike | None = None,
    seed: PRNGKeyArray | int,
) -> FittedNeuralField:
    r"""Fit the ensemble on arrays.

    Args:
        X: Coordinates of shape ``(N, D)`` (the encoder's input units).
        y: Targets of shape ``(N,)``.
        sigma: Optional per-row noise stds $\sigma_i$ of shape ``(N,)``,
            finite and > 0 on valid rows, in target units.
        valid: Optional boolean mask of shape ``(N,)``; rows with
            ``False`` (padding) are ignored, whatever their values.
        seed: PRNG key or integer seed.

    Returns:
        The fitted ensemble.

    Raises:
        ValueError: On a bad configuration, mismatched shapes, a mask
            with no valid row, or non-finite values (or $\sigma_i \le 0$)
            on a valid row.
    """
    _check_config(
        noise=self.noise,
        sigma_obs=self.sigma_obs,
        inference=self.inference,
        prior_weight=self.prior_weight,
        has_sigma=sigma is not None,
    )
    x_train, y_train = _pack_data(X, y, sigma, valid)
    if isinstance(seed, int):
        seed = jr.PRNGKey(seed)
    field = self.model_fn()
    model_fn = _field_model(
        _make_forward(field, self.encoder),
        self.sigma_obs,
        noise=self.noise,
        has_sigma=sigma is not None,
        has_valid=valid is not None,
    )
    params, losses = _fit_ensemble(
        model_fn,
        x_train,
        y_train,
        inference=self.inference,
        ensemble_size=self.ensemble_size,
        num_epochs=self.num_epochs,
        learning_rate=self.learning_rate,
        prior_weight=self.prior_weight,
        guide_factory=self.guide_factory,
        seed=seed,
    )
    return FittedNeuralField(
        config=self,
        field=field,
        params=params,
        losses=losses,
        has_sigma=sigma is not None,
    )

Every variable named in coords, target and sigma (a dimension, coordinate or data variable) is broadcast against the others and flattened, in the target's dimension order, to one row per grid point; coords become the columns of X in the order given. A timedelta coordinate becomes float days. The origins are stored on the fit; FittedNeuralField.predict_xarray applies the same mapping, and predict on arrays expects the same units.

def fit_xarray(
    self,
    ds: Any,
    *,
    coords: Sequence[str],
    target: str,
    sigma: str | None = None,
    time_origin: Any = None,
    seed: PRNGKeyArray | int,
) -> FittedNeuralField:
    r"""Fit on an xarray Dataset (``pip install pyrox-nn[xarray]``).

    Every variable named in ``coords``, ``target`` and ``sigma`` (a
    dimension, coordinate or data variable) is broadcast against the
    others and flattened, in the target's dimension order, to one row
    per grid point; ``coords`` become the columns of ``X`` in the order
    given. Rows where any of them is missing (NaN, NaT) are masked out,
    so a gappy grid needs no reshaping.

    A datetime coordinate becomes float days since ``time_origin``
    (default: its earliest timestamp), so the column starts near 0
    instead of at ~2·10⁴ days since 1970, which float32 would resolve
    only to minutes and a SIREN would see as a huge frequency. A
    timedelta coordinate becomes float days. The origins are stored on
    the fit; `FittedNeuralField.predict_xarray` applies the same
    mapping, and ``predict`` on arrays expects the same units.

    Args:
        ds: An ``xarray.Dataset``.
        coords: Names of the input variables, e.g. ``("lon", "lat", "time")``.
        target: Name of the target variable.
        sigma: Optional name of the per-row noise std variable.
        time_origin: Optional reference time for every datetime
            coordinate (anything ``numpy.datetime64`` accepts).
        seed: PRNG key or integer seed.

    Returns:
        The fitted ensemble, which remembers ``coords`` and the time
        origins.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If xarray is not installed.
        ValueError: If a name is not a variable of ``ds``, or as `fit`.
    """
    xr = _require_xarray("fit_xarray")
    names = [*coords, target, *([sigma] if sigma is not None else [])]
    _check_names(ds, names)
    # Flatten in the target's dimension order (C order), whatever the
    # order of ``coords``.
    arrays = xr.broadcast(*(ds[name] for name in names))
    dims = (
        *ds[target].dims,
        *(d for d in arrays[0].dims if d not in ds[target].dims),
    )
    arrays = [a.transpose(*dims) for a in arrays]
    origins = tuple(_time_origin(ds[name].values, time_origin) for name in coords)
    cols = [
        _numeric_column(a.values.ravel(), origin)
        for a, origin in zip(
            arrays, (*origins, *([None] * (len(names) - len(coords)))), strict=True
        )
    ]
    X = np.stack(cols[: len(coords)], axis=-1)
    valid = np.isfinite(np.stack(cols, axis=-1)).all(axis=-1)
    fitted = self.fit(
        X,
        cols[len(coords)],
        sigma=None if sigma is None else cols[-1],
        valid=valid,
        seed=seed,
    )
    return FittedNeuralField(
        config=fitted.config,
        field=fitted.field,
        params=fitted.params,
        losses=fitted.losses,
        has_sigma=fitted.has_sigma,
        xarray_coords=tuple(coords),
        time_origins=origins,
    )

class FittedNeuralField(eqx.Module):
    """Output of `NeuralFieldEstimator.fit`.

    Attributes:
        config: The `NeuralFieldEstimator` that produced this fit.
        field: The field returned by ``model_fn()`` (identical across
            members; the weights live in ``params``).
        params: Stacked per-member parameters: a dict of the field's sites
            with a leading ``(E,)`` axis for MAP, or the guide's
            variational parameters for VI.
        losses: Per-member loss history, shape ``(E, num_epochs)``.
        has_sigma: Whether per-row $\\sigma_i$ were given at fit time.
        xarray_coords: The ``coords`` of ``fit_xarray`` (``None`` after
            ``fit``).
        time_origins: Per coordinate, the reference time of a datetime
            coordinate as an ISO string (``None`` for the others), from
            ``fit_xarray``.
    """

    config: NeuralFieldEstimator
    field: Any
    params: Any
    losses: Float[Array, "E T"]
    has_sigma: bool = eqx.field(static=True, default=False)
    xarray_coords: tuple[str, ...] | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)
    time_origins: tuple[str | None, ...] | None = eqx.field(static=True, default=None)

    def predict(
        self,
        X: Float[ArrayLike, "N D"],
        *,
        quantiles: Sequence[float] | None = None,
        predict_seed: int = 0,
        num_posterior_samples: int = 32,
    ) -> Prediction:
        r"""Posterior-predictive mean (and optional quantiles).

        MAP members give one prediction each; VI members give
        ``num_posterior_samples`` guide draws each. The quantiles are those
        of the equal-weight mixture of $\mathcal N(f_m(x), \sigma_{0,m}^2)$
        over members (or draws), estimated by Monte Carlo, with
        $\sigma_{0,m}$ the fixed ``sigma_obs``, the member's learned value,
        or its $\sigma_m(x)$ when heteroscedastic. Per-row $\sigma_i$ are not
        known at new points, so they are not added.

        Args:
            X: Coordinates of shape ``(N, D)``, in the units used to fit.
            quantiles: Optional levels; then returns
                ``(mean, (q_1, ..., q_K))``.
            predict_seed: PRNG seed for VI posterior draws and quantile MC.
            num_posterior_samples: Per-member draws for VI predictions and
                quantile MC.

        Returns:
            The mean of shape ``(N,)``, or ``(mean, quantiles)``.
        """
        cfg = self.config
        return _predict(
            self.params,
            self.field,
            _floating(X),
            encoder=cfg.encoder,
            noise=cfg.noise,
            sigma_obs=cfg.sigma_obs,
            has_sigma=self.has_sigma,
            inference=cfg.inference,
            guide_factory=cfg.guide_factory,
            quantiles=quantiles,
            predict_seed=predict_seed,
            num_posterior_samples=num_posterior_samples,
        )

    def predict_xarray(
        self,
        ds: Any,
        *,
        quantiles: Sequence[float] | None = None,
        predict_seed: int = 0,
        num_posterior_samples: int = 32,
    ) -> Any:
        """Predict on the grid of an xarray Dataset, as fitted by ``fit_xarray``.

        The fitted ``coords`` are read from ``ds``, broadcast against each
        other and mapped to the fit's units (datetimes as days since the
        stored origins); the result has their broadcast shape and
        coordinates. A grid point with a missing coordinate predicts NaN.

        Args:
            ds: An ``xarray.Dataset`` holding the fitted ``coords``.
            quantiles: Optional levels, as in `predict`.
            predict_seed: As in `predict`.
            num_posterior_samples: As in `predict`.

        Returns:
            The mean as an ``xarray.DataArray``, or ``(mean, quantiles)``
            with one ``DataArray`` per level.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If this fit did not come from ``fit_xarray``, or a
                coordinate is not a variable of ``ds``.
        """
        if self.xarray_coords is None or self.time_origins is None:
            raise ValueError("predict_xarray needs a fit from fit_xarray.")
        xr = _require_xarray("predict_xarray")
        _check_names(ds, self.xarray_coords)
        arrays = xr.broadcast(*(ds[name] for name in self.xarray_coords))
        template = arrays[0]
        cols = [
            _numeric_column(a.transpose(*template.dims).values.ravel(), origin)
            for a, origin in zip(arrays, self.time_origins, strict=True)
        ]
        X = np.stack(cols, axis=-1)
        rows = np.asarray(np.isfinite(X).all(axis=-1))
        out = self.predict(
            np.where(rows[:, None], X, 0.0),
            quantiles=quantiles,
            predict_seed=predict_seed,
            num_posterior_samples=num_posterior_samples,
        )

        def as_grid(values: Any) -> Any:
            grid = np.where(rows, np.asarray(values), np.nan).reshape(template.shape)
            return xr.DataArray(grid, coords=template.coords, dims=template.dims)

        if quantiles is None:
            return as_grid(out)
        mean, qs = out
        return as_grid(mean), tuple(as_grid(q) for q in qs)

Shared base for modules with priors, constraints, and mode switching.

Subclasses typically declare parameters inside setup, which is invoked automatically after __init__ completes. Use register_param to declare a parameter, set_prior to attach a prior, autoguide to pick a guide type, and set_mode to switch between sampling from the prior and sampling from the guide.

Per-instance state (params, priors, guides, mode) lives in a class-level registry keyed by id(self). Cleanup happens via weakref.finalize when the instance is collected; call _teardown for explicit cleanup.
