        # float64 under x64 and would promote float32 kernels.
        identity_1 = jnp.eye(state_size_1, dtype=params_1.F.dtype)
        identity_2 = jnp.eye(state_size_2, dtype=params_2.F.dtype)

        # F_c = F_c^(1) ⊗ I + I ⊗ F_c^(2)
        drift = jnp.kron(params_1.F, identity_2) + jnp.kron(identity_1, params_2.F)
        # H = H^(1) ⊗ H^(2)
        obs_operator = jnp.kron(params_1.H, params_2.H)
        # Σ_x,∞ = Σ_x,∞^(1) ⊗ Σ_x,∞^(2)
        stationary_covariance = jnp.kron(params_1.P_inf, params_2.P_inf)

        # B_c = B_c^(1) ⊗ Σ_x,∞^(2) + Σ_x,∞^(1) ⊗ B_c^(2), kept in the
        # (L_c, Q_c) pair by putting each factor's Σ_x,∞ in the *spectral
        # density* rather than taking its square root:
        #
        #     B_c^(1) ⊗ Σ_x,∞^(2)
        #         = (L_c^(1) ⊗ I) (Q_c^(1) ⊗ Σ_x,∞^(2)) (L_c^(1) ⊗ I)ᵀ
        #     Σ_x,∞^(1) ⊗ B_c^(2)
        #         = (I ⊗ L_c^(2)) (Σ_x,∞^(1) ⊗ Q_c^(2)) (I ⊗ L_c^(2))ᵀ
        #
        # by the mixed-product property. Exact for any PSD Σ_x,∞, including
        # singular or zero ones, where a Cholesky would need jitter and stop
        # satisfying the Lyapunov equation this is here to enforce. The
        # noise dimension widens from D_b^(1) D_b^(2) to
        # D_b^(1) D_x^(2) + D_x^(1) D_b^(2).
        # L_c = [L_c^(1) ⊗ I, I ⊗ L_c^(2)]
        noise_effect = jnp.concatenate(
            [jnp.kron(params_1.L, identity_2), jnp.kron(identity_1, params_2.L)],
            axis=1,
        )
        # Q_c = blockdiag(Q_c^(1) ⊗ Σ_x,∞^(2), Σ_x,∞^(1) ⊗ Q_c^(2))
        spectral_density = jsl.block_diag(
            jnp.kron(params_1.Q_c, params_2.P_inf),
            jnp.kron(params_1.P_inf, params_2.Q_c),
        )

        return SDEParams(
            F=drift,
            L=noise_effect,
            H=obs_operator,
            Q_c=spectral_density,
            P_inf=stationary_covariance,
        )

    def discretise(
        self,
        dt: Float[Array, ""],
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "d d"], Float[Array, "d d"]]:
        """Discretise per factor, through the Kronecker exponential identity.

            F_t = exp(F_c Δt) = exp(F_c^(1) Δt) ⊗ exp(F_c^(2) Δt)
                = F_t^(1) ⊗ F_t^(2)
            Σ_η,t = Σ_x,∞ − (F_t^(1) Σ_x,∞^(1) F_t^(1)ᵀ)
                            ⊗ (F_t^(2) Σ_x,∞^(2) F_t^(2)ᵀ)

        The two terms of the Kronecker sum F_c^(1) ⊗ I and I ⊗ F_c^(2)
        commute, so the exponential factorises: two exponentials of size
        D_x^(1) and D_x^(2) plus one Kronecker product, instead of one of
        size D_x^(1) D_x^(2). By the mixed-product property the congruence
        F_t Σ_x,∞ F_tᵀ factorises too, so `gaussx.process_noise_covariance`
        evaluates it per factor on `gaussx.Kronecker` operands, in
        O((D_x^(1))³ + (D_x^(2))³) instead of O((D_x^(1) D_x^(2))³). Only
        the final Σ_η,t is materialised, to keep the consumer-facing
        ``(A, Q)`` interface unchanged.

        Algorithm:
            1. Exponentiate each factor's drift, F_t^(i) = exp(F_c^(i) Δt).
            2. Form F_t = F_t^(1) ⊗ F_t^(2).
            3. Take Σ_η,t = Σ_x,∞ − F_t Σ_x,∞ F_tᵀ on Kronecker operands,
               then materialise and symmetrise it.

        Args:
            dt: Time step Δt > 0.

        Returns:
            Tuple ``(A, Q)`` holding the transition F_t and the
            model-noise covariance Σ_η,t, as in `SDEKernel.discretise`.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: If either factor lacks a stationary
                covariance.
        """
        params_1 = self.kernel1.sde_params()
        params_2 = self.kernel2.sde_params()
        # F_t^(1) = exp(F_c^(1) Δt)
        transition_1 = jsl.expm(params_1.F * dt)
        # F_t^(2) = exp(F_c^(2) Δt)
        transition_2 = jsl.expm(params_2.F * dt)
        # F_t = F_t^(1) ⊗ F_t^(2)
        transition = jnp.kron(transition_1, transition_2)

        # Use the per-factor stationary covariances directly; building
        # the full F_c via ``self.sde_params()`` would defeat the
        # whole point of this override. Keeping both operands as
        # ``Kronecker`` lets the shared helper contract each factor
        # separately instead of forming the full-size triple product.
        if params_1.P_inf is None or params_2.P_inf is None:
            # Deferring to the base MFD path here would be *wrong*, not
            # merely slower: the composite diffusion covariance
            #
            #     B_c = B_c^(1) ⊗ Σ_x,∞^(2) + Σ_x,∞^(1) ⊗ B_c^(2)
            #
            # needs both factor stationary covariances, exactly what is
            # missing, so MFD has nothing correct to consume. Checked
            # against the factors directly rather than via
            # ``self.sde_params()`` (which raises for the same reason)
            # so the message names the offending factor, and so the
            # happy path never builds the full-size drift it would
            # otherwise have to discard.
            msg = (
                f"ProductSDE cannot be discretised when a factor has no "
                f"stationary covariance: "
                f"{type(self.kernel1).__name__}.P_inf is "
                f"{'None' if params_1.P_inf is None else 'set'} and "
                f"{type(self.kernel2).__name__}.P_inf is "
                f"{'None' if params_2.P_inf is None else 'set'}. The composite "
                f"diffusion of a product kernel is B1 (x) P2 + P1 (x) B2, "
                f"which needs both. Discretise the factors separately, or "
                f"give the factor a P_inf."
            )
            raise NotImplementedError(msg)

        transition_op = Kronecker(
            lx.MatrixLinearOperator(transition_1),
            lx.MatrixLinearOperator(transition_2),
        )
        stationary_covariance_op = Kronecker(
            lx.MatrixLinearOperator(params_1.P_inf, lx.symmetric_tag),
            lx.MatrixLinearOperator(params_2.P_inf, lx.symmetric_tag),
        )
        # Σ_η,t = Σ_x,∞ − F_t Σ_x,∞ F_tᵀ, factor by factor
        model_noise_op = process_noise_covariance(
            transition_op, stationary_covariance_op
        )
        model_noise_covariance = symmetrize(model_noise_op.as_matrix())
        return transition, model_noise_covariance

    The two terms of the Kronecker sum F_c^(1) ⊗ I and I ⊗ F_c^(2)
    commute, so the exponential factorises: two exponentials of size
    D_x^(1) and D_x^(2) plus one Kronecker product, instead of one of
    size D_x^(1) D_x^(2). By the mixed-product property the congruence
    F_t Σ_x,∞ F_tᵀ factorises too, so `gaussx.process_noise_covariance`
    evaluates it per factor on `gaussx.Kronecker` operands, in
    O((D_x^(1))³ + (D_x^(2))³) instead of O((D_x^(1) D_x^(2))³). Only
    the final Σ_η,t is materialised, to keep the consumer-facing
    ``(A, Q)`` interface unchanged.

    Algorithm:
        1. Exponentiate each factor's drift, F_t^(i) = exp(F_c^(i) Δt).
        2. Form F_t = F_t^(1) ⊗ F_t^(2).
        3. Take Σ_η,t = Σ_x,∞ − F_t Σ_x,∞ F_tᵀ on Kronecker operands,
           then materialise and symmetrise it.

    Args:
        dt: Time step Δt > 0.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(A, Q)`` holding the transition F_t and the
        model-noise covariance Σ_η,t, as in `SDEKernel.discretise`.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If either factor lacks a stationary
            covariance.
    """
    params_1 = self.kernel1.sde_params()
    params_2 = self.kernel2.sde_params()
    # F_t^(1) = exp(F_c^(1) Δt)
    transition_1 = jsl.expm(params_1.F * dt)
    # F_t^(2) = exp(F_c^(2) Δt)
    transition_2 = jsl.expm(params_2.F * dt)
    # F_t = F_t^(1) ⊗ F_t^(2)
    transition = jnp.kron(transition_1, transition_2)

    # Use the per-factor stationary covariances directly; building
    # the full F_c via ``self.sde_params()`` would defeat the
    # whole point of this override. Keeping both operands as
    # ``Kronecker`` lets the shared helper contract each factor
    # separately instead of forming the full-size triple product.
    if params_1.P_inf is None or params_2.P_inf is None:
        # Deferring to the base MFD path here would be *wrong*, not
        # merely slower: the composite diffusion covariance
        #
        #     B_c = B_c^(1) ⊗ Σ_x,∞^(2) + Σ_x,∞^(1) ⊗ B_c^(2)
        #
        # needs both factor stationary covariances, exactly what is
        # missing, so MFD has nothing correct to consume. Checked
        # against the factors directly rather than via
        # ``self.sde_params()`` (which raises for the same reason)
        # so the message names the offending factor, and so the
        # happy path never builds the full-size drift it would
        # otherwise have to discard.
        msg = (
            f"ProductSDE cannot be discretised when a factor has no "
            f"stationary covariance: "
            f"{type(self.kernel1).__name__}.P_inf is "
            f"{'None' if params_1.P_inf is None else 'set'} and "
            f"{type(self.kernel2).__name__}.P_inf is "
            f"{'None' if params_2.P_inf is None else 'set'}. The composite "
            f"diffusion of a product kernel is B1 (x) P2 + P1 (x) B2, "
            f"which needs both. Discretise the factors separately, or "
            f"give the factor a P_inf."
        )
        raise NotImplementedError(msg)

    transition_op = Kronecker(
        lx.MatrixLinearOperator(transition_1),
        lx.MatrixLinearOperator(transition_2),
    )
    stationary_covariance_op = Kronecker(
        lx.MatrixLinearOperator(params_1.P_inf, lx.symmetric_tag),
        lx.MatrixLinearOperator(params_2.P_inf, lx.symmetric_tag),
    )
    # Σ_η,t = Σ_x,∞ − F_t Σ_x,∞ F_tᵀ, factor by factor
    model_noise_op = process_noise_covariance(
        transition_op, stationary_covariance_op
    )
    model_noise_covariance = symmetrize(model_noise_op.as_matrix())
    return transition, model_noise_covariance

docs.title: Linear-Gaussian state-space models
docs.text:
LinearGaussianSSMPrior is the general Gaussian state-space model, given directly by its transitions A_k, observation matrices H_k, process and observation noise covariances Q_k and R_k, an initial state N(m_0, P_0) and an optional known observation offset b_k, so that x_k = A_k x_{k-1} + eta_k and y_k = H_k x_k + b_k + eps_k for k = 1, …, T. Use it when the dynamics are known as matrices rather than as a GP kernel: a local-level model, a multi-output state, a discretised physical model whose matrices carry priors. It follows the gaussx.kalman_filter convention of predicting before every update, so y[0] is scored against A_1 x_0; set transition[0] = I and process_noise[0] = 0 to observe the initial state itself.

Observations are (T, M) (a flat (T,) series is accepted when M = 1), and every method takes a mask= either per step, (T,), or per entry, (T, M); a masked entry is marginalised out exactly and may hold NaN. log_marginal, smooth and condition give the prediction-error log marginal and the RTS-smoothed state moments, and lgssm_factor adds the log marginal to a NumPyro model:

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro
import numpyro.distributions as dist
import pyrox_ssm as pss

def local_level(y, mask):
    T = y.shape[0]
    q = numpyro.sample("q", dist.LogNormal(-2.0, 1.0))
    r = numpyro.sample("r", dist.LogNormal(-1.0, 1.0))
    prior = pss.LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
        transition=jnp.ones((T, 1, 1)), obs_model=jnp.eye(1),
        process_noise=q * jnp.ones((T, 1, 1)), obs_noise=r * jnp.eye(1),
        init_mean=jnp.zeros(1), init_cov=10.0 * jnp.eye(1),
    )
    pss.lgssm_factor("y", prior, y, mask=mask)

MarkovGPPrior is its kernel-built special case: as_lgssm(noise_var) returns the kernel's discretised transitions over the time grid (with a leading zero step, so A_1 = I and Q_1 = 0), H, R_k = noise_var + obs_noise_floor, m_0 = 0, P_0 = initial_covariance() and the offset b_k = mean_fn(t_k). MarkovGPPrior's filtering and smoothing run through this model, so the two agree bit for bit.

docs.title: LinearGaussianSSMPrior
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Prior over a linear-Gaussian state-space model given by its matrices.

With \(T\) observation steps, a state of length \(D\) and observations of length \(M\), the model is

\[ x_0 \sim \mathcal{N}(m_0, P_0), \qquad x_k = A_k x_{k-1} + \eta_k, \quad \eta_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, Q_k), \qquad y_k = H_k x_k + b_k + \varepsilon_k, \quad \varepsilon_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R_k), \]

for \(k = 1, \dots, T\), and row \(k - 1\) of every time-stacked field holds step \(k\). This is the convention of gaussx.kalman_filter, which predicts before every update: the first observation y[0] is \(y_1\), scored against \(A_1 x_0\), not against \(x_0\). To observe the initial state itself, set transition[0] = I and process_noise[0] = 0, which is what pyrox_ssm.MarkovGPPrior.as_lgssm does (its first step has \(\Delta t = 0\)).

The marginal likelihood is the prediction-error decomposition

\[ \log p(y \mid \theta) = \sum_{k=1}^{T} \log \mathcal{N}\!\left(y_k;\, H_k m_k^- + b_k,\, H_k P_k^- H_k^\top + R_k\right), \]

with \(m_k^-, P_k^-\) the predicted moments of \(x_k\) given \(y_{1:k-1}\), at \(O(T D^3)\) cost.

Every method that reads observations takes an optional mask, either per step, shaped (T,) (a masked step runs the predict only), or per entry, shaped (T, M) (the masked entries of \(y_k\) are marginalised out exactly, so the log marginal is that of the observed entries). Masked entries of y are replaced by zero before any arithmetic, so a NaN placeholder there reaches neither the value nor a gradient.

The prior registers no NumPyro sites itself; lgssm_factor adds its log marginal as a factor. Shapes are checked at construction (array shapes are static, so the check also runs on traced matrices), and integer arrays are promoted to float.

Attributes:

Name Type Description transition Float[Array, 'T D D']

Transitions \(A_k\), shaped (T, D, D).

obs_model Float[Array, 'T M D'] | Float[Array, 'M D']

Observation matrices \(H_k\), shaped (T, M, D), or one (M, D) matrix for every step.

process_noise Float[Array, 'T D D']

Process-noise covariances \(Q_k\), shaped (T, D, D).

obs_noise Float[Array, 'T M M'] | Float[Array, 'M M']

Observation-noise covariances \(R_k\), shaped (T, M, M), or one (M, M) matrix for every step.

init_mean Float[Array, ' D']

Mean \(m_0\) of the initial state, shaped (D,).

init_cov Float[Array, 'D D']

Covariance \(P_0\) of the initial state, shaped (D, D).

obs_offset Float[Array, 'T M'] | None

Optional known observation offset \(b_k\), shaped (T, M); None is \(b_k = 0\). It is subtracted from y before filtering, so a GP with a mean function becomes an exact special case (pyrox_ssm.MarkovGPPrior.as_lgssm sets it to the mean at the observation times).

Examples:

A local-level model, \(x_k = x_{k-1} + \eta_k\) observed with noise:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
>>> T, q, r = 5, 0.1, 0.5
>>> prior = pss.LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
...     transition=jnp.ones((T, 1, 1)),
...     obs_model=jnp.eye(1),
...     process_noise=jnp.full((T, 1, 1), q),
...     obs_noise=r * jnp.eye(1),
...     init_mean=jnp.zeros(1),
...     init_cov=10.0 * jnp.eye(1),
... )
>>> y = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.4], [jnp.nan], [0.3], [0.2]])
>>> mask = jnp.array([True, True, False, True, True])
>>> log_marg = prior.log_marginal(y, mask=mask)
>>> log_marg.shape
()
Source code in packages/pyrox-ssm/src/pyrox_ssm/_lgssm.py 
class LinearGaussianSSMPrior(eqx.Module):
    r"""Prior over a linear-Gaussian state-space model given by its matrices.

    With $T$ observation steps, a state of length $D$ and observations of
    length $M$, the model is

    $$
    x_0 \sim \mathcal{N}(m_0, P_0), \qquad
    x_k = A_k x_{k-1} + \eta_k, \quad \eta_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, Q_k), \qquad
    y_k = H_k x_k + b_k + \varepsilon_k, \quad
    \varepsilon_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R_k),
    $$

    for $k = 1, \dots, T$, and row $k - 1$ of every time-stacked field
    holds step $k$. This is the convention of `gaussx.kalman_filter`, which
    predicts before every update: the first observation ``y[0]`` is $y_1$,
    scored against $A_1 x_0$, not against $x_0$. To observe the initial
    state itself, set ``transition[0] = I`` and ``process_noise[0] = 0``,
    which is what `pyrox_ssm.MarkovGPPrior.as_lgssm` does (its first step
    has $\Delta t = 0$).

    The marginal likelihood is the prediction-error decomposition

    $$
    \log p(y \mid \theta) = \sum_{k=1}^{T}
      \log \mathcal{N}\!\left(y_k;\, H_k m_k^- + b_k,\,
      H_k P_k^- H_k^\top + R_k\right),
    $$

    with $m_k^-, P_k^-$ the predicted moments of $x_k$ given
    $y_{1:k-1}$, at $O(T D^3)$ cost.

    Every method that reads observations takes an optional ``mask``, either
    per step, shaped ``(T,)`` (a masked step runs the predict only), or per
    entry, shaped ``(T, M)`` (the masked entries of $y_k$ are marginalised
    out exactly, so the log marginal is that of the observed entries).
    Masked entries of ``y`` are replaced by zero before any arithmetic, so a
    ``NaN`` placeholder there reaches neither the value nor a gradient.

    The prior registers no NumPyro sites itself; `lgssm_factor` adds its log
    marginal as a factor. Shapes are checked at construction (array shapes
    are static, so the check also runs on traced matrices), and integer
    arrays are promoted to float.

    Attributes:
        transition: Transitions $A_k$, shaped ``(T, D, D)``.
        obs_model: Observation matrices $H_k$, shaped ``(T, M, D)``, or one
            ``(M, D)`` matrix for every step.
        process_noise: Process-noise covariances $Q_k$, shaped
            ``(T, D, D)``.
        obs_noise: Observation-noise covariances $R_k$, shaped
            ``(T, M, M)``, or one ``(M, M)`` matrix for every step.
        init_mean: Mean $m_0$ of the initial state, shaped ``(D,)``.
        init_cov: Covariance $P_0$ of the initial state, shaped ``(D, D)``.
        obs_offset: Optional known observation offset $b_k$, shaped
            ``(T, M)``; ``None`` is $b_k = 0$. It is subtracted from ``y``
            before filtering, so a GP with a mean function becomes an exact
            special case (`pyrox_ssm.MarkovGPPrior.as_lgssm` sets it to the
            mean at the observation times).

    Examples:
        A local-level model, $x_k = x_{k-1} + \eta_k$ observed with noise:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> T, q, r = 5, 0.1, 0.5
        >>> prior = pss.LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
        ...     transition=jnp.ones((T, 1, 1)),
        ...     obs_model=jnp.eye(1),
        ...     process_noise=jnp.full((T, 1, 1), q),
        ...     obs_noise=r * jnp.eye(1),
        ...     init_mean=jnp.zeros(1),
        ...     init_cov=10.0 * jnp.eye(1),
        ... )
        >>> y = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.4], [jnp.nan], [0.3], [0.2]])
        >>> mask = jnp.array([True, True, False, True, True])
        >>> log_marg = prior.log_marginal(y, mask=mask)
        >>> log_marg.shape
        ()
    """

    transition: Float[Array, "T D D"]
    obs_model: Float[Array, "T M D"] | Float[Array, "M D"]
    process_noise: Float[Array, "T D D"]
    obs_noise: Float[Array, "T M M"] | Float[Array, "M M"]
    init_mean: Float[Array, " D"]
    init_cov: Float[Array, "D D"]
    obs_offset: Float[Array, "T M"] | None = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        transition: Float[Array, "T D D"],
        obs_model: Float[Array, "T M D"] | Float[Array, "M D"],
        process_noise: Float[Array, "T D D"],
        obs_noise: Float[Array, "T M M"] | Float[Array, "M M"],
        init_mean: Float[Array, " D"],
        init_cov: Float[Array, "D D"],
        obs_offset: Float[Array, "T M"] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        transition = _as_float(transition)
        obs_model = _as_float(obs_model)
        process_noise = _as_float(process_noise)
        obs_noise = _as_float(obs_noise)
        init_mean = _as_float(init_mean)
        init_cov = _as_float(init_cov)
        if transition.ndim != 3 or transition.shape[1] != transition.shape[2]:
            raise ValueError(
                "transition must be a (T, D, D) stack of square matrices, got "
                f"shape {tuple(transition.shape)!r}"
            )
        T, D = transition.shape[0], transition.shape[1]
        if obs_model.ndim not in (2, 3) or obs_model.shape[-1] != D:
            raise ValueError(
                f"obs_model must have shape (T, M, D) or (M, D) with D = {D}, "
                f"got {tuple(obs_model.shape)!r}"
            )
        M = obs_model.shape[-2]
        _check_shape("obs_model", obs_model, ((T, M, D), (M, D)))
        _check_shape("process_noise", process_noise, ((T, D, D),))
        _check_shape("obs_noise", obs_noise, ((T, M, M), (M, M)))
        _check_shape("init_mean", init_mean, ((D,),))
        _check_shape("init_cov", init_cov, ((D, D),))
        if obs_offset is not None:
            obs_offset = _as_float(obs_offset)
            _check_shape("obs_offset", obs_offset, ((T, M),))
        self.transition = transition
        self.obs_model = obs_model
        self.process_noise = process_noise
        self.obs_noise = obs_noise
        self.init_mean = init_mean
        self.init_cov = init_cov
        self.obs_offset = obs_offset

    @property
    def n_steps(self) -> int:
        """Number of observation steps $T$."""
        return self.transition.shape[0]

    @property
    def state_dim(self) -> int:
        """State dimension $D$."""
        return self.transition.shape[-1]

    @property
    def obs_dim(self) -> int:
        """Observation dimension $M$."""
        return self.obs_model.shape[-2]

    def _observations(
        self, y: Float[Array, "T M"] | Float[Array, " T"]
    ) -> Float[Array, "T M"]:
        """``y`` as a float ``(T, M)`` array; ``(T,)`` is accepted when M = 1."""
        y = _as_float(y)
        T, M = self.n_steps, self.obs_dim
        if y.ndim == 1 and M == 1:
            y = einx.id("t -> t 1", y)
        if tuple(y.shape) != (T, M):
            accepted = f"({T}, {M})" + (f" or ({T},)" if M == 1 else "")
            raise ValueError(
                f"y must have shape {accepted} for {T} steps and {M} outputs, "
                f"got {tuple(y.shape)!r}"
            )
        return y

    def _mask(
        self, mask: Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None
    ) -> Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None:
        """Validate ``mask`` as per step ``(T,)`` or per entry ``(T, M)``."""
        if mask is None:
            return None
        mask = jnp.asarray(mask).astype(bool)
        T, M = self.n_steps, self.obs_dim
        if tuple(mask.shape) not in ((T,), (T, M)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"mask has shape {tuple(mask.shape)!r}, but must be ({T},) to "
                f"mask whole steps or ({T}, {M}) to mask single entries"
            )
        return mask

    def _sanitise(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, "T M"],
        mask: Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None,
    ) -> Float[Array, "T M"]:
        """Zero the masked entries of ``y``, so a ``NaN`` there is inert."""
        if mask is None:
            return y
        keep = mask if mask.ndim == 2 else einx.id("t -> t 1", mask)
        return jnp.where(keep, y, jnp.zeros((), dtype=y.dtype))

    def _residual(self, y: Float[Array, "T M"]) -> Float[Array, "T M"]:
        """``y - b``, the observations of the zero-offset model."""
        if self.obs_offset is None:
            return y
        return y - self.obs_offset

    def filter(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, "T M"] | Float[Array, " T"],
        *,
        mask: Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None = None,
    ) -> FilterState:
        r"""Run the forward Kalman filter.

        Each step predicts, then updates on the observed entries of $y_k$,

        $$
        m_k^- = A_k m_{k-1}, \qquad P_k^- = A_k P_{k-1} A_k^\top + Q_k,
        $$

        and adds $\log \mathcal{N}(y_k;\, H_k m_k^- + b_k,\,
        H_k P_k^- H_k^\top + R_k)$ over those entries to the log marginal.

        Args:
            y: Observations, shaped ``(T, M)``; ``(T,)`` is accepted when
                $M = 1$. Masked entries may be ``NaN``.
            mask: Optional boolean mask, ``(T,)`` per step or ``(T, M)`` per
                entry, ``True`` where observed. ``None`` observes everything.

        Returns:
            The `gaussx.FilterState`: filtered and predicted means
            ``(T, D)`` and covariances ``(T, D, D)``, row $k - 1$ holding
            step $k$, and the scalar ``log_likelihood``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``y`` or ``mask`` has the wrong shape.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
            >>> prior = pss.LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
            ...     jnp.ones((3, 1, 1)), jnp.eye(1), jnp.full((3, 1, 1), 0.1),
            ...     0.5 * jnp.eye(1), jnp.zeros(1), jnp.eye(1),
            ... )
            >>> state = prior.filter(jnp.array([0.1, 0.3, 0.2]))
            >>> state.filtered_means.shape, state.log_likelihood.shape
            ((3, 1), ())
        """
        mask = self._mask(mask)
        residual = self._residual(self._sanitise(self._observations(y), mask))
        return gaussx.kalman_filter(
            transition=self.transition,
            obs_model=self.obs_model,
            process_noise=self.process_noise,
            obs_noise=self.obs_noise,
            observations=residual,
            init_mean=self.init_mean,
            init_cov=self.init_cov,
            mask=mask,
        )

    def log_marginal(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, "T M"] | Float[Array, " T"],
        *,
        mask: Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None = None,
    ) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        r"""Marginal log-likelihood $\log p(y_{\mathrm{obs}} \mid \theta)$.

        $$
        \log p(y \mid \theta) = \sum_{k=1}^{T}
          \log \mathcal{N}\!\left(y_k;\, H_k m_k^- + b_k,\,
          H_k P_k^- H_k^\top + R_k\right),
        $$

        restricted to the observed entries when a mask is given.

        Args:
            y: Observations, shaped ``(T, M)`` (or ``(T,)`` when $M = 1$);
                masked entries may be ``NaN``.
            mask: Optional ``(T,)`` or ``(T, M)`` mask, ``True`` where
                observed.

        Returns:
            The scalar log marginal of the observed entries.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
            >>> prior = pss.LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
            ...     jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.eye(2), (4, 2, 2)), jnp.eye(2),
            ...     jnp.broadcast_to(0.1 * jnp.eye(2), (4, 2, 2)),
            ...     0.5 * jnp.eye(2), jnp.zeros(2), jnp.eye(2),
            ... )
            >>> y = jnp.array([[0.1, 0.2], [0.3, jnp.nan], [0.2, 0.1], [0.0, 0.4]])
            >>> mask = ~jnp.isnan(y)  # one output missing at step 2
            >>> log_marg = prior.log_marginal(y, mask=mask)
        """
        return self.filter(y, mask=mask).log_likelihood

    def smooth(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, "T M"] | Float[Array, " T"],
        *,
        mask: Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "T D"], Float[Array, "T D D"], Float[Array, ""]]:
        r"""Run the Kalman filter and the RTS smoother.

        Returns the moments of $p(x_k \mid y_{1:T})$ for $k = 1, \dots, T$
        (row $k - 1$), via `gaussx.rts_smoother`.

        Args:
            y: Observations, shaped ``(T, M)`` (or ``(T,)`` when $M = 1$);
                masked entries may be ``NaN``.
            mask: Optional ``(T,)`` or ``(T, M)`` mask, ``True`` where
                observed.

        Returns:
            ``(smoothed_means, smoothed_covs, log_marginal)``, shaped
            ``(T, D)``, ``(T, D, D)`` and ``()``.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
            >>> prior = pss.LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
            ...     jnp.ones((3, 1, 1)), jnp.eye(1), jnp.full((3, 1, 1), 0.1),
            ...     0.5 * jnp.eye(1), jnp.zeros(1), jnp.eye(1),
            ... )
            >>> m, P, _ = prior.smooth(jnp.array([0.1, 0.3, 0.2]))
            >>> m.shape, P.shape
            ((3, 1), (3, 1, 1))
        """
        state = self.filter(y, mask=mask)
        m_smooth, P_smooth = gaussx.rts_smoother(state, self.transition)
        return m_smooth, P_smooth, state.log_likelihood

    def condition(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, "T M"] | Float[Array, " T"],
        *,
        mask: Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None = None,

        """Condition on ``y`` with the filter and the RTS smoother.

                masked entries may be ``NaN``.

            ... )
            >>> cond = prior.condition(jnp.array([0.1, 0.3, 0.2]))
            >>> cond.smoothed_means.shape
            (3, 1)

def filter(
    self,
    y: Float[Array, "T M"] | Float[Array, " T"],
    *,
    mask: Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None = None,
) -> FilterState:
    r"""Run the forward Kalman filter.

    Each step predicts, then updates on the observed entries of $y_k$,

    $$
    m_k^- = A_k m_{k-1}, \qquad P_k^- = A_k P_{k-1} A_k^\top + Q_k,
    $$

    and adds $\log \mathcal{N}(y_k;\, H_k m_k^- + b_k,\,
    H_k P_k^- H_k^\top + R_k)$ over those entries to the log marginal.

    Args:
        y: Observations, shaped ``(T, M)``; ``(T,)`` is accepted when
            $M = 1$. Masked entries may be ``NaN``.
        mask: Optional boolean mask, ``(T,)`` per step or ``(T, M)`` per
            entry, ``True`` where observed. ``None`` observes everything.

    Returns:
        The `gaussx.FilterState`: filtered and predicted means
        ``(T, D)`` and covariances ``(T, D, D)``, row $k - 1$ holding
        step $k$, and the scalar ``log_likelihood``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``y`` or ``mask`` has the wrong shape.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> prior = pss.LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
        ...     jnp.ones((3, 1, 1)), jnp.eye(1), jnp.full((3, 1, 1), 0.1),
        ...     0.5 * jnp.eye(1), jnp.zeros(1), jnp.eye(1),
        ... )
        >>> state = prior.filter(jnp.array([0.1, 0.3, 0.2]))
        >>> state.filtered_means.shape, state.log_likelihood.shape
        ((3, 1), ())
    """
    mask = self._mask(mask)
    residual = self._residual(self._sanitise(self._observations(y), mask))
    return gaussx.kalman_filter(
        transition=self.transition,
        obs_model=self.obs_model,
        process_noise=self.process_noise,
        obs_noise=self.obs_noise,
        observations=residual,
        init_mean=self.init_mean,
        init_cov=self.init_cov,
        mask=mask,
    )

docs.title: Nonlinear state-space models
docs.text:
nonlinear_ssm_factor scores a series under nonlinear dynamics x_k = f(x_{k-1}) + eta_k and observations y_k = h(x_k) + eps_k with gaussx.nonlinear_kalman_filter, adds its log likelihood to the NumPyro model and returns the gaussx.FilterState; the gaussx integrator picks the filter (TaylorIntegrator for the EKF, UnscentedIntegrator for the UKF and the default, CubatureIntegrator for the CKF, GaussHermiteIntegrator, MonteCarloIntegrator). The log likelihood is gaussx's moment-matched surrogate, exact only when f and h are affine, and the time convention and the mask= are those of LinearGaussianSSMPrior:

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro
import numpyro.distributions as dist
import pyrox_ssm as pss

def log_emission(y):  # x_k = a x_{k-1} + eta_k,  y_k = exp(x_k) + eps_k
    a = numpyro.sample("a", dist.Uniform(-1.0, 1.0))
    pss.nonlinear_ssm_factor(
        "y", lambda x: a * x, jnp.exp, 0.1 * jnp.eye(1), 0.05 * jnp.eye(1),
        y, jnp.zeros(1), jnp.eye(1),
    )

docs.text:
Register a nonlinear state-space model's log likelihood as a factor.

With \(T\) observation steps, a state of length \(D\) and observations of length \(M\), the model is

\[ x_0 \sim \mathcal{N}(m_0, P_0), \qquad x_k = f(x_{k-1}) + \eta_k, \quad \eta_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, Q_k), \qquad y_k = h(x_k) + \varepsilon_k, \quad \varepsilon_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R_k), \]

for \(k = 1, \dots, T\), with \(f\) the dynamics and \(h\) the obs_fn, and row \(k - 1\) of y holds step \(k\). This is the convention of gaussx.nonlinear_kalman_filter (and of pyrox_ssm.LinearGaussianSSMPrior), which predicts before every update: the first observation y[0] is \(y_1\), scored against \(f(x_0) + \eta_1\), not against \(x_0\).

gaussx.nonlinear_kalman_filter pushes the Gaussian belief through \(f\) and \(h\) by the integrator's moment transform. With \(m_k^-, P_k^-\) the predicted moments of \(x_k\) given \(y_{1:k-1}\), the update matches

\[ \hat{y}_k = \mathbb{E}[h(x_k)], \qquad S_k = \operatorname{Cov}[h(x_k)] + R_k, \qquad x_k \sim \mathcal{N}(m_k^-, P_k^-), \]

and the factor is the prediction-error sum

\[ \log p(y_{1:T} \mid \theta) \approx \sum_{k=1}^{T} \log \mathcal{N}(y_k;\, \hat{y}_k,\, S_k). \]

In gaussx's words, this log_likelihood "is a moment-matched surrogate, not the exact marginal likelihood: Σ_y,t is the matched observation covariance rather than the true one. It is exact when f and h are affine." Maximising it, or sampling under it, targets that surrogate.

The integrator picks the filter:

integrator filter gaussx.TaylorIntegrator extended Kalman filter (EKF) gaussx.UnscentedIntegrator unscented Kalman filter (UKF), the default gaussx.CubatureIntegrator cubature Kalman filter (CKF) gaussx.FifthOrderCubatureIntegrator degree-5 cubature Kalman filter gaussx.GaussHermiteIntegrator Gauss-Hermite Kalman filter (GHKF) gaussx.MonteCarloIntegrator Monte Carlo Kalman filter

Masked entries of y are replaced by zero before the filter runs, so a NaN placeholder there reaches neither the value nor a gradient. A per-step mask, shaped (T,), runs the predict only at a masked step; a per-entry mask, shaped (T, M), marginalises the masked entries out of the update, so either one scores exactly the observed entries.

Registers the one NumPyro site name, a factor. Library code adds no jax.jit; jit the model or the loss at the top.

required obs_fn Callable[[Float[Array, ' D']], Float[Array, ' M']]

Observation map \(h\), from a (D,) state to an (M,) observation.

required process_noise Float[Array, 'D D'] | Float[Array, 'T D D'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Process-noise covariance \(Q_k\): one (D, D) matrix for every step, a (T, D, D) stack, or a lineax operator.

Observation-noise covariance \(R_k\), (M, M), (T, M, M) or a lineax operator.

Observations \(y_{1:T}\), shaped (T, M); masked entries may be NaN.

def nonlinear_ssm_factor(
    name: str,
    dynamics: Callable[[Float[Array, " D"]], Float[Array, " D"]],
    obs_fn: Callable[[Float[Array, " D"]], Float[Array, " M"]],
    process_noise: Float[Array, "D D"]
    | Float[Array, "T D D"]
    | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    obs_noise: Float[Array, "M M"] | Float[Array, "T M M"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    y: Float[Array, "T M"],
    init_mean: Float[Array, " D"],
    init_cov: Float[Array, "D D"],
    *,
    integrator: AbstractIntegrator | None = None,
    mask: Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None = None,
    joseph: bool = True,
    solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None,
) -> FilterState:
    r"""Register a nonlinear state-space model's log likelihood as a factor.

    With $T$ observation steps, a state of length $D$ and observations of
    length $M$, the model is

    $$
    x_0 \sim \mathcal{N}(m_0, P_0), \qquad
    x_k = f(x_{k-1}) + \eta_k, \quad \eta_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, Q_k), \qquad
    y_k = h(x_k) + \varepsilon_k, \quad \varepsilon_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R_k),
    $$

    for $k = 1, \dots, T$, with $f$ the ``dynamics`` and $h$ the
    ``obs_fn``, and row $k - 1$ of ``y`` holds step $k$. This is the
    convention of `gaussx.nonlinear_kalman_filter` (and of
    `pyrox_ssm.LinearGaussianSSMPrior`), which predicts before every
    update: the first observation ``y[0]`` is $y_1$, scored against
    $f(x_0) + \eta_1$, not against $x_0$.

    `gaussx.nonlinear_kalman_filter` pushes the Gaussian belief through $f$
    and $h$ by the integrator's moment transform. With
    $m_k^-, P_k^-$ the predicted moments of $x_k$ given $y_{1:k-1}$, the
    update matches

    $$
    \hat{y}_k = \mathbb{E}[h(x_k)], \qquad
    S_k = \operatorname{Cov}[h(x_k)] + R_k, \qquad
    x_k \sim \mathcal{N}(m_k^-, P_k^-),
    $$

    and the factor is the prediction-error sum

    $$
    \log p(y_{1:T} \mid \theta) \approx \sum_{k=1}^{T}
      \log \mathcal{N}(y_k;\, \hat{y}_k,\, S_k).
    $$

    In gaussx's words, this ``log_likelihood`` "is a moment-matched
    surrogate, not the exact marginal likelihood: Σ_y,t is the matched
    observation covariance rather than the true one. It is exact when f and
    h are affine." Maximising it, or sampling under it, targets that
    surrogate.

    The integrator picks the filter:

    | integrator | filter |
    |---|---|
    | `gaussx.TaylorIntegrator` | extended Kalman filter (EKF) |
    | `gaussx.UnscentedIntegrator` | unscented Kalman filter (UKF), the default |
    | `gaussx.CubatureIntegrator` | cubature Kalman filter (CKF) |
    | `gaussx.FifthOrderCubatureIntegrator` | degree-5 cubature Kalman filter |
    | `gaussx.GaussHermiteIntegrator` | Gauss-Hermite Kalman filter (GHKF) |
    | `gaussx.MonteCarloIntegrator` | Monte Carlo Kalman filter |

    Masked entries of ``y`` are replaced by zero before the filter runs, so
    a ``NaN`` placeholder there reaches neither the value nor a gradient. A
    per-step mask, shaped ``(T,)``, runs the predict only at a masked step;
    a per-entry mask, shaped ``(T, M)``, marginalises the masked entries
    out of the update, so either one scores exactly the observed entries.

    Registers the one NumPyro site ``name``, a factor. Library code adds no
    `jax.jit`; jit the model or the loss at the top.

    Args:
        name: The factor site name.
        dynamics: Deterministic dynamics $f$, from a ``(D,)`` state to a
            ``(D,)`` state; the process noise is added separately.
        obs_fn: Observation map $h$, from a ``(D,)`` state to an ``(M,)``
            observation.
        process_noise: Process-noise covariance $Q_k$: one ``(D, D)``
            matrix for every step, a ``(T, D, D)`` stack, or a lineax
            operator.
        obs_noise: Observation-noise covariance $R_k$, ``(M, M)``,
            ``(T, M, M)`` or a lineax operator.
        y: Observations $y_{1:T}$, shaped ``(T, M)``; masked entries may be
            ``NaN``.
        init_mean: Mean $m_0$ of the initial state $x_0$, shaped ``(D,)``.
        init_cov: Covariance $P_0$ of $x_0$, shaped ``(D, D)``.
        integrator: The gaussx moment-matching rule. ``None`` (the default)
            is ``gaussx.UnscentedIntegrator(alpha=1.0)``, the default of
            `gaussx.nonlinear_kalman_filter`: derivative-free and exact for
            affine maps. `gaussx.UnscentedIntegrator`'s own default
            ``alpha=1e-3`` recovers the moments by cancellation and loses
            about six digits, which float32 cannot afford.
        mask: Optional boolean mask, ``(T,)`` per step or ``(T, M)`` per
            entry, ``True`` where observed. ``None`` observes everything.
        joseph: Use the Joseph-form covariance update, passed through to
            `gaussx.nonlinear_kalman_filter`. Defaults to ``True``.
        solver: Solver strategy for $S_k$, passed through to
            `gaussx.nonlinear_kalman_filter`. ``None`` factorises $S_k$ once
            by Cholesky.

    Returns:
        The `gaussx.FilterState`: filtered and predicted means ``(T, D)``
        and covariances ``(T, D, D)``, row $k - 1$ holding step $k$, and the
        scalar ``log_likelihood`` registered as the factor.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``y`` is not ``(T, M)`` or ``mask`` is not ``(T,)``
            or ``(T, M)``; gaussx raises for misshapen noise covariances.

    Examples:
        A log-emission AR(1) state, $x_k = a x_{k-1} + \eta_k$ observed
        through $y_k = \exp(x_k) + \varepsilon_k$, with a prior on $a$:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import numpyro
        >>> import numpyro.distributions as dist
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> def model(y):
        ...     a = numpyro.sample("a", dist.Uniform(-1.0, 1.0))
        ...     pss.nonlinear_ssm_factor(
        ...         "y",
        ...         lambda x: a * x,
        ...         jnp.exp,
        ...         0.1 * jnp.eye(1),
        ...         0.05 * jnp.eye(1),
        ...         y,
        ...         jnp.zeros(1),
        ...         jnp.eye(1),
        ...     )
        >>> y = jnp.array([[1.1], [0.9], [1.3], [1.0]])
        >>> trace = numpyro.handlers.trace(numpyro.handlers.seed(model, 0)).get_trace(y)
        >>> sorted(trace)
        ['a', 'y']
    """
    y, mask = _check_observations(y, mask)
    if integrator is None:
        integrator = gaussx.UnscentedIntegrator(alpha=1.0)
    state = gaussx.nonlinear_kalman_filter(
        dynamics,
        obs_fn,
        process_noise,
        obs_noise,
        y,
        init_mean,
        init_cov,
        integrator=integrator,
        mask=mask,
        joseph=joseph,
        solver=solver,
    )
    numpyro.factor(name, state.log_likelihood)
    return state

docs.title: Markov GP — Kalman / RTS workflow
docs.text:
MarkovGPPrior consumes any SDEKernel over a sorted 1-D grid and gives O(N d^3) marginal likelihood (forward Kalman filter) and posterior smoothing (backward RTS), where d is the SDE state dimension. Use it for temporal GP regression / forecasting when the training grid lives on a single time axis. Predictions at arbitrary test times — including forecasting, backcasting, and within-window interpolation — re-run the filter+smoother over the merged grid with the test points masked out of the update step.

import jax.numpy as jnp
from pyrox_ssm import MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior, markov_gp_factor

times = jnp.linspace(0.0, 5.0, 200)
y     = jnp.sin(times) + 0.05 * jnp.cos(7.0 * times)

prior = MarkovGPPrior(
    MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=0.5, order=1),  # Matern-3/2
    times,
)
log_marg = prior.log_marginal(y, jnp.asarray(0.01))     # Kalman forward
cond     = prior.condition(y, jnp.asarray(0.01))        # filter + RTS smoother
mean, var = cond.predict(jnp.linspace(-0.5, 6.0, 50))   # arbitrary test times

Inside a NumPyro model, swap gp_factor for markov_gp_factor:

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro
from numpyro import distributions as dist
from pyrox_ssm import MarkovGPPrior, MaternSDE, markov_gp_factor

def temporal_model(times, y):
    sigma2 = numpyro.sample("variance",  dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0))
    ell    = numpyro.sample("lengthscale", dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0))
    sde    = MaternSDE(variance=sigma2, lengthscale=ell, order=1)
    prior  = MarkovGPPrior(sde, times)
    markov_gp_factor("obs", prior, y, jnp.array(0.01))

For non-Gaussian likelihoods on the Markov path, see the Markov non-Gaussian strategies below; for inducing-grid scalability, the sparse Markov GP.

docs.title: MarkovGPPrior
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Linear-time temporal GP prior over a sorted 1-D grid.

Wraps any pyrox_ssm.SDEKernel (e.g. pyrox_ssm.MaternSDE, pyrox_ssm.SumSDE, pyrox_ssm.PeriodicSDE) to give Kalman filtering for the marginal log-likelihood and RTS smoothing for the posterior on the training grid. Supports an optional mean function and a small observation-noise floor for numerical stability.

Attributes:

Name Type Description sde_kernel SDEKernel

Any SDEKernel. Provides (F, L, H, Q_c, P_inf) via sde_params() and the discrete transition sequence via discretise_sequence(dt).

times Float[Array, ' N']

Sorted, strictly increasing observation times of shape (N,). Concrete (non-traced) times arrays are validated for monotonicity at construction time; under jax.jit / SVI / MCMC the input is a tracer and the check is silently skipped — callers must guarantee monotonicity in that case.

mean_fn Callable[[Float[Array, ' N']], Float[Array, ' N']] | None

Optional callable mapping times -> (N,) mean values. Defaults to the zero mean. The mean is subtracted from observations before filtering and added back at predict time.

obs_noise_floor float

Small extra diagonal added to the observation variance R = noise_var + obs_noise_floor for stability when noise_var is near zero. Defaults to 0.0.

init_cov Float[Array, 'd d'] | None

Optional (d, d) covariance of the state at the first time point. None (the default) asks the kernel via initial_covariance(), which is \(P_\infty\) for a stationary kernel — so nothing changes for the kernels that have one — and an explicit diffuse covariance for a non-stationary one such as gaussx.IntegratedWienerSDE. Supply it to state what is known about the level (and its derivatives) before the first observation. Worth supplying for the site-based non-Gaussian strategies in particular: pyrox_ssm.PosteriorLinearizationMarkov and pyrox_ssm.ExpectationPropagationMarkov seed their cavities from the prior marginal variance, and a very diffuse prior can overflow their quadrature under an exponential-link likelihood — as a stationary kernel with an equally large variance does.

Every method that reads observations (filter, smooth, log_marginal, condition, condition_nongauss) takes an optional mask of shape (N,). A masked step runs the Kalman predict only, so it adds nothing to the log marginal, and its observation is replaced by zero before any arithmetic, so a NaN placeholder there is safe. pyrox_ssm.pad_sites builds such masks for ragged per-site series.

Examples:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> from pyrox_ssm import MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior
>>> times = jnp.linspace(0.0, 5.0, 50)
>>> sde = MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=0.5, order=1)
>>> prior = MarkovGPPrior(sde, times)
>>> y = jnp.sin(times) + 0.05 * jnp.cos(3.0 * times)
>>> log_marg = prior.log_marginal(y, jnp.asarray(0.01))
>>> mask = jnp.arange(50) % 5 != 0  # every fifth step unobserved
>>> log_marg_masked = prior.log_marginal(y, jnp.asarray(0.01), mask=mask)
Notes

The solver-strategy plumbing used by pyrox_gp.GPPrior does not apply here — Kalman filtering is its own linear-algebra path and does not factor through gaussx.AbstractSolverStrategy.

class MarkovGPPrior(eqx.Module):
    r"""Linear-time temporal GP prior over a sorted 1-D grid.

    Wraps any `pyrox_ssm.SDEKernel` (e.g. `pyrox_ssm.MaternSDE`,
    `pyrox_ssm.SumSDE`, `pyrox_ssm.PeriodicSDE`) to give Kalman
    filtering for the marginal log-likelihood and RTS smoothing for the
    posterior on the training grid. Supports an optional mean function and a
    small observation-noise floor for numerical stability.

    Attributes:
        sde_kernel: Any `SDEKernel`. Provides ``(F, L, H, Q_c, P_inf)``
            via ``sde_params()`` and the discrete transition sequence via
            ``discretise_sequence(dt)``.
        times: Sorted, strictly increasing observation times of shape
            ``(N,)``. Concrete (non-traced) ``times`` arrays are validated
            for monotonicity at construction time; under `jax.jit` /
            SVI / MCMC the input is a tracer and the check is silently
            skipped — callers must guarantee monotonicity in that case.
        mean_fn: Optional callable mapping ``times -> (N,)`` mean values.
            Defaults to the zero mean. The mean is subtracted from
            observations before filtering and added back at predict time.
        obs_noise_floor: Small extra diagonal added to the observation
            variance ``R = noise_var + obs_noise_floor`` for stability when
            ``noise_var`` is near zero. Defaults to ``0.0``.
        init_cov: Optional ``(d, d)`` covariance of the state at the first
            time point. ``None`` (the default) asks the kernel via
            ``initial_covariance()``, which is $P_\infty$ for a stationary
            kernel — so nothing changes for the kernels that have one — and
            an explicit diffuse covariance for a non-stationary one such as
            `gaussx.IntegratedWienerSDE`. Supply it to state what is known
            about the level (and its derivatives) before the first
            observation. Worth supplying for the site-based non-Gaussian
            strategies in particular: `pyrox_ssm.PosteriorLinearizationMarkov`
            and `pyrox_ssm.ExpectationPropagationMarkov` seed their cavities
            from the prior marginal variance, and a very diffuse prior can
            overflow their quadrature under an exponential-link likelihood
            — as a stationary kernel with an equally large variance does.

    Every method that reads observations (`filter`, `smooth`,
    `log_marginal`, `condition`, `condition_nongauss`) takes an optional
    ``mask`` of shape ``(N,)``. A masked step runs the Kalman predict only,
    so it adds nothing to the log marginal, and its observation is replaced
    by zero before any arithmetic, so a ``NaN`` placeholder there is safe.
    `pyrox_ssm.pad_sites` builds such masks for ragged per-site series.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> from pyrox_ssm import MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior
        >>> times = jnp.linspace(0.0, 5.0, 50)
        >>> sde = MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=0.5, order=1)
        >>> prior = MarkovGPPrior(sde, times)
        >>> y = jnp.sin(times) + 0.05 * jnp.cos(3.0 * times)
        >>> log_marg = prior.log_marginal(y, jnp.asarray(0.01))
        >>> mask = jnp.arange(50) % 5 != 0  # every fifth step unobserved
        >>> log_marg_masked = prior.log_marginal(y, jnp.asarray(0.01), mask=mask)

    Notes:
        The solver-strategy plumbing used by `pyrox_gp.GPPrior` does
        not apply here — Kalman filtering is its own linear-algebra path
        and does not factor through ``gaussx.AbstractSolverStrategy``.
    """

    sde_kernel: SDEKernel
    times: Float[Array, " N"]
    mean_fn: Callable[[Float[Array, " N"]], Float[Array, " N"]] | None = None
    obs_noise_floor: float = eqx.field(static=True, default=0.0)
    init_cov: Float[Array, "d d"] | None = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        sde_kernel: SDEKernel,
        times: Float[Array, " N"],
        mean_fn: Callable[[Float[Array, " N"]], Float[Array, " N"]] | None = None,
        obs_noise_floor: float = 0.0,
        init_cov: Float[Array, "d d"] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if obs_noise_floor < 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"obs_noise_floor must be non-negative, got {obs_noise_floor!r}"
            )
        times_arr = jnp.asarray(times, dtype=jnp.result_type(times, 0.0))
        if times_arr.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"times must be 1-D, got shape {tuple(times_arr.shape)!r}")
        # Eager monotonicity check for concrete (non-traced) inputs only.
        # Under ``jax.jit`` / SVI / similar transforms ``times`` may arrive as
        # a tracer; the ``bool`` conversion would raise, so we silence that
        # path and let downstream Kalman steps trust the contract.
        if times_arr.shape[0] >= 2:
            try:
                if not bool(jnp.all(jnp.diff(times_arr) > 0)):
                    raise ValueError("times must be strictly increasing")
            except jax.errors.TracerBoolConversionError:
                pass
        if init_cov is not None:
            # Promoted like ``times``: an integer covariance would seed the
            # scan with an int carry and fail inside it on a dtype mismatch.
            init_cov = jnp.asarray(init_cov, dtype=jnp.result_type(init_cov, 0.0))
            d = sde_kernel.state_dim
            if init_cov.shape != (d, d):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"init_cov must be ({d}, {d}) for a state dimension of "
                    f"{d}, got shape {tuple(init_cov.shape)!r}"
                )
        self.sde_kernel = sde_kernel
        self.times = times_arr
        self.mean_fn = mean_fn
        self.obs_noise_floor = float(obs_noise_floor)
        self.init_cov = init_cov

    @property
    def state_dim(self) -> int:
        """SDE state dimension $d$ for this kernel."""
        return self.sde_kernel.state_dim

    def initial_covariance(self) -> Float[Array, "d d"]:
        r"""Covariance the Kalman recursions start from.

        The ``init_cov`` given at construction if there is one, otherwise
        whatever the kernel reports — $P_\infty$ for a stationary kernel,
        an explicit diffuse covariance for a non-stationary one. This is
        the single seed every filtering surface here uses, so a kernel
        with no $P_\infty$ is only a problem for the paths that are
        *defined* in terms of it (`log_prob`, the dense Gram).
        """
        if self.init_cov is not None:
            return self.init_cov
        return _kernel_initial_covariance(self.sde_kernel)

    def mean(self, times: Float[Array, " M"]) -> Float[Array, " M"]:
        """Evaluate the mean function at ``times``; zero by default."""
        if self.mean_fn is None:
            return jnp.zeros_like(times)
        return self.mean_fn(times)

    def _R(self, noise_var: Float[Array, ""]) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        return jnp.asarray(noise_var) + jnp.asarray(self.obs_noise_floor)

    def _observed(self, mask: Bool[Array, " N"] | None) -> Bool[Array, " N"] | None:
        """``mask`` checked against ``times``, or ``None`` when not given."""
        return None if mask is None else _observation_mask(mask, self.times)

    def as_lgssm(self, noise_var: Float[Array, ""]) -> LinearGaussianSSMPrior:
        r"""This prior as a `pyrox_ssm.LinearGaussianSSMPrior`.

        With $\Delta t_1 = 0$ and $\Delta t_k = t_k - t_{k-1}$, the
        kernel's discretisation gives the transitions and process noise,

        $$
        (A_k, Q_k) = \mathrm{discretise}(\Delta t_k), \qquad
        H_k = H, \qquad R_k = \sigma_n^2 + \epsilon, \qquad
        b_k = \mu(t_k), \qquad (m_0, P_0) = (0, P_{\mathrm{init}}),
        $$

        where $\epsilon$ is ``obs_noise_floor``, $\mu$ the mean function
        and $P_{\mathrm{init}}$ `initial_covariance` ($P_\infty$ for a
        stationary kernel). The zero first step makes $A_1 = I$ and
        $Q_1 = 0$, so the first observation sees the initial state itself.
        `filter`, `smooth` and `log_marginal` run through this model, so
        the two give the same results bit for bit.

        Args:
            noise_var: Observation noise variance $\sigma_n^2$.

        Returns:
            The `pyrox_ssm.LinearGaussianSSMPrior` over ``times``, with
            $T = N$ steps, state dimension $d$ and one output.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> from pyrox_ssm import MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior
            >>> prior = MarkovGPPrior(MaternSDE(1.0, 0.5, order=1), jnp.arange(4.0))
            >>> lgssm = prior.as_lgssm(jnp.asarray(0.1))
            >>> lgssm.transition.shape, lgssm.obs_model.shape
            ((4, 2, 2), (1, 2))
            >>> y = jnp.array([0.1, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2])
            >>> log_marg = lgssm.log_marginal(y)  # == prior.log_marginal(y, 0.1)
        """
        _F, _L, H, _Qc, _P_inf = self.sde_kernel.sde_params()
        init_cov = self.initial_covariance()
        A_seq, Q_seq = self.sde_kernel.discretise_sequence(_build_dt_full(self.times))
        R_seq = jnp.broadcast_to(self._R(noise_var), self.times.shape)
        return LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
            transition=A_seq,
            obs_model=H,
            process_noise=Q_seq,
            obs_noise=einx.id("n -> n 1 1", R_seq),
            init_mean=jnp.zeros(init_cov.shape[0], dtype=init_cov.dtype),
            init_cov=init_cov,
            obs_offset=einx.id("n -> n 1", self.mean(self.times)),
        )

    def filter(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, " N"],
        noise_var: Float[Array, ""],
        *,
        mask: Bool[Array, " N"] | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[
        Float[Array, "N d"],
        Float[Array, "N d d"],
        Float[Array, "N d"],
        Float[Array, "N d d"],
        Float[Array, ""],
    ]:
        r"""Run the forward Kalman filter on the training grid.

        With $o_k \in \{0, 1\}$ the mask, an observed step ($o_k = 1$)
        runs the usual update and a masked step ($o_k = 0$) runs the
        predict only,

        $$
        \mu_k^+ = \mu_k^-, \qquad P_k^+ = P_k^-, \qquad
        \log p(y \mid \theta)
          = \sum_k o_k \log \mathcal{N}(y_k;\, H \mu_k^-,\, H P_k^- H^\top + R).
        $$

        Args:
            y: Observations of shape ``(N,)``. Masked entries are replaced
                by zero before the residual, so they may be ``NaN``.
            noise_var: Observation noise variance $\sigma_n^2$.
            mask: Optional ``(N,)`` boolean mask, ``True`` where a step is
                observed. ``None`` observes every step.

        Returns:
            Tuple ``(m_pred, P_pred, m_filt, P_filt, log_marginal)`` where
            each ``*_pred`` / ``*_filt`` is shaped ``(N, d)`` or
            ``(N, d, d)`` and ``log_marginal`` is the scalar log-likelihood
            ``log p(y | theta)`` of the observed steps.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``mask`` is not shaped like ``times``.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> from pyrox_ssm import MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior
            >>> prior = MarkovGPPrior(MaternSDE(1.0, 0.5, order=1), jnp.arange(4.0))
            >>> y = jnp.array([0.1, jnp.nan, 0.3, 0.2])
            >>> mask = jnp.array([True, False, True, True])
            >>> *_, log_marg = prior.filter(y, jnp.asarray(0.1), mask=mask)
        """
        lgssm = self.as_lgssm(noise_var)
        return _filter_tuple(lgssm.filter(y, mask=self._observed(mask)))

    def log_marginal(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, " N"],
        noise_var: Float[Array, ""],
        *,
        mask: Bool[Array, " N"] | None = None,
    ) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        r"""Marginal log-likelihood ``log p(y | theta)`` via Kalman filtering.

        A masked step contributes nothing,

        $$
        \log p(y \mid \theta)
          = \sum_k o_k \log \mathcal{N}(y_k;\, H \mu_k^-,\, H P_k^- H^\top + R),
        $$

        so padding a series after its last observation and masking the
        padded steps leaves the result unchanged.

        Args:
            y: Observations of shape ``(N,)``; masked entries may be ``NaN``.
            noise_var: Observation noise variance $\sigma_n^2$.
            mask: Optional ``(N,)`` boolean mask, ``True`` where observed.

        Returns:
            The scalar log marginal of the observed steps.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> from pyrox_ssm import MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior
            >>> prior = MarkovGPPrior(MaternSDE(1.0, 0.5, order=1), jnp.arange(4.0))
            >>> y = jnp.array([0.1, 0.4, 0.3, jnp.nan])
            >>> mask = jnp.array([True, True, True, False])
            >>> log_marg = prior.log_marginal(y, jnp.asarray(0.1), mask=mask)
        """
        lgssm = self.as_lgssm(noise_var)
        return lgssm.log_marginal(y, mask=self._observed(mask))

    def smooth(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, " N"],
        noise_var: Float[Array, ""],
        *,
        mask: Bool[Array, " N"] | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "N d"], Float[Array, "N d d"], Float[Array, ""]]:
        r"""Run filter + RTS smoother on the training grid.

        Masked steps run the predict only (see `filter`), so their smoothed
        moments are interpolations from the observed neighbours.

        Args:
            y: Observations of shape ``(N,)``; masked entries may be ``NaN``.
            noise_var: Observation noise variance $\sigma_n^2$.
            mask: Optional ``(N,)`` boolean mask, ``True`` where observed.

        Returns:
            ``(m_smooth, P_smooth, log_marginal)`` over the training times,
            shaped ``(N, d)``, ``(N, d, d)`` and ``()``.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> from pyrox_ssm import MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior
            >>> prior = MarkovGPPrior(MaternSDE(1.0, 0.5, order=1), jnp.arange(4.0))
            >>> mask = jnp.array([True, False, True, True])
            >>> m, P, _ = prior.smooth(jnp.ones(4), jnp.asarray(0.1), mask=mask)
            >>> m.shape, P.shape
            ((4, 2), (4, 2, 2))
        """
        lgssm = self.as_lgssm(noise_var)
        return lgssm.smooth(y, mask=self._observed(mask))

    def condition(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, " N"],
        noise_var: Float[Array, ""],
        *,
        mask: Bool[Array, " N"] | None = None,
    ) -> ConditionedMarkovGP:
        """Condition on Gaussian-likelihood observations via filter + smoother.

        Args:
            y: Observations of shape ``(N,)``; masked entries may be ``NaN``.
            noise_var: Observation noise variance.
            mask: Optional ``(N,)`` boolean mask, ``True`` where observed. The
                conditioned GP keeps it, so `ConditionedMarkovGP.predict`
                treats the masked steps as unobserved too.

        Returns:
            The `ConditionedMarkovGP`, holding ``y`` with its masked entries
            set to zero.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> from pyrox_ssm import MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior
            >>> prior = MarkovGPPrior(MaternSDE(1.0, 0.5, order=1), jnp.arange(4.0))
            >>> mask = jnp.array([True, False, True, True])
            >>> cond = prior.condition(jnp.ones(4), jnp.asarray(0.1), mask=mask)
            >>> mean, var = cond.predict(jnp.array([1.0, 5.0]))
        """
        m_smooth, P_smooth, log_marg = self.smooth(y, noise_var, mask=mask)
        return ConditionedMarkovGP(
            prior=self,
            y=_sanitise(y, mask),
            noise_var=jnp.asarray(noise_var),
            smoothed_means=m_smooth,
            smoothed_covs=P_smooth,
            log_marginal=log_marg,
            mask=None if mask is None else _observation_mask(mask, self.times),
        )

    def condition_nongauss(
        self,
        likelihood: Likelihood,
        y: Float[Array, " N"],
        *,
        strategy: _NonGaussMarkovStrategy,
        mask: Bool[Array, " N"] | None = None,
    ) -> NonGaussConditionedMarkovGP:
        """Condition on a non-Gaussian likelihood via a site-based strategy.

        Convenience that forwards to ``strategy.fit(self, likelihood, y)``.
        Pick any of the Markov-aware site-based strategies in
        `pyrox_ssm._inference_nongauss_markov`:
        `pyrox_ssm.LaplaceMarkovInference`,
        `pyrox_ssm.GaussNewtonMarkovInference`,
        `pyrox_ssm.PosteriorLinearizationMarkov`, or
        `pyrox_ssm.ExpectationPropagationMarkov`. Returns a
        `pyrox_ssm.NonGaussConditionedMarkovGP` with the same
        ``predict`` API as the Gaussian-likelihood
        `ConditionedMarkovGP`.

        Args:
            likelihood: Any scalar-latent `pyrox.likelihoods.Likelihood`.
            y: Observations of shape ``(N,)``; masked entries may be ``NaN``.
            strategy: The site-based strategy that fits the sites.
            mask: Optional ``(N,)`` boolean mask, ``True`` where observed. A
                masked site has zero gradient and curvature, so its site
                precision is zero and the filter skips its update. Passed
                to ``strategy.fit`` only when given, so a strategy without
                a ``mask`` keyword still works unmasked.

        Returns:
            The `pyrox_ssm.NonGaussConditionedMarkovGP` from the strategy.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> from pyrox_gp import BernoulliLikelihood
            >>> from pyrox_ssm import LaplaceMarkovInference, MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior
            >>> prior = MarkovGPPrior(MaternSDE(1.0, 0.5, order=1), jnp.arange(4.0))
            >>> y = jnp.array([1.0, 0.0, jnp.nan, 1.0])
            >>> cond = prior.condition_nongauss(
            ...     BernoulliLikelihood(), y,
            ...     strategy=LaplaceMarkovInference(),
            ...     mask=jnp.array([True, True, False, True]),
            ... )
        """
        if mask is None:
            return strategy.fit(self, likelihood, y)
        return strategy.fit(self, likelihood, y, mask=mask)

    def log_prob(self, f: Float[Array, " N"]) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        r"""Log density of an exact-state path $f(t_n) = H x_n$ under the prior.

        Evaluates ``log N(f | mu(times), K_NN)`` where ``K_NN`` is the dense
        Gram of the kernel encoded by ``sde_kernel`` on ``self.times``.
        Computes the dense covariance via ``H exp(F |t_i - t_j|) P_inf H^T``
        — one ``expm`` per pairwise lag, costing $O(N^2 d^3)$ for the
        Gram plus $O(N^3)$ for the Cholesky solve — intended for
        sanity checks and small-grid use rather than scalable inference.
        For training, prefer `log_marginal`.
        """
        K = _dense_sde_gram(self.sde_kernel, self.times)
        cov_op = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(K, lx.positive_semidefinite_tag)
        return gaussx.gaussian_log_prob(self.mean(self.times), cov_op, f)

      = \sum_k o_k \log \mathcal{N}(y_k;\, H \mu_k^-,\, H P_k^- H^\top + R),
    $$

    so padding a series after its last observation and masking the
    padded steps leaves the result unchanged.

        y: Observations of shape ``(N,)``; masked entries may be ``NaN``.
        noise_var: Observation noise variance $\sigma_n^2$.
        mask: Optional ``(N,)`` boolean mask, ``True`` where observed.

    Returns:
        The scalar log marginal of the observed steps.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> from pyrox_ssm import MaternSDE, MarkovGPPrior
        >>> prior = MarkovGPPrior(MaternSDE(1.0, 0.5, order=1), jnp.arange(4.0))
        >>> y = jnp.array([0.1, 0.4, 0.3, jnp.nan])
        >>> mask = jnp.array([True, True, True, False])
        >>> log_marg = prior.log_marginal(y, jnp.asarray(0.1), mask=mask)
    """
    lgssm = self.as_lgssm(noise_var)
    return lgssm.log_marginal(y, mask=self._observed(mask))

        >>> cond = prior.condition_nongauss(
        ...     BernoulliLikelihood(), y,
        ...     strategy=LaplaceMarkovInference(),
        ...     mask=jnp.array([True, True, False, True]),
        ... )
    """
    if mask is None:

Computes the dense covariance via H exp(F |t_i - t_j|) P_inf H^T — one expm per pairwise lag, costing \(O(N^2 d^3)\) for the Gram plus \(O(N^3)\) for the Cholesky solve — intended for sanity checks and small-grid use rather than scalable inference. def log_prob(self, f: Float[Array, " N"]) -> Float[Array, ""]:
    r"""Log density of an exact-state path $f(t_n) = H x_n$ under the prior.

    Evaluates ``log N(f | mu(times), K_NN)`` where ``K_NN`` is the dense
    Gram of the kernel encoded by ``sde_kernel`` on ``self.times``.
    Computes the dense covariance via ``H exp(F |t_i - t_j|) P_inf H^T``
    — one ``expm`` per pairwise lag, costing $O(N^2 d^3)$ for the
    Gram plus $O(N^3)$ for the Cholesky solve — intended for
    sanity checks and small-grid use rather than scalable inference.
    For training, prefer `log_marginal`.
    """
    K = _dense_sde_gram(self.sde_kernel, self.times)
    cov_op = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(K, lx.positive_semidefinite_tag)
    return gaussx.gaussian_log_prob(self.mean(self.times), cov_op, f)

class ConditionedMarkovGP(eqx.Module):
    """Markov GP conditioned on Gaussian-likelihood observations.

    Holds the smoothed posterior on the training grid plus the marginal
    log-likelihood. Use `predict` for marginal posterior mean / variance
    at arbitrary test times.

    Attributes:
        prior: The originating `MarkovGPPrior`.
        y: Observations of shape ``(N,)``.
        noise_var: Observation variance used for conditioning.
        smoothed_means: ``(N, d)`` smoothed state means at training times.
        smoothed_covs: ``(N, d, d)`` smoothed state covariances at training
            times.
        log_marginal: Scalar $\\log p(y \\mid \\theta)$.
        mask: Optional ``(N,)`` boolean observation mask from
            `MarkovGPPrior.condition`; `predict` leaves the masked steps
            out of the update. ``None`` means every step is observed.
    """

    prior: MarkovGPPrior
    y: Float[Array, " N"]
    noise_var: Float[Array, ""]
    smoothed_means: Float[Array, "N d"]
    smoothed_covs: Float[Array, "N d d"]
    log_marginal: Float[Array, ""]
    mask: Bool[Array, " N"] | None = None

    def predict(
        self,
        t_star: Float[Array, " M"],
        *,
        include_noise: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, " M"], Float[Array, " M"]]:
        r"""Predictive marginals ``(mean, var)`` at arbitrary test times.

        With ``include_noise=False`` (the default) ``var`` is the variance of
        the latent signal, $\sigma_*^2$. With ``include_noise=True`` it is the
        variance of a new observation at each test time,
        $\sigma_*^2 + R$, where $R$ = ``noise_var + obs_noise_floor`` is the
        observation variance the posterior was conditioned on. Use it for the
        band a withheld observation should fall in. The mean is the same
        either way.

        Implementation: re-run the filter+smoother over the merged grid
        ``sort(times \\cup t_star)`` with the test points masked out of the
        update step, then read off the smoothed marginals at the test
        positions via ``H @ m`` and ``H @ P @ H^T``. Cost is
        $O((N + M)\\,d^3)$. Handles training-grid lookups, forecasting,
        backcasting, and within-window interpolation under one code path.
        """
        F, _L, H, _Qc, _P_inf = self.prior.sde_kernel.sde_params()
        init_cov = self.prior.initial_covariance()
        times = self.prior.times
        t_star = jnp.asarray(t_star)

        N = times.shape[0]
        M = t_star.shape[0]
        merged = jnp.concatenate([times, t_star], axis=0)
        # Stable sort so the relative ordering of identical times is preserved
        # (training point sorts before a duplicate test point, so the test
        # point still sees the observation update earlier in the grid).
        order = jnp.argsort(merged, stable=True)
        merged_sorted = merged[order]

        observed = (
            jnp.ones(N, dtype=times.dtype)
            if self.mask is None
            else self.mask.astype(times.dtype)
        )
        is_obs = jnp.concatenate([observed, jnp.zeros(M, dtype=times.dtype)])[order]
        residual_full = jnp.concatenate(
            [self.y - self.prior.mean(times), jnp.zeros(M, dtype=self.y.dtype)]
        )[order]

        dt_full = _build_dt_full(merged_sorted)
        A_seq, Q_seq = self.prior.sde_kernel.discretise_sequence(dt_full)
        R_seq = jnp.broadcast_to(self.prior._R(self.noise_var), merged_sorted.shape)
        m_pred, P_pred, m_filt, P_filt, _ = _kalman_filter(
            F, H, init_cov, A_seq, Q_seq, residual_full, is_obs, R_seq
        )
        m_smooth, P_smooth = _rts_smoother(m_pred, P_pred, m_filt, P_filt, A_seq)

        # Inverse permutation: position in the sorted grid for each original
        # entry, then slice off the trailing M test entries.
        inv_order = jnp.argsort(order, stable=True)
        test_positions = inv_order[N:]
        m_test_state = m_smooth[test_positions]  # (M, d)
        P_test_state = P_smooth[test_positions]  # (M, d, d)
        means = (m_test_state @ H.T)[:, 0] + self.prior.mean(t_star)
        # var = H P H^T per test point — vmap over axis 0
        vars_ = jax.vmap(lambda P: (H @ P @ H.T)[0, 0])(P_test_state)
        if include_noise:
            vars_ = vars_ + self.prior._R(self.noise_var)
        return means, vars_

def markov_gp_factor(
    name: str,
    prior: MarkovGPPrior,
    y: Float[Array, " N"],
    noise_var: Float[Array, ""],
    *,
    mask: Bool[Array, " N"] | None = None,

    Computes ``log p(y | times, theta)`` via Kalman filtering and adds it as

    Gaussian-likelihood temporal GP regression — the latent function is
    marginalized analytically. With a mask, only the observed steps score,

    $$
    \log p(y \mid \theta)
      = \sum_k o_k \log \mathcal{N}(y_k;\, H \mu_k^-,\, H P_k^- H^\top + R).
    $$

    Args:
        name: The factor site name.
        prior: The `MarkovGPPrior` over the observation times.
        y: Observations of shape ``(N,)``; masked entries may be ``NaN``.
        noise_var: Observation noise variance.
