    Examples:
        One factor per site over padded ragged series:

        >>> import jax
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import numpyro
        >>> import numpyro.distributions as dist
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> t, y, mask = pss.pad_sites(
        ...     [jnp.arange(5.0), jnp.arange(3.0)], [jnp.ones(5), jnp.zeros(3)]
        ... )
        >>> def model():
        ...     with numpyro.plate("site", 2):
        ...         ell = numpyro.sample("lengthscale", dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0))
        ...     def site(ell_s, t_s, y_s, m_s):
        ...         prior = pss.MarkovGPPrior(pss.MaternSDE(1.0, ell_s, order=1), t_s)
        ...         return prior.log_marginal(y_s, jnp.asarray(0.1), mask=m_s)
        ...     numpyro.factor("y", jax.vmap(site)(ell, t, y, mask).sum())
    """
    numpyro.factor(name, prior.log_marginal(y, noise_var, mask=mask))

docs.title: markov_gp_sample(name: str, prior: MarkovGPPrior) -> Float[Array, ' N']
docs.text:
Sample a latent function f at the prior's training times.

Registers a single numpyro.sample(name, MVN(mu, K)) site where K is the dense Gram derived from the SDE autocovariance H exp(F|tau|) P_inf H^T. This is the simple, dense path: building K costs \(O(N^2 d^3)\) and every log-density evaluation an \(O(N^3)\) Cholesky, so use it when N is a few hundred at most and the kernel is stationary. For longer series, a non-stationary kernel, or NUTS over a non-Gaussian likelihood, use markov_gp_innovations_sample, which builds the same path from whitened innovations in \(O(N d^3)\).

Source code in packages/pyrox-ssm/src/pyrox_ssm/_markov.py 
def markov_gp_sample(
    name: str,
    prior: MarkovGPPrior,
) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
    """Sample a latent function ``f`` at the prior's training times.

    Registers a single ``numpyro.sample(name, MVN(mu, K))`` site where ``K``
    is the dense Gram derived from the SDE autocovariance
    ``H exp(F|tau|) P_inf H^T``. This is the simple, dense path: building
    ``K`` costs $O(N^2 d^3)$ and every log-density evaluation an $O(N^3)$
    Cholesky, so use it when ``N`` is a few hundred at most and the kernel
    is stationary. For longer series, a non-stationary kernel, or NUTS over
    a non-Gaussian likelihood, use `markov_gp_innovations_sample`, which
    builds the same path from whitened innovations in $O(N d^3)$.
    """
    K = _dense_sde_gram(prior.sde_kernel, prior.times)
    mu = prior.mean(prior.times)
    return numpyro.sample(  # ty: ignore[invalid-return-type]
        name, dist.MultivariateNormal(mu, covariance_matrix=K)
    )

docs.title: Latent paths from whitened innovations
docs.text:
When the latent path has to be sampled, as under a Bernoulli or Poisson likelihood with NUTS or SVI, markov_gp_sample builds the dense N × N Gram and pays an O(N^3) Cholesky per evaluation. markov_gp_innovations_sample samples standard normal innovations eps of shape (N, d) as the one site f"{name}_eps" instead and records the path f, built by markov_gp_from_innovations with a scan over the kernel's discretisation, as the deterministic site name. That costs O(N d^3), works for non-stationary kernels such as IntegratedWienerSDE, and is the whitened, non-centred parameterisation NUTS prefers. Keep markov_gp_sample for short series of a stationary kernel. The sqrt= option chooses the square roots of the process noise: "cholesky" (the default, with a small jitter) or "eigh", which also handles a process noise that is only positive semi-definite, as at closely spaced times.

import numpyro
import numpyro.distributions as dist
import pyrox_ssm as pss

def bernoulli_model(times, y):
    ell = numpyro.sample("lengthscale", dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0))
    prior = pss.MarkovGPPrior(pss.MaternSDE(1.0, ell, order=1), times)
    f = pss.markov_gp_innovations_sample("f", prior)               # (N,)
    numpyro.sample("y", dist.Bernoulli(logits=f), obs=y)

docs.title: markov_gp_from_innovations(prior: MarkovGPPrior, eps: Float[Array, '*batch N d'], *, sqrt: _SqrtMethod = 'cholesky', jitter: float = 1e-10) -> Float[Array, '*batch N']
docs.text:
Latent path of a Markov GP from whitened innovations, in linear time.

With \(\Delta t_k = t_k - t_{k-1}\) and \((A_k, Q_k)\) the kernel's discretisation over \(\Delta t_k\) (the time convention of MarkovGPPrior.as_lgssm), the state is run forward from standard normal innovations \(\varepsilon_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_d)\) by a jax.lax.scan,

\[ x_1 = L_0 \varepsilon_1, \qquad x_k = A_k x_{k-1} + L_{Q,k} \varepsilon_k \quad (k = 2, \dots, N), \qquad f(t_k) = H x_k + \mu(t_k), \]

where \(L_0 L_0^\top = P_0\) (MarkovGPPrior.initial_covariance, so \(P_\infty\) for a stationary kernel) and \(L_{Q,k} L_{Q,k}^\top = Q_k\). The map \(\varepsilon \mapsto f\) is linear, \(f = \mu + M \varepsilon\) with \(M M^\top = K\) the prior covariance of the path, so for a stationary kernel \(f\) has the law markov_gp_sample draws from. Time is \(O(N d^3)\) and memory \(O(N d^2)\): no \(N \times N\) array is formed, and a non-stationary kernel such as gaussx.IntegratedWienerSDE works as well as a stationary one.

Use it as a non-centred parameterisation of the latent path: sample eps and compute f deterministically, which is what NUTS prefers and what markov_gp_innovations_sample registers. markov_gp_sample's dense MultivariateNormal site stays the simpler choice for short series (a few hundred points) of a stationary kernel.

The square roots are taken by sqrt. \(Q_k\) is only positive semi-definite when \(\Delta t_k\) is small (it is computed as a difference, and its round-off can be slightly indefinite) and, for gaussx.IntegratedWienerSDE, close to singular whenever \(\Delta t_k\) is small.

  • "cholesky" (the default): gaussx.cholesky of \(\Sigma + \beta I\) with \(\beta\) = jitter, so each covariance is inflated by \(\beta I\). Cheapest; fine in float64 for the default \(\beta = 10^{-10}\) unless the round-off in \(Q_k\) exceeds \(\beta\) (large variances, very short lengthscales), when the factor turns NaN.
  • "eigh": the symmetric root \(Q \operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\max(\gamma, 0)}) Q^\top\) from gaussx.sqrt (a dense eigh with a Sylvester-equation derivative). It clips negative round-off, needs no jitter and is exact for a singular \(Q_k\), so it is the one that handles a \(Q_k\) that is only positive semi-definite, and the one to use in float32. jitter is ignored.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default prior MarkovGPPrior

The MarkovGPPrior over the \(N\) sorted times.

required eps Float[Array, '*batch N d']

Standard normal innovations of shape (*batch, N, d), one row per time, with \(d\) = prior.state_dim. Leading batch dimensions (a numpyro.plate, several paths) give one independent path each; the covariance roots are taken once and shared.

required sqrt _SqrtMethod

How the covariance square roots are taken, "cholesky" or "eigh".

'cholesky' jitter float

The diagonal \(\beta\) added before the Cholesky factor.

1e-10

Returns:

Type Description Float[Array, '*batch N']

The path \(f(t_1), \dots, f(t_N)\), shape (*batch, N), mean

Float[Array, '*batch N']

included.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the trailing shape of eps is not (N, d) or sqrt is unknown.

Examples:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import jax.random as jr
>>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
>>> times = jnp.linspace(0.0, 10.0, 500)
>>> prior = pss.MarkovGPPrior(pss.MaternSDE(1.0, 0.5, order=1), times)
>>> eps = jr.normal(jr.key(0), (500, prior.state_dim))
>>> f = pss.markov_gp_from_innovations(prior, eps)
>>> f.shape
(500,)
>>> eps_batch = jr.normal(jr.key(1), (8, 500, prior.state_dim))
>>> paths = pss.markov_gp_from_innovations(prior, eps_batch)
>>> paths.shape
(8, 500)

def markov_gp_from_innovations(
    prior: MarkovGPPrior,
    eps: Float[Array, "*batch N d"],
    *,
    sqrt: _SqrtMethod = "cholesky",
    jitter: float = 1e-10,
) -> Float[Array, "*batch N"]:
    r"""Latent path of a Markov GP from whitened innovations, in linear time.

    With $\Delta t_k = t_k - t_{k-1}$ and $(A_k, Q_k)$ the kernel's
    discretisation over $\Delta t_k$ (the time convention of
    `MarkovGPPrior.as_lgssm`), the state is run forward from standard
    normal innovations $\varepsilon_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_d)$ by a
    `jax.lax.scan`,

    $$
    x_1 = L_0 \varepsilon_1, \qquad
    x_k = A_k x_{k-1} + L_{Q,k} \varepsilon_k \quad (k = 2, \dots, N), \qquad
    f(t_k) = H x_k + \mu(t_k),
    $$

    where $L_0 L_0^\top = P_0$ (`MarkovGPPrior.initial_covariance`, so
    $P_\infty$ for a stationary kernel) and $L_{Q,k} L_{Q,k}^\top = Q_k$.
    The map $\varepsilon \mapsto f$ is linear, $f = \mu + M \varepsilon$
    with $M M^\top = K$ the prior covariance of the path, so for a
    stationary kernel $f$ has the law `markov_gp_sample` draws from. Time
    is $O(N d^3)$ and memory $O(N d^2)$: no $N \times N$ array is formed,
    and a non-stationary kernel such as `gaussx.IntegratedWienerSDE` works
    as well as a stationary one.

    Use it as a non-centred parameterisation of the latent path: sample
    ``eps`` and compute ``f`` deterministically, which is what NUTS prefers
    and what `markov_gp_innovations_sample` registers. `markov_gp_sample`'s
    dense ``MultivariateNormal`` site stays the simpler choice for short
    series (a few hundred points) of a stationary kernel.

    The square roots are taken by ``sqrt``. $Q_k$ is only positive
    *semi*-definite when $\Delta t_k$ is small (it is computed as a
    difference, and its round-off can be slightly indefinite) and, for
    `gaussx.IntegratedWienerSDE`, close to singular whenever $\Delta t_k$
    is small.

    * ``"cholesky"`` (the default): `gaussx.cholesky` of
      $\Sigma + \beta I$ with $\beta$ = ``jitter``, so each covariance is
      inflated by $\beta I$. Cheapest; fine in float64 for the default
      $\beta = 10^{-10}$ unless the round-off in $Q_k$ exceeds $\beta$
      (large variances, very short lengthscales), when the factor turns
      ``NaN``.
    * ``"eigh"``: the symmetric root
      $Q \operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\max(\gamma, 0)}) Q^\top$ from
      `gaussx.sqrt` (a dense ``eigh`` with a Sylvester-equation
      derivative). It clips negative round-off, needs no jitter and is
      exact for a singular $Q_k$, so it is the one that handles a $Q_k$
      that is only positive semi-definite, and the one to use in float32.
      ``jitter`` is ignored.

    Args:
        prior: The `MarkovGPPrior` over the $N$ sorted times.
        eps: Standard normal innovations of shape ``(*batch, N, d)``, one
            row per time, with $d$ = ``prior.state_dim``. Leading batch
            dimensions (a ``numpyro.plate``, several paths) give one
            independent path each; the covariance roots are taken once and
            shared.
        sqrt: How the covariance square roots are taken, ``"cholesky"`` or
            ``"eigh"``.
        jitter: The diagonal $\beta$ added before the Cholesky factor.

    Returns:
        The path $f(t_1), \dots, f(t_N)$, shape ``(*batch, N)``, mean
        included.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the trailing shape of ``eps`` is not ``(N, d)`` or
            ``sqrt`` is unknown.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import jax.random as jr
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> times = jnp.linspace(0.0, 10.0, 500)
        >>> prior = pss.MarkovGPPrior(pss.MaternSDE(1.0, 0.5, order=1), times)
        >>> eps = jr.normal(jr.key(0), (500, prior.state_dim))
        >>> f = pss.markov_gp_from_innovations(prior, eps)
        >>> f.shape
        (500,)
        >>> eps_batch = jr.normal(jr.key(1), (8, 500, prior.state_dim))
        >>> paths = pss.markov_gp_from_innovations(prior, eps_batch)
        >>> paths.shape
        (8, 500)
    """
    if sqrt not in _SQRT_METHODS:
        raise ValueError(f"sqrt must be one of {_SQRT_METHODS!r}, got {sqrt!r}")
    n, d = prior.times.shape[0], prior.state_dim
    eps = jnp.asarray(eps)
    if eps.ndim < 2 or eps.shape[-2:] != (n, d):
        raise ValueError(
            f"eps must have shape (*batch, {n}, {d}), one row of {d} "
            f"innovations per time for a state dimension of {d}, got "
            f"{tuple(eps.shape)!r}"
        )
    batch_shape = eps.shape[:-2]
    _F, _L, H, _Qc, _P_inf = prior.sde_kernel.sde_params()
    # The leading zero step gives A_1 = I, so starting from x_0 = 0 and
    # replacing Q_1 = 0 by P_0 makes the first step draw x_1 = L_0 eps_1.
    A_seq, Q_seq = prior.sde_kernel.discretise_sequence(_build_dt_full(prior.times))
    cov_seq = Q_seq.at[0].set(prior.initial_covariance())
    L_seq = jax.vmap(lambda cov: _covariance_root(cov, sqrt=sqrt, jitter=jitter))(
        cov_seq
    )

    def step(
        x_prev: Float[Array, " d"],
        inputs: tuple[Float[Array, "d d"], Float[Array, "d d"], Float[Array, " d"]],
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, " d"], Float[Array, " d"]]:
        A, L, e = inputs
        # xₖ = Aₖ xₖ₋₁ + L_{Q,k} εₖ
        x = einx.dot("i j, j -> i", A, x_prev) + einx.dot("i j, j -> i", L, e)
        return x, x

    x_init = jnp.zeros((d,), dtype=jnp.result_type(L_seq, eps))

    def path(e: Float[Array, "N d"]) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
        _, x_seq = jax.lax.scan(step, x_init, (A_seq, L_seq, e))
        # f(tₖ) = H xₖ
        return einx.dot("n d, o d -> n o", x_seq, H)[:, 0]

    # One scan per leading batch index, sharing A_seq and L_seq.
    f = jax.vmap(path)(eps.reshape((-1, n, d))).reshape((*batch_shape, n))
    # f(tₖ) += μ(tₖ)
    return f + prior.mean(prior.times)

docs.title: markov_gp_innovations_sample(name: str, prior: MarkovGPPrior, *, sqrt: _SqrtMethod = 'cholesky', jitter: float = 1e-10) -> Float[Array, ' N']
docs.text:
Sample a Markov-GP latent path through whitened innovations.

Registers the innovations as one sample site and the path, built from them by markov_gp_from_innovations, as a deterministic one,

\[ \varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_{N d}), \qquad f = \mu + M \varepsilon, \qquad M M^\top = K, \]

so the path costs \(O(N d^3)\) per model evaluation instead of the \(O(N^3)\) Cholesky of markov_gp_sample, and NUTS sees a whitened, non-centred parameterisation. Use it for long series, non-stationary kernels, and non-Gaussian likelihoods sampled with NUTS or fitted with SVI; keep markov_gp_sample for short series of a stationary kernel. The sqrt and jitter options are those of markov_gp_from_innovations; "eigh" handles a process noise \(Q_k\) that is only positive semi-definite (closely spaced times, gaussx.IntegratedWienerSDE).

It registers two sites, unscoped like markov_gp_sample's:

  • f"{name}_eps", the innovations: Normal(0, 1) of shape (N, d) with both dimensions in the event (.expand([N, d]).to_event(2));
  • name, a numpyro.deterministic holding the path of shape (N,), so numpyro.infer.Predictive returns it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str

The deterministic site's name; the innovations site is f"{name}_eps".

required prior MarkovGPPrior

The MarkovGPPrior over the \(N\) sorted times.

required sqrt _SqrtMethod

How the covariance square roots are taken, "cholesky" or "eigh".

'cholesky' jitter float

The diagonal added before the Cholesky factor.

1e-10

Returns:

Type Description Float[Array, ' N']

The path \(f(t_1), \dots, f(t_N)\), shape (N,), or

Float[Array, ' N']

(*batch, N) under enclosing numpyro.plate contexts, one

Float[Array, ' N']

independent path per plate index.

Examples:

A Bernoulli series with a latent Matérn-3/2 path:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import jax.random as jr
>>> import numpyro
>>> import numpyro.distributions as dist
>>> from numpyro.infer import MCMC, NUTS
>>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
>>> times = jnp.linspace(0.0, 10.0, 200)
>>> y = (jnp.sin(times) > 0).astype(jnp.int32)
>>> def model(times, y):
...     ell = numpyro.sample("lengthscale", dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0))
...     sde = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=ell, order=1)
...     f = pss.markov_gp_innovations_sample("f", pss.MarkovGPPrior(sde, times))
...     numpyro.sample("y", dist.Bernoulli(logits=f), obs=y)
>>> mcmc = MCMC(
...     NUTS(model), num_warmup=100, num_samples=100, progress_bar=False
... )
>>> mcmc.run(jr.key(0), times, y)
>>> mcmc.get_samples()["f"].shape
(100, 200)

def markov_gp_innovations_sample(
    name: str,
    prior: MarkovGPPrior,
    *,
    sqrt: _SqrtMethod = "cholesky",
    jitter: float = 1e-10,
) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
    r"""Sample a Markov-GP latent path through whitened innovations.

    Registers the innovations as one sample site and the path, built from
    them by `markov_gp_from_innovations`, as a deterministic one,

    $$
    \varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_{N d}), \qquad
    f = \mu + M \varepsilon, \qquad M M^\top = K,
    $$

    so the path costs $O(N d^3)$ per model evaluation instead of the
    $O(N^3)$ Cholesky of `markov_gp_sample`, and NUTS sees a whitened,
    non-centred parameterisation. Use it for long series, non-stationary
    kernels, and non-Gaussian likelihoods sampled with NUTS or fitted with
    SVI; keep `markov_gp_sample` for short series of a stationary kernel.
    The ``sqrt`` and ``jitter`` options are those of
    `markov_gp_from_innovations`; ``"eigh"`` handles a process noise $Q_k$
    that is only positive semi-definite (closely spaced times,
    `gaussx.IntegratedWienerSDE`).

    It registers two sites, unscoped like `markov_gp_sample`'s:

    * ``f"{name}_eps"``, the innovations: ``Normal(0, 1)`` of shape
      ``(N, d)`` with both dimensions in the event
      (``.expand([N, d]).to_event(2)``);
    * ``name``, a ``numpyro.deterministic`` holding the path of shape
      ``(N,)``, so `numpyro.infer.Predictive` returns it.

    Args:
        name: The deterministic site's name; the innovations site is
            ``f"{name}_eps"``.
        prior: The `MarkovGPPrior` over the $N$ sorted times.
        sqrt: How the covariance square roots are taken, ``"cholesky"`` or
            ``"eigh"``.
        jitter: The diagonal added before the Cholesky factor.

    Returns:
        The path $f(t_1), \dots, f(t_N)$, shape ``(N,)``, or
        ``(*batch, N)`` under enclosing ``numpyro.plate`` contexts, one
        independent path per plate index.

    Examples:
        A Bernoulli series with a latent Matérn-3/2 path:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import jax.random as jr
        >>> import numpyro
        >>> import numpyro.distributions as dist
        >>> from numpyro.infer import MCMC, NUTS
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> times = jnp.linspace(0.0, 10.0, 200)
        >>> y = (jnp.sin(times) > 0).astype(jnp.int32)
        >>> def model(times, y):
        ...     ell = numpyro.sample("lengthscale", dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0))
        ...     sde = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=ell, order=1)
        ...     f = pss.markov_gp_innovations_sample("f", pss.MarkovGPPrior(sde, times))
        ...     numpyro.sample("y", dist.Bernoulli(logits=f), obs=y)
        >>> mcmc = MCMC(
        ...     NUTS(model), num_warmup=100, num_samples=100, progress_bar=False
        ... )
        >>> mcmc.run(jr.key(0), times, y)
        >>> mcmc.get_samples()["f"].shape
        (100, 200)
    """
    n, d = prior.times.shape[0], prior.state_dim
    zero = jnp.zeros((), dtype=prior.times.dtype)
    eps = numpyro.sample(
        f"{name}_eps", dist.Normal(zero, 1.0).expand([n, d]).to_event(2)
    )
    # Enclosing plates prepend batch dimensions to eps; the path keeps them.
    f = markov_gp_from_innovations(prior, jnp.asarray(eps), sqrt=sqrt, jitter=jitter)
    return numpyro.deterministic(name, f)  # ty: ignore[invalid-return-type]

docs.title: Ragged sites
docs.text:
Every method that reads observations (filter, smooth, log_marginal, condition, condition_nongauss, markov_gp_factor, each non-Gaussian strategy's fit, sparse_markov_elbo and sparse_markov_factor) takes an optional boolean mask= of the observations' shape. A masked step runs the Kalman predict only, so it adds nothing to the log marginal, and its observation is replaced before any arithmetic, so a NaN placeholder there reaches neither the value nor the gradient. mask=None is the unmasked result, bit for bit.

Sites observed on different days become one vmapped factor with pad_sites, which pads each series after its last observation (at its median spacing, so the padded times stay strictly increasing) and returns the mask. Padding after the last observation adds predict-only steps, so each site's log marginal is unchanged:

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro
import numpyro.distributions as dist
import pyrox_ssm as pss

t, y, mask = pss.pad_sites(times_per_site, y_per_site)           # (S, N) each

def site_log_marginal(ell_s, t_s, y_s, m_s):
    sde = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=ell_s, order=1)
    return pss.MarkovGPPrior(sde, t_s).log_marginal(y_s, jnp.asarray(0.01), mask=m_s)

def pooled_model(t, y, mask):
    mu = numpyro.sample("mu", dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0))
    with numpyro.plate("site", t.shape[0]):
        ell = numpyro.sample("lengthscale", dist.LogNormal(mu, 0.5))  # (S,)
    numpyro.factor("y", jax.vmap(site_log_marginal)(ell, t, y, mask).sum())

markov_gp_sites_factor writes that factor in one call. It takes one kernel whose array leaves carry the leading site axis (a scalar leaf is shared by every site), the (S, N) arrays from pad_sites, and a shared or per-site noise variance:

def pooled_model(t, y, mask):
    mu = numpyro.sample("mu", dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0))
    with numpyro.plate("site", t.shape[0]):
        ell = numpyro.sample("lengthscale", dist.LogNormal(mu, 0.5))  # (S,)
    kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=ell, order=1)
    pss.markov_gp_sites_factor("y", kernel, t, y, jnp.asarray(0.01), mask=mask)

Per-site hyperparameters drawn around a population value with an unknown spread give NUTS a funnel when the spread is small. noncentred_log_normal samples a standard normal f"{name}_z" per site under the plate and records exp(loc + scale * z) as the deterministic site name:

with numpyro.plate("site", t.shape[0]):
    ell = pss.noncentred_log_normal("lengthscale", ell_loc, ell_scale)  # (S,)

docs.title: pad_sites(times: Sequence[Float[Array, ' N_s']], ys: Sequence[Float[Array, ' N_s']], *, masks: Sequence[Bool[Array, ' N_s']] | None = None, length: int | None = None) -> tuple[Float[Array, 'S N'], Float[Array, 'S N'], Bool[Array, 'S N']]
docs.text:
Pad ragged site series to (S, N) with strictly increasing padded times.

Site \(s\) with \(N_s\) observations at times \(t_1 < \dots < t_{N_s}\) is extended to length \(N\) by stepping on from its last observation at its median spacing,

\[ t_{N_s + j} = t_{N_s} + j\, \delta_s, \qquad \delta_s = \operatorname{median}(\operatorname{diff}(t_s)), \qquad j = 1, \dots, N - N_s, \]

with \(\delta_s = 1\) for a site with one observation. The padded steps are masked, and a masked step runs the Kalman predict only,

\[ \mu_k^+ = \mu_k^-, \qquad P_k^+ = P_k^-, \]

def pad_sites(
    times: Sequence[Float[Array, " N_s"]],
    ys: Sequence[Float[Array, " N_s"]],
    *,
    masks: Sequence[Bool[Array, " N_s"]] | None = None,
    length: int | None = None,
) -> tuple[Float[Array, "S N"], Float[Array, "S N"], Bool[Array, "S N"]]:
    r"""Pad ragged site series to ``(S, N)`` with strictly increasing padded times.

    Site $s$ with $N_s$ observations at times $t_1 < \dots < t_{N_s}$ is
    extended to length $N$ by stepping on from its last observation at its
    median spacing,

    $$
    t_{N_s + j} = t_{N_s} + j\, \delta_s, \qquad
    \delta_s = \operatorname{median}(\operatorname{diff}(t_s)), \qquad
    j = 1, \dots, N - N_s,
    $$

    with $\delta_s = 1$ for a site with one observation. The padded steps
    are masked, and a masked step runs the Kalman predict only,

    $$
    \mu_k^+ = \mu_k^-, \qquad P_k^+ = P_k^-,
    $$

    so it adds nothing to the log marginal: padding after the last
    observation changes no site's log marginal or smoothed moments at its
    observed steps. The padded times stay strictly increasing, so the
    monotonicity check and the kernel discretisation are unchanged. Padded
    entries of ``y`` are zero.

    Missing steps inside a record are masked the same way, so a record on a
    regular grid with gaps can be passed as it is: a step is masked where
    ``masks`` is ``False`` or, by default, where ``y`` is ``NaN``. A masked
    step runs the predict step only, as a padded one does, so the site's log
    marginal equals that of the same site with those steps dropped. Masked
    entries of ``y`` are zero, as padded ones are.

    Args:
        times: One strictly increasing ``(N_s,)`` array of observation times
            per site.
        ys: One ``(N_s,)`` array of observations per site, matching
            ``times``. ``NaN`` marks a missing step when ``masks`` is not
            given.
        masks: Optional ``(N_s,)`` boolean array per site, ``True`` where the
            step is observed. Defaults to ``~jnp.isnan(y)`` per site.
        length: Padded length $N$. Defaults to the longest site,
            $\max_s N_s$.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(t, y, mask)``, each of shape ``(S, N)``: the padded times,
        the padded observations and a boolean mask that is ``True`` at each
        row's observed steps: its first $N_s$ steps less any masked ones.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no site is given, if ``times``, ``ys`` and ``masks``
            differ in length or shape, if a site is not a non-empty 1-D series, if a
            site's (concrete) times are not strictly increasing, or if
            ``length`` is shorter than the longest site.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> times = [jnp.array([0.0, 1.0, 3.0]), jnp.array([0.5, 1.0])]
        >>> ys = [jnp.array([0.2, 0.1, -0.3]), jnp.array([1.0, 0.8])]
        >>> t, y, mask = pss.pad_sites(times, ys)
        >>> t.tolist()
        [[0.0, 1.0, 3.0], [0.5, 1.0, 1.5]]
        >>> mask.tolist()
        [[True, True, True], [True, True, False]]
        >>> def site_log_marginal(t_s, y_s, m_s):
        ...     prior = pss.MarkovGPPrior(pss.MaternSDE(1.0, 1.0, order=1), t_s)
        ...     return prior.log_marginal(y_s, jnp.asarray(0.1), mask=m_s)
        >>> jax.vmap(site_log_marginal)(t, y, mask).shape
        (2,)
    """
    if len(times) != len(ys):
        raise ValueError(
            f"times has {len(times)} sites but ys has {len(ys)}; pass one "
            "series of each per site."
        )
    if len(times) == 0:
        raise ValueError("pad_sites needs at least one site.")
    if masks is not None and len(masks) != len(times):
        raise ValueError(
            f"masks has {len(masks)} sites but times has {len(times)}; pass "
            "one mask per site."
        )
    t_dtype = jnp.result_type(*times, 0.0)
    y_dtype = jnp.result_type(*ys)
    sites = []
    site_masks = [None] * len(times) if masks is None else list(masks)
    for s, (t_s, y_s, m_s) in enumerate(zip(times, ys, site_masks, strict=True)):
        t_s = jnp.asarray(t_s, dtype=t_dtype)
        y_s = jnp.asarray(y_s, dtype=y_dtype)
        if t_s.ndim != 1 or t_s.shape[0] == 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"site {s}: times must be a non-empty 1-D series, got shape "
                f"{tuple(t_s.shape)!r}."
            )
        if y_s.shape != t_s.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"site {s}: ys has shape {tuple(y_s.shape)!r} but times has "
                f"{tuple(t_s.shape)!r}; each observation needs one time."
            )
        m_s = ~jnp.isnan(y_s) if m_s is None else jnp.asarray(m_s, dtype=bool)
        if m_s.shape != t_s.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"site {s}: masks has shape {tuple(m_s.shape)!r} but times has "
                f"{tuple(t_s.shape)!r}; pass one flag per observation."
            )
        if t_s.shape[0] >= 2:
            # Concrete times only; a tracer cannot be checked and is trusted,
            # as in MarkovGPPrior.
            try:
                if not bool(jnp.all(jnp.diff(t_s) > 0)):
                    raise ValueError(f"site {s}: times must be strictly increasing.")
            except jax.errors.TracerBoolConversionError:
                pass
        sites.append((t_s, jnp.where(m_s, y_s, 0), m_s))

    longest = max(t_s.shape[0] for t_s, _, _ in sites)
    n = longest if length is None else int(length)
    if n < longest:
        raise ValueError(
            f"length={n} is shorter than the longest site ({longest} "
            "observations); padding cannot drop observations."
        )

    t_rows, y_rows, mask_rows = [], [], []
    for t_s, y_s, m_s in sites:
        n_s = t_s.shape[0]
        # δₛ = median(diff(tₛ)), one time unit for a single observation
        step = jnp.median(jnp.diff(t_s)) if n_s >= 2 else jnp.ones((), dtype=t_dtype)
        # t_{Nₛ + j} = t_{Nₛ} + j δₛ,  j = 1, …, N − Nₛ
        padded_times = t_s[-1] + step * jnp.arange(1, n - n_s + 1, dtype=t_dtype)
        t_rows.append(jnp.concatenate([t_s, padded_times]))
        y_rows.append(jnp.concatenate([y_s, jnp.zeros(n - n_s, dtype=y_dtype)]))
        mask_rows.append(jnp.concatenate([m_s, jnp.zeros(n - n_s, dtype=bool)]))
    return jnp.stack(t_rows), jnp.stack(y_rows), jnp.stack(mask_rows)

...     kernel = pss.MaternSDE(1.0, ell, order=1)

def markov_gp_sites_factor(
    name: str,
    sde_kernel: SDEKernel,
    times: Float[Array, "S N"],
    y: Float[Array, "S N"],
    noise_var: Float[Array, ""] | Float[Array, " S"],
    *,
    mask: Bool[Array, "S N"] | None = None,
    mean_fn: Callable[[Float[Array, " N"]], Float[Array, " N"]] | None = None,
    obs_noise_floor: float = 0.0,
) -> None:
    r"""Register the summed Markov-GP log marginal of ``S`` sites as one factor.

    The multi-site form of `markov_gp_factor`, for the ``(S, N)`` padded
    times, observations and mask that `pyrox_ssm.pad_sites` returns. Site
    $s$ has its own kernel $\theta_s$ and noise variance $\sigma_s^2$, and the
    sites are independent given them, so the factor is

    $$
    \log p(Y \mid \theta) = \sum_{s=1}^{S} \log p(y_s \mid \theta_s, \sigma_s^2),
    $$

    each term the masked Kalman log marginal of `MarkovGPPrior.log_marginal`.
    It replaces the hand-written ``jax.vmap`` over sites shown in
    `markov_gp_factor`'s example, and is one ``numpyro.factor`` site, so it
    composes with NUTS and SVI as that pattern does.

    One kernel per site is one kernel whose array leaves carry a leading
    ``(S,)`` axis, such as ``MaternSDE(variance, lengthscale, order=1)`` with
    ``(S,)`` arrays sampled under a ``numpyro.plate`` over sites. A 0-d leaf
    (a Python float or a scalar array) is shared by every site.

    Args:
        name: The factor site name.
        sde_kernel: An `SDEKernel` whose non-scalar array leaves have a
            leading site axis of length ``S``.
        times: ``(S, N)`` strictly increasing times per row.
        y: ``(S, N)`` observations; masked entries may be ``NaN``.
        noise_var: Observation noise variance, shared ``()`` or per site
            ``(S,)``.
        mask: Optional ``(S, N)`` boolean mask, ``True`` where observed.
        mean_fn: Optional mean function shared by every site, as in
            `MarkovGPPrior`.
        obs_noise_floor: Extra observation variance, as in `MarkovGPPrior`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``times``, ``y`` or ``mask`` is not ``(S, N)``, or if a
            non-scalar kernel leaf or ``noise_var`` has a leading axis whose
            length is not ``S``.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import numpyro
        >>> import numpyro.distributions as dist
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> t, y, mask = pss.pad_sites(
        ...     [jnp.arange(5.0), jnp.arange(3.0)], [jnp.ones(5), jnp.zeros(3)]
        ... )
        >>> def model():
        ...     with numpyro.plate("site", 2):
        ...         ell = numpyro.sample("lengthscale", dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0))
        ...     kernel = pss.MaternSDE(1.0, ell, order=1)
        ...     noise = jnp.asarray(0.1)
        ...     pss.markov_gp_sites_factor("y", kernel, t, y, noise, mask=mask)
    """
    times = jnp.asarray(times)
    if times.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"times must be (S, N), one row per site, got shape {tuple(times.shape)!r}."
        )
    n_sites = times.shape[0]
    y = jnp.asarray(y)
    if y.shape != times.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"y has shape {tuple(y.shape)!r} but times has {tuple(times.shape)!r}."
        )
    if mask is not None and jnp.shape(mask) != times.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"mask has shape {tuple(jnp.shape(mask))!r} but times has "
            f"{tuple(times.shape)!r}."
        )

    kernel_axes = _site_axes(sde_kernel, n_sites)
    noise_var = jnp.asarray(noise_var)
    if noise_var.ndim not in (0, 1) or (
        noise_var.ndim == 1 and noise_var.shape[0] != n_sites
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"noise_var must be () or (S,)=({n_sites},), got shape "
            f"{tuple(noise_var.shape)!r}."
        )
    noise_axis = None if noise_var.ndim == 0 else 0

    def _site(
        kernel_s: SDEKernel,
        t_s: Float[Array, " N"],
        y_s: Float[Array, " N"],
        m_s: Bool[Array, " N"] | None,
        noise_s: Float[Array, ""],
    ) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        prior = MarkovGPPrior(
            kernel_s, t_s, mean_fn=mean_fn, obs_noise_floor=obs_noise_floor
        )
        return prior.log_marginal(y_s, noise_s, mask=m_s)

    mask_axis = None if mask is None else 0
    log_marginals = jax.vmap(_site, in_axes=(kernel_axes, 0, 0, mask_axis, noise_axis))(
        sde_kernel, times, y, mask, noise_var
    )
    numpyro.factor(name, jnp.sum(log_marginals))

docs.title: noncentred_log_normal(name: str, loc: Float[Array, ' *batch'] | float, scale: Float[Array, ' *batch'] | float) -> Float[Array, ' *batch']
docs.text:
A positive per-site parameter around a population value, non-centred.

Site \(n\)'s parameter \(\theta_n\) (a lengthscale, a variance) is log-normal around a population log-mean \(m\) with spread \(\tau\),

\[ \log \theta_n = m + \tau z_n, \qquad z_n \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1), \]

which has the distribution of the centred form \(\log \theta_n \sim \mathcal{N}(m, \tau^2)\). The sampler sees \(z_n\), which is independent of \(\tau\) a priori, instead of \(\log \theta_n\), whose spread shrinks with \(\tau\). That removes the funnel NUTS meets when \(\tau\) is small, the usual case for sites that differ little. NumPyro's LocScaleReparam(centered=0) does the same rewrite on a centred Normal site through a reparam handler; this helper writes it out and names its sites predictably.

Call it inside the numpyro.plate over sites, so there is one \(z_n\) per site; loc and scale broadcast against the plate.

Registers the sample site f"{name}_z" (standard normal) and the deterministic site name (\(\theta_n\), so its posterior is in the trace).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str

Name of the deterministic site; the sample site is f"{name}_z".

required loc Float[Array, ' *batch'] | float

Population log-mean \(m\).

required scale Float[Array, ' *batch'] | float

Population log-spread \(\tau > 0\).

required

Returns:

Type Description Float[Array, ' *batch']

\(\theta_n = \exp(m + \tau z_n)\), shaped by the enclosing plates.

Examples:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import numpyro
>>> import numpyro.distributions as dist
>>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
>>> t, y, mask = pss.pad_sites(
...     [jnp.arange(5.0), jnp.arange(3.0)], [jnp.ones(5), jnp.zeros(3)]
... )
>>> def model():
...     loc = numpyro.sample("lengthscale_loc", dist.Normal(jnp.log(7.0), 1.0))
...     scale = numpyro.sample("lengthscale_scale", dist.HalfNormal(0.5))
...     with numpyro.plate("site", 2):
...         ell = pss.noncentred_log_normal("lengthscale", loc, scale)
...     kernel = pss.MaternSDE(1.0, ell, order=1)
...     noise = jnp.asarray(0.1)
...     pss.markov_gp_sites_factor("y", kernel, t, y, noise, mask=mask)

def noncentred_log_normal(
    name: str,
    loc: Float[Array, " *batch"] | float,
    scale: Float[Array, " *batch"] | float,
) -> Float[Array, " *batch"]:
    r"""A positive per-site parameter around a population value, non-centred.

    Site $n$'s parameter $\theta_n$ (a lengthscale, a variance) is log-normal
    around a population log-mean $m$ with spread $\tau$,

    $$
    \log \theta_n = m + \tau z_n, \qquad z_n \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1),
    $$

    which has the distribution of the centred form
    $\log \theta_n \sim \mathcal{N}(m, \tau^2)$. The sampler sees $z_n$, which
    is independent of $\tau$ a priori, instead of $\log \theta_n$, whose
    spread shrinks with $\tau$. That removes the funnel NUTS meets when $\tau$
    is small, the usual case for sites that differ little. NumPyro's
    ``LocScaleReparam(centered=0)`` does the same rewrite on a centred
    ``Normal`` site through a reparam handler; this helper writes it out and
    names its sites predictably.

    Call it inside the ``numpyro.plate`` over sites, so there is one $z_n$ per
    site; ``loc`` and ``scale`` broadcast against the plate.

    Registers the sample site ``f"{name}_z"`` (standard normal) and the
    deterministic site ``name`` ($\theta_n$, so its posterior is in the
    trace).

    Args:
        name: Name of the deterministic site; the sample site is
            ``f"{name}_z"``.
        loc: Population log-mean $m$.
        scale: Population log-spread $\tau > 0$.

    Returns:
        $\theta_n = \exp(m + \tau z_n)$, shaped by the enclosing plates.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import numpyro
        >>> import numpyro.distributions as dist
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> t, y, mask = pss.pad_sites(
        ...     [jnp.arange(5.0), jnp.arange(3.0)], [jnp.ones(5), jnp.zeros(3)]
        ... )
        >>> def model():
        ...     loc = numpyro.sample("lengthscale_loc", dist.Normal(jnp.log(7.0), 1.0))
        ...     scale = numpyro.sample("lengthscale_scale", dist.HalfNormal(0.5))
        ...     with numpyro.plate("site", 2):
        ...         ell = pss.noncentred_log_normal("lengthscale", loc, scale)
        ...     kernel = pss.MaternSDE(1.0, ell, order=1)
        ...     noise = jnp.asarray(0.1)
        ...     pss.markov_gp_sites_factor("y", kernel, t, y, noise, mask=mask)
    """
    z = numpyro.sample(f"{name}_z", dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0))
    # log θ_n = m + τ z_n
    log_value = jnp.asarray(loc) + jnp.asarray(scale) * z
    return numpyro.deterministic(  # ty: ignore[invalid-return-type]
        name, jnp.exp(log_value)
    )

docs.title: A shared GP plus one GP per site
docs.text:
When the sites share a regional signal, y_s(t) = g(t) + h_s(t) + eps_s(t) with one shared GP g and an independent GP h_s per site is one linear-Gaussian SSM on the merged grid of all site times: SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP.from_sites merges the ragged series (NaN and a (T, S) mask where a site was not observed), as_lgssm builds the block-diagonal transitions and the observation rows H[s] = (H_g, 0, …, H_h at block s, …, 0), log_marginal is the exact log marginal of the observed pairs and decompose splits the smoothed means into E[g | y] and E[h_s | y]. The site kernel's hyperparameters are pooled (scalar leaves) or per site (leaves with a leading axis of length S), and each pass costs O(T D^3) with D = d_g + S d_h, so it suits a few dozen sites:

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro
import numpyro.distributions as dist
import pyrox_ssm as pss

shared = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=30.0, order=1)
site = pss.MaternSDE(variance=jnp.full(S, 0.3), lengthscale=5.0, order=1)  # per-site variance
model, y_grid = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP.from_sites(shared, site, times_per_site, y_per_site)

def regional_model(y_grid):
    noise_var = numpyro.sample("noise_var", dist.LogNormal(-3.0, 1.0))
    numpyro.factor("y", model.log_marginal(y_grid, noise_var))

g_mean, h_mean = model.decompose(y_grid, jnp.asarray(0.05))         # (T,), (T, S)

decompose(..., return_var=True) also returns the marginal variances V[g | y] and V[h_s | y] from the same smoother pass. The two parts are correlated a posteriori, so their variances do not add to that of g + h_s. A known per-site mean, such as a station climatology, goes in as mean_fn, a callable from the (T,) grid to (T, S) means. It is the observation offset of as_lgssm, so the model fits raw readings and its log marginal equals that of the anomalies y - mean. A ConstantSDE term in the site kernel instead integrates an unknown level out.

To predict at times no site observed, such as a gap or a forecast, condition once and call predict, which adds the test times to the grid as unobserved rows:

cond = model.condition(y_grid, jnp.asarray(0.05))
g_mean, h_mean, g_var, h_var = cond.predict(t_star)                   # (M,), (M, S), (M,), (M, S)

from_sites takes the union of the site times with jnp.unique, so it needs concrete times. Inside jax.jit or a NumPyro model under NUTS, build the grid and mask once outside and construct the model with SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP(shared, site, times, mask) from the sampled kernels.

Bases: Module

A shared GP plus one independent GP per site, on a merged time grid.

Site \(s = 1, \dots, S\) is observed on its own days as

\[ y_s(t) = \mu_s(t) + g(t) + h_s(t) + \varepsilon_s(t), \qquad g \sim \mathcal{GP}(0, k_g), \quad h_s \sim \mathcal{GP}(0, k_{h,s}), \quad \varepsilon_s(t) \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_{n,s}^2), \]

with \(g\), \(h_1, \dots, h_S\) independent and \(\mu_s\) an optional known per-site mean (mean_fn, zero by default). Every kernel is an SDE kernel with state \(x_g \in \mathbb{R}^{d_g}\) or \(x_{h,s} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h}\), and the joint state on the merged grid \(t_1 < \dots < t_T\) stacks them,

\[ x = (x_g, x_{h,1}, \dots, x_{h,S}) \in \mathbb{R}^{D}, \qquad D = d_g + S\, d_h . \]

as_lgssm returns that model as a pyrox_ssm.LinearGaussianSSMPrior with block-diagonal transitions, process noise and initial covariance,

\[ A_k = \mathrm{blockdiag}(A_k^{(g)}, A_k^{(h,1)}, \dots, A_k^{(h,S)}), \qquad Q_k \text{ likewise}, \qquad P_0 = \mathrm{blockdiag}(P_0^{(g)}, P_0^{(h,1)}, \dots, P_0^{(h,S)}), \]

observation rows \(H[s] = (H_g, 0, \dots, H_h \text{ at block } s, \dots, 0)\) and \(R = \mathrm{diag}(\sigma_{n,1}^2, \dots, \sigma_{n,S}^2)\). mask[k, s] says whether site \(s\) was observed at \(t_k\); an unobserved entry is marginalised out exactly, so the log marginal is that of the observed \((t, s)\) pairs under the dense Gaussian with covariance \(K = K_g \otimes \mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top + \mathrm{blockdiag}_s(K_{h,s}) + \mathrm{diag}(\sigma_{n,s}^2)\).

The site kernel's array leaves are either scalars, shared by every site (pooled hyperparameters), or carry a leading axis of length \(S\) (per-site hyperparameters); the two may be mixed, for example a per-site variance with a pooled lengthscale. \(S\) is mask.shape[1]. Each site's discretisation runs once, under jax.vmap over the batched leaves, or once in total when every leaf is pooled.

Cost: each filter or smoother pass is \(O(T D^3)\), cubic in the number of sites. Beyond a few dozen sites \(D^3\) dominates. Two cheaper routes exist: gaussx's meanfield_kalman_filter and meanfield_rts_smoother run independent filters on the diagonal state blocks at \(O(T L d^3)\) for \(L\) blocks of size \(d\), dropping every cross-block covariance; that projection is exact only when the blocks do not couple, and here every site couples \(g\) to \(h_s\) through the observation, so it is an approximation that ignores the posterior correlation between the shared and the site parts. An ensemble Kalman filter (filterax) keeps that correlation at the price of Monte Carlo error in the covariances.

The per-site mean \(\mu_s(t)\) (a station climatology, an offset) enters as_lgssm as the observation offset, so it shifts the observations and leaves every covariance unchanged: the log marginal is that of the anomalies \(y - \mu\), and gradients flow to whatever parameters mean_fn closes over. That is a fixed shift, given its parameters; a pyrox_ssm.ConstantSDE term in the site kernel instead integrates an unknown level out.

To predict at times no site observed (a gap, a forecast), condition once and call predict: model.condition(y, noise_var).predict(t_star) adds the test times to the grid as unobserved rows. from_sites takes the union of the site times with jnp.unique, so it needs concrete times and runs outside jax.jit. A model rebuilt from sampled kernels inside jax.jit or a NumPyro model under NUTS uses the constructor with a grid and mask computed once outside, for example the times and mask of one from_sites call made before sampling.

The model registers no NumPyro sites; wrap log_marginal in numpyro.factor (or pass as_lgssm to pyrox_ssm.lgssm_factor). Shapes are checked at construction, and concrete times must be strictly increasing (a traced times is trusted, as in pyrox_ssm.MarkovGPPrior).

    \varepsilon_s(t) \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_{n,s}^2),

    A_k = \mathrm{blockdiag}(A_k^{(g)}, A_k^{(h,1)}, \dots, A_k^{(h,S)}),
    \qquad Q_k \text{ likewise}, \qquad
    P_0 = \mathrm{blockdiag}(P_0^{(g)}, P_0^{(h,1)}, \dots, P_0^{(h,S)}),

    \sigma_{n,S}^2)$. ``mask[k, s]`` says whether site $s$ was observed at

    marginal is that of the observed $(t, s)$ pairs under the dense
    Gaussian with covariance $K = K_g \otimes \mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top +

    The site kernel's array leaves are either scalars, shared by every site

    (per-site hyperparameters); the two may be mixed, for example a
    per-site variance with a pooled lengthscale. $S$ is ``mask.shape[1]``.
    Each site's discretisation runs once, under `jax.vmap` over the
    batched leaves, or once in total when every leaf is pooled.

    of sites. Beyond a few dozen sites $D^3$ dominates. Two cheaper routes
    exist: gaussx's ``meanfield_kalman_filter`` and
    ``meanfield_rts_smoother`` run independent filters on the diagonal
    state blocks at $O(T L d^3)$ for $L$ blocks of size $d$, dropping every

    do not couple, and here every site couples $g$ to $h_s$ through the
    observation, so it is an approximation that ignores the posterior
    correlation between the shared and the site parts. An ensemble Kalman
    filter (filterax) keeps that correlation at the price of Monte Carlo
    error in the covariances.

    The per-site mean $\mu_s(t)$ (a station climatology, an offset) enters
    `as_lgssm` as the observation offset, so it shifts the observations and
    leaves every covariance unchanged: the log marginal is that of the

    `pyrox_ssm.ConstantSDE` term in the site kernel instead integrates an

    and call ``predict``: ``model.condition(y, noise_var).predict(t_star)``

    times and runs outside `jax.jit`. A model rebuilt from sampled kernels
    inside `jax.jit` or a NumPyro model under NUTS uses the constructor with

    ``numpyro.factor`` (or pass `as_lgssm` to `pyrox_ssm.lgssm_factor`).
    Shapes are checked at construction, and concrete ``times`` must be
    strictly increasing (a traced ``times`` is trusted, as in
    `pyrox_ssm.MarkovGPPrior`).

    Attributes:
        shared: The SDE kernel $k_g$ of the shared GP.
        site: The SDE kernel $k_h$ of the site GPs; each array leaf is a
            scalar (pooled) or has a leading axis of length $S$ (per site).
        times: Merged, strictly increasing grid, shaped ``(T,)``.
        mask: Boolean ``(T, S)`` mask, ``True`` where site $s$ was observed
            at ``times[k]``.
        mean_fn: Optional callable mapping times ``(T,)`` to the per-site
            means $\mu_s(t_k)$, ``(T, S)``. ``None`` (the default) is the
            zero mean.

    Examples:
        Three sites on ragged days, a per-site variance and a pooled
        lengthscale:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import numpyro
        >>> import numpyro.distributions as dist
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> t_per_site = [jnp.array([0.0, 1.0, 3.0]), jnp.array([1.0, 2.0]),
        ...               jnp.array([0.0, 2.0, 3.0])]
        >>> y_per_site = [jnp.array([0.2, 0.1, -0.3]), jnp.array([0.4, 0.0]),
        ...               jnp.array([0.1, -0.2, 0.3])]
        >>> shared = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=2.0, order=1)
        >>> site = pss.MaternSDE(variance=jnp.array([0.3, 0.5, 0.2]),
        ...                      lengthscale=0.5, order=1)
        >>> model, y_grid = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP.from_sites(
        ...     shared, site, t_per_site, y_per_site
        ... )
        >>> y_grid.shape, model.state_dim
        ((4, 3), 8)
        >>> log_marg = model.log_marginal(y_grid, jnp.asarray(0.01))
        >>> g_mean, h_mean = model.decompose(y_grid, jnp.asarray(0.01))
        >>> g_mean.shape, h_mean.shape
        ((4,), (4, 3))

        Inside a NumPyro model, the log marginal is a factor:

        >>> def numpyro_model(y_grid):
        ...     noise_var = numpyro.sample("noise_var", dist.LogNormal(-3.0, 1.0))
        ...     numpyro.factor("y", model.log_marginal(y_grid, noise_var))
    """

    shared: SDEKernel
    site: SDEKernel
    times: Float[Array, " T"]
    mask: Bool[Array, "T S"]
    mean_fn: Callable[[Float[Array, " T"]], Float[Array, "T S"]] | None = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        shared: SDEKernel,
        site: SDEKernel,
        times: Float[Array, " T"],
        mask: Bool[Array, "T S"],
        mean_fn: Callable[[Float[Array, " T"]], Float[Array, "T S"]] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        times_arr = jnp.asarray(times, dtype=jnp.result_type(times, 0.0))
        if times_arr.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"times must be 1-D, got shape {tuple(times_arr.shape)!r}")
        if times_arr.shape[0] >= 2:
            # Concrete times only; a tracer cannot be checked and is trusted.
            try:
                if not bool(jnp.all(jnp.diff(times_arr) > 0)):
                    raise ValueError("times must be strictly increasing")
            except jax.errors.TracerBoolConversionError:
                pass
        mask_arr = jnp.asarray(mask).astype(bool)
        if mask_arr.ndim != 2 or mask_arr.shape[0] != times_arr.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"mask must have shape (T, S) with T = {times_arr.shape[0]} "
                f"steps, got {tuple(mask_arr.shape)!r}"
            )
        if mask_arr.shape[1] == 0:
            raise ValueError("mask must cover at least one site (S >= 1)")
        _site_axes(site, mask_arr.shape[1])
        self.shared = shared
        self.site = site
        self.times = times_arr
        self.mask = mask_arr
        self.mean_fn = mean_fn

    @property
    def n_sites(self) -> int:
        """Number of sites $S$, ``mask.shape[1]``."""
        return self.mask.shape[1]

    @property
    def state_dim(self) -> int:
        """Joint state dimension $D = d_g + S d_h$."""
        return self.shared.state_dim + self.n_sites * self.site.state_dim

    @classmethod
    def from_sites(
        cls,
        shared: SDEKernel,
        site: SDEKernel,
        times_per_site: Sequence[Float[Array, " N_s"]],
        y_per_site: Sequence[Float[Array, " N_s"]],
        mean_fn: Callable[[Float[Array, " T"]], Float[Array, "T S"]] | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP, Float[Array, "T S"]]:
        r"""Merge ragged site series onto one grid and build the model.

        The grid is the sorted union of the site times,
        $\{t_1 < \dots < t_T\} = \bigcup_s \{t_{s,1}, \dots, t_{s,N_s}\}$;
        site $s$'s observations land in column $s$ at their own times, and
        every other entry is ``NaN`` and masked. Where `pyrox_ssm.pad_sites`
        pads each site on its own axis for a vmapped per-site factor, this
        lays every site on the shared axis that the shared GP needs. The
        union is taken with ``jnp.unique``, so the times must be concrete
        (call it outside `jax.jit`).

        Args:
            shared: The SDE kernel $k_g$ of the shared GP.
            site: The SDE kernel $k_h$ of the site GPs (scalar leaves pooled,
                leaves with a leading axis of length $S$ per site).
            times_per_site: One strictly increasing ``(N_s,)`` array of
                observation times per site.
            y_per_site: One ``(N_s,)`` array of observations per site.
            mean_fn: Optional per-site mean, as in the class.

        Returns:
            ``(model, y_grid)``: the model over the merged ``(T,)`` grid with
            its ``(T, S)`` mask, and the ``(T, S)`` observations, ``NaN``
            where a site was not observed.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no site is given, if the two sequences differ in
                length, if a site is not a non-empty 1-D series matching its
                observations, or if a site's times are not strictly
                increasing.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
            >>> kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=1.0, order=0)
            >>> model, y_grid = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP.from_sites(
            ...     kernel, kernel,
            ...     [jnp.array([0.0, 2.0]), jnp.array([1.0, 2.0])],
            ...     [jnp.array([0.5, 0.1]), jnp.array([0.3, 0.2])],
            ... )
            >>> model.times.tolist(), model.mask.tolist()
            ([0.0, 1.0, 2.0], [[True, False], [False, True], [True, True]])
        """
        if len(times_per_site) != len(y_per_site):
            raise ValueError(
                f"times_per_site has {len(times_per_site)} sites but y_per_site "
                f"has {len(y_per_site)}; pass one series of each per site."
            )
        if len(times_per_site) == 0:
            raise ValueError("from_sites needs at least one site.")
        t_dtype = jnp.result_type(*times_per_site, 0.0)
        y_dtype = jnp.result_type(*y_per_site, 0.0)
        sites = []
        for s, (t_s, y_s) in enumerate(zip(times_per_site, y_per_site, strict=True)):
            t_s = jnp.asarray(t_s, dtype=t_dtype)
            y_s = jnp.asarray(y_s, dtype=y_dtype)
            if t_s.ndim != 1 or t_s.shape[0] == 0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"site {s}: times must be a non-empty 1-D series, got shape "
                    f"{tuple(t_s.shape)!r}."
                )
            if y_s.shape != t_s.shape:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"site {s}: y has shape {tuple(y_s.shape)!r} but times has "
                    f"{tuple(t_s.shape)!r}; each observation needs one time."
                )
            if t_s.shape[0] >= 2 and not bool(jnp.all(jnp.diff(t_s) > 0)):
                raise ValueError(f"site {s}: times must be strictly increasing.")
            sites.append((t_s, y_s))

        times = jnp.unique(jnp.concatenate([t_s for t_s, _ in sites]))
        n_steps, n_sites = times.shape[0], len(sites)
        y_grid = jnp.full((n_steps, n_sites), jnp.nan, dtype=y_dtype)
        mask = jnp.zeros((n_steps, n_sites), dtype=bool)
        for s, (t_s, y_s) in enumerate(sites):
            rows = jnp.searchsorted(times, t_s)
            y_grid = y_grid.at[rows, s].set(y_s)
            mask = mask.at[rows, s].set(True)
        return cls(shared, site, times, mask, mean_fn), y_grid

    def _noise_vector(
        self, noise_var: Float[Array, ""] | Float[Array, " S"]
    ) -> Float[Array, " S"]:
        """``noise_var`` as the ``(S,)`` per-site observation variances."""
        noise_var = jnp.asarray(noise_var)
        if noise_var.shape not in ((), (self.n_sites,)):
            raise ValueError(
                f"noise_var must be a scalar or have shape ({self.n_sites},), "
                f"one variance per site, got {tuple(noise_var.shape)!r}"
            )
        return jnp.broadcast_to(noise_var, (self.n_sites,))

    def as_lgssm(
        self, noise_var: Float[Array, ""] | Float[Array, " S"]
    ) -> LinearGaussianSSMPrior:
        r"""This model as a `pyrox_ssm.LinearGaussianSSMPrior` over $D$ states.

        With $\Delta t_1 = 0$ and $\Delta t_k = t_k - t_{k-1}$, as in
        `pyrox_ssm.MarkovGPPrior.as_lgssm`,

        $$
        A_k = \mathrm{blockdiag}(A_k^{(g)}, A_k^{(h,1)}, \dots,
        A_k^{(h,S)}), \qquad
        Q_k = \mathrm{blockdiag}(Q_k^{(g)}, Q_k^{(h,1)}, \dots,
        Q_k^{(h,S)}),
        $$

        each block from its kernel's discretisation over $\Delta t_k$, so
        $A_1 = I$ and $Q_1 = 0$ and the first observation sees the initial
        state. $m_0 = 0$, $P_0$ is the block diagonal of each kernel's
        ``initial_covariance()`` ($P_\infty$ for a stationary kernel), the
        time-invariant observation matrix is the ``(S, D)`` stack of rows
        $H[s] = (H_g, 0, \dots, H_h \text{ at block } s, \dots, 0)$ and
        $R = \mathrm{diag}(\sigma_{n,1}^2, \dots, \sigma_{n,S}^2)$. With a
        ``mean_fn``, its ``(T, S)`` values on the grid are the observation
        offset $b_k$.

        Args:
            noise_var: Observation noise variance, a scalar shared by every
                site or one per site, shaped ``(S,)``.

        Returns:
            The `pyrox_ssm.LinearGaussianSSMPrior` with $T$ steps, state
            dimension $D = d_g + S d_h$ and $S$ outputs; filter it with
            ``mask=self.mask``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``noise_var`` is neither a scalar nor ``(S,)``, or
                if ``mean_fn`` does not return ``(T, S)``.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
            >>> kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=1.0, order=1)
            >>> model = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP(
            ...     kernel, kernel, jnp.arange(5.0), jnp.ones((5, 3), dtype=bool)
            ... )
            >>> lgssm = model.as_lgssm(jnp.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.1]))
            >>> lgssm.transition.shape, lgssm.obs_model.shape
            ((5, 8, 8), (3, 8))
        """
        n_sites = self.n_sites
        dt = _build_dt_full(self.times)
        A_g, Q_g = self.shared.discretise_sequence(dt)
        P_g = _kernel_initial_covariance(self.shared)
        H_g = self.shared.sde_params().H

        def site_model(kernel: SDEKernel):
            A_h, Q_h = kernel.discretise_sequence(dt)
            return A_h, Q_h, _kernel_initial_covariance(kernel), kernel.sde_params().H

        A_h, Q_h, P_h, H_h = _per_site(site_model, self.site, n_sites)
        # (S, T, d, d) → (T, S, d, d): one block per site at every step
        A_h = einx.id("s t i j -> t s i j", A_h)
        Q_h = einx.id("s t i j -> t s i j", Q_h)
        dtype = jnp.result_type(A_g, A_h)

        noise = self._noise_vector(noise_var).astype(dtype)
        init_cov = _stack_block_diag(P_g.astype(dtype), P_h.astype(dtype))
        offset = None if self.mean_fn is None else self.mean_fn(self.times)
        return LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
            transition=_stack_block_diag(A_g.astype(dtype), A_h.astype(dtype)),
            obs_model=_shared_plus_site_rows(H_g[0], H_h[:, 0]).astype(dtype),
            process_noise=_stack_block_diag(Q_g.astype(dtype), Q_h.astype(dtype)),
            obs_noise=jnp.diag(noise),
            init_mean=jnp.zeros(init_cov.shape[0], dtype=dtype),
            init_cov=init_cov,
            obs_offset=offset,
        )

    def log_marginal(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, "T S"],
        noise_var: Float[Array, ""] | Float[Array, " S"],
    ) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        r"""Marginal log-likelihood of the observed $(t, s)$ pairs.

        $$
        \log p(y_{\mathrm{obs}} \mid \theta) = \sum_{k=1}^{T}
          \log \mathcal{N}\!\left(y_{k, o_k};\, H_{o_k} m_k^-,\,
          H_{o_k} P_k^- H_{o_k}^\top + R_{o_k o_k}\right),
        $$

        with $o_k$ the sites observed at $t_k$ (``mask[k]``), equal to the
        dense Gaussian over the observed pairs.

        Args:
            y: Observations, shaped ``(T, S)``; unobserved entries may be
                ``NaN`` and reach neither the value nor a gradient.
            noise_var: Observation noise variance, scalar or ``(S,)``.

        Returns:
            The scalar log marginal.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
            >>> kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=1.0, order=0)
            >>> mask = jnp.array([[True, False], [True, True]])
            >>> times = jnp.arange(2.0)
            >>> model = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP(kernel, kernel, times, mask)
            >>> y = jnp.array([[0.3, jnp.nan], [0.1, -0.2]])
            >>> log_marg = model.log_marginal(y, jnp.asarray(0.1))
        """
        return self.as_lgssm(noise_var).log_marginal(y, mask=self.mask)

    def decompose(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, "T S"],
        noise_var: Float[Array, ""] | Float[Array, " S"],
        *,
        return_var: bool = False,
    ) -> (
        tuple[Float[Array, " T"], Float[Array, "T S"]]
        | tuple[
            Float[Array, " T"],
            Float[Array, "T S"],
            Float[Array, " T"],
            Float[Array, "T S"],
        ]
    ):
        r"""Posterior means, and optionally variances, of the shared and site GPs.

        Runs the Kalman filter and RTS smoother on `as_lgssm` and reads the
        blocks of the smoothed state mean $\hat{x}_k = \mathbb{E}[x_k \mid y]$,

        $$
        \mathbb{E}[g(t_k) \mid y] = H_g \hat{x}_{g,k}, \qquad
        \mathbb{E}[h_s(t_k) \mid y] = H_h \hat{x}_{h,s,k},
        $$

        so the two sum to the posterior mean of site $s$'s signal,
        $\mathbb{E}[g(t_k) + h_s(t_k) \mid y] = H[s] \hat{x}_k$. With
        ``return_var=True`` the marginal variances come from the same
        smoothed state covariance $\hat{P}_k$,

        $$
        \mathbb{V}[g(t_k) \mid y] = H_g \hat{P}_{gg,k} H_g^\top, \qquad
        \mathbb{V}[h_s(t_k) \mid y] = H_h \hat{P}_{h_s h_s,k} H_h^\top .
        $$

        The two parts are correlated a posteriori (one observation informs
        both), so their variances do not add to the variance of
        $g + h_s$, $H[s] \hat{P}_k H[s]^\top$. The RTS smoother solves
        against the predicted state covariance, so a kernel of exactly zero
        variance (a singular block) gives ``NaN`` here; `log_marginal` is unaffected.

        Args:
            y: Observations, shaped ``(T, S)``; unobserved entries may be
                ``NaN``.
            noise_var: Observation noise variance, scalar or ``(S,)``.
            return_var: Also return the marginal variances.

        Returns:
            ``(g_mean, h_mean)``: $\mathbb{E}[g \mid y]$ on the grid,
            ``(T,)``, and $\mathbb{E}[h_s \mid y]$, ``(T, S)``. With
            ``return_var=True``, ``(g_mean, h_mean, g_var, h_var)``, the
            variances shaped like the means.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
            >>> kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=1.0, order=0)
            >>> mask = jnp.array([[True, False], [True, True]])
            >>> times = jnp.arange(2.0)
            >>> model = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP(kernel, kernel, times, mask)
            >>> y = jnp.array([[0.3, jnp.nan], [0.1, -0.2]])
            >>> g_mean, h_mean = model.decompose(y, jnp.asarray(0.1))
            >>> g_mean.shape, h_mean.shape
            ((2,), (2, 2))
        """
        lgssm = self.as_lgssm(noise_var)
        means, covs, _ = lgssm.smooth(y, mask=self.mask)
        d_g, d_h = self.shared.state_dim, self.site.state_dim
        n_steps, n_sites = means.shape[0], self.n_sites
        H = lgssm.obs_model
        # H[s] = (H_g, 0, …, H_h at block s, …, 0): read each block separately
        H_g = H[0, :d_g]
        g_mean = einx.dot("t i, i -> t", means[:, :d_g], H_g)
        site_means = means[:, d_g:].reshape(n_steps, n_sites, d_h)
        H_h = H[:, d_g:].reshape(n_sites, n_sites, d_h)
        H_h = jnp.diagonal(H_h, axis1=0, axis2=1).T  # (S, d_h), row s = H_h,s
        h_mean = einx.dot("t s i, s i -> t s", site_means, H_h)
        if not return_var:
            return g_mean, h_mean
        # V[g] = H_g P̂_gg H_gᵀ
        g_var = einx.dot("t i j, i, j -> t", covs[:, :d_g, :d_g], H_g, H_g)
        # the (d_h, d_h) diagonal block of each site: P̂_{h_s h_s}
        site_cov = covs[:, d_g:, d_g:].reshape(n_steps, n_sites, d_h, n_sites, d_h)
        site_cov = jnp.diagonal(site_cov, axis1=1, axis2=3)  # (T, d_h, d_h, S)
        # V[h_s] = H_h,s P̂_{h_s h_s} H_h,sᵀ
        h_var = einx.dot("t i j s, s i, s j -> t s", site_cov, H_h, H_h)
        return g_mean, h_mean, g_var, h_var

    def condition(
        self,
        y: Float[Array, "T S"],
        noise_var: Float[Array, ""] | Float[Array, " S"],
    ) -> ConditionedSharedPlusSiteMarkovGP:
        r"""Condition on the observations, to predict $g$ and $h_s$ at any times.

        Args:
            y: Observations on the grid, ``(T, S)``; unobserved entries may be
                ``NaN``.
            noise_var: Observation noise variance, scalar or ``(S,)``.

        Returns:
            A `ConditionedSharedPlusSiteMarkovGP`, whose ``predict(t_star)``
            gives the posterior marginals of the shared and site signals.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``y`` is not ``(T, S)`` or ``noise_var`` is neither
                a scalar nor ``(S,)``.

        Examples:
            >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
            >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
            >>> kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=1.0, order=0)
            >>> mask = jnp.array([[True, False], [True, True]])
            >>> times = jnp.arange(2.0)
            >>> model = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP(kernel, kernel, times, mask)
            >>> y = jnp.array([[0.3, jnp.nan], [0.1, -0.2]])
            >>> cond = model.condition(y, jnp.asarray(0.1))
            >>> g_mean, h_mean, g_var, h_var = cond.predict(jnp.array([0.5, 3.0]))
        """
        y = jnp.asarray(y)
        if y.shape != self.mask.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"y must have the mask's shape {tuple(self.mask.shape)!r}, got "
                f"{tuple(y.shape)!r}"
            )
        noise_var = jnp.asarray(noise_var)
        self._noise_vector(noise_var)  # validates the shape
        return ConditionedSharedPlusSiteMarkovGP(self, y, noise_var)

>>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
>>> kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=1.0, order=0)
>>> model, y_grid = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP.from_sites(
...     kernel, kernel,
...     [jnp.array([0.0, 2.0]), jnp.array([1.0, 2.0])],
...     [jnp.array([0.5, 0.1]), jnp.array([0.3, 0.2])],
... )
>>> model.times.tolist(), model.mask.tolist()

@classmethod
def from_sites(
    cls,
    shared: SDEKernel,
    site: SDEKernel,
    times_per_site: Sequence[Float[Array, " N_s"]],
    y_per_site: Sequence[Float[Array, " N_s"]],
    mean_fn: Callable[[Float[Array, " T"]], Float[Array, "T S"]] | None = None,
) -> tuple[SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP, Float[Array, "T S"]]:
    r"""Merge ragged site series onto one grid and build the model.

    The grid is the sorted union of the site times,
    $\{t_1 < \dots < t_T\} = \bigcup_s \{t_{s,1}, \dots, t_{s,N_s}\}$;
    site $s$'s observations land in column $s$ at their own times, and
    every other entry is ``NaN`` and masked. Where `pyrox_ssm.pad_sites`
    pads each site on its own axis for a vmapped per-site factor, this
    lays every site on the shared axis that the shared GP needs. The
    union is taken with ``jnp.unique``, so the times must be concrete
    (call it outside `jax.jit`).

    Args:
        shared: The SDE kernel $k_g$ of the shared GP.
        site: The SDE kernel $k_h$ of the site GPs (scalar leaves pooled,
            leaves with a leading axis of length $S$ per site).
        times_per_site: One strictly increasing ``(N_s,)`` array of
            observation times per site.
        y_per_site: One ``(N_s,)`` array of observations per site.
        mean_fn: Optional per-site mean, as in the class.

    Returns:
        ``(model, y_grid)``: the model over the merged ``(T,)`` grid with
        its ``(T, S)`` mask, and the ``(T, S)`` observations, ``NaN``
        where a site was not observed.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no site is given, if the two sequences differ in
            length, if a site is not a non-empty 1-D series matching its
            observations, or if a site's times are not strictly
            increasing.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=1.0, order=0)
        >>> model, y_grid = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP.from_sites(
        ...     kernel, kernel,
        ...     [jnp.array([0.0, 2.0]), jnp.array([1.0, 2.0])],
        ...     [jnp.array([0.5, 0.1]), jnp.array([0.3, 0.2])],
        ... )
        >>> model.times.tolist(), model.mask.tolist()
        ([0.0, 1.0, 2.0], [[True, False], [False, True], [True, True]])
    """
    if len(times_per_site) != len(y_per_site):
        raise ValueError(
            f"times_per_site has {len(times_per_site)} sites but y_per_site "
            f"has {len(y_per_site)}; pass one series of each per site."
        )
    if len(times_per_site) == 0:
        raise ValueError("from_sites needs at least one site.")
    t_dtype = jnp.result_type(*times_per_site, 0.0)
    y_dtype = jnp.result_type(*y_per_site, 0.0)
    sites = []
    for s, (t_s, y_s) in enumerate(zip(times_per_site, y_per_site, strict=True)):
        t_s = jnp.asarray(t_s, dtype=t_dtype)
        y_s = jnp.asarray(y_s, dtype=y_dtype)
        if t_s.ndim != 1 or t_s.shape[0] == 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"site {s}: times must be a non-empty 1-D series, got shape "
                f"{tuple(t_s.shape)!r}."
            )
        if y_s.shape != t_s.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"site {s}: y has shape {tuple(y_s.shape)!r} but times has "
                f"{tuple(t_s.shape)!r}; each observation needs one time."
            )
        if t_s.shape[0] >= 2 and not bool(jnp.all(jnp.diff(t_s) > 0)):
            raise ValueError(f"site {s}: times must be strictly increasing.")
        sites.append((t_s, y_s))

    times = jnp.unique(jnp.concatenate([t_s for t_s, _ in sites]))
    n_steps, n_sites = times.shape[0], len(sites)
    y_grid = jnp.full((n_steps, n_sites), jnp.nan, dtype=y_dtype)
    mask = jnp.zeros((n_steps, n_sites), dtype=bool)
    for s, (t_s, y_s) in enumerate(sites):
        rows = jnp.searchsorted(times, t_s)
        y_grid = y_grid.at[rows, s].set(y_s)
        mask = mask.at[rows, s].set(True)
    return cls(shared, site, times, mask, mean_fn), y_grid

...     kernel, kernel, jnp.arange(5.0), jnp.ones((5, 3), dtype=bool)

def as_lgssm(
    self, noise_var: Float[Array, ""] | Float[Array, " S"]
) -> LinearGaussianSSMPrior:
    r"""This model as a `pyrox_ssm.LinearGaussianSSMPrior` over $D$ states.

    With $\Delta t_1 = 0$ and $\Delta t_k = t_k - t_{k-1}$, as in
    `pyrox_ssm.MarkovGPPrior.as_lgssm`,

    $$
    A_k = \mathrm{blockdiag}(A_k^{(g)}, A_k^{(h,1)}, \dots,
    A_k^{(h,S)}), \qquad
    Q_k = \mathrm{blockdiag}(Q_k^{(g)}, Q_k^{(h,1)}, \dots,
    Q_k^{(h,S)}),
    $$

    each block from its kernel's discretisation over $\Delta t_k$, so
    $A_1 = I$ and $Q_1 = 0$ and the first observation sees the initial
    state. $m_0 = 0$, $P_0$ is the block diagonal of each kernel's
    ``initial_covariance()`` ($P_\infty$ for a stationary kernel), the
    time-invariant observation matrix is the ``(S, D)`` stack of rows
    $H[s] = (H_g, 0, \dots, H_h \text{ at block } s, \dots, 0)$ and
    $R = \mathrm{diag}(\sigma_{n,1}^2, \dots, \sigma_{n,S}^2)$. With a
    ``mean_fn``, its ``(T, S)`` values on the grid are the observation
    offset $b_k$.

    Args:
        noise_var: Observation noise variance, a scalar shared by every
            site or one per site, shaped ``(S,)``.

    Returns:
        The `pyrox_ssm.LinearGaussianSSMPrior` with $T$ steps, state
        dimension $D = d_g + S d_h$ and $S$ outputs; filter it with
        ``mask=self.mask``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``noise_var`` is neither a scalar nor ``(S,)``, or
            if ``mean_fn`` does not return ``(T, S)``.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=1.0, order=1)
        >>> model = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP(
        ...     kernel, kernel, jnp.arange(5.0), jnp.ones((5, 3), dtype=bool)
        ... )
        >>> lgssm = model.as_lgssm(jnp.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.1]))
        >>> lgssm.transition.shape, lgssm.obs_model.shape
        ((5, 8, 8), (3, 8))
    """
    n_sites = self.n_sites
    dt = _build_dt_full(self.times)
    A_g, Q_g = self.shared.discretise_sequence(dt)
    P_g = _kernel_initial_covariance(self.shared)
    H_g = self.shared.sde_params().H

    def site_model(kernel: SDEKernel):
        A_h, Q_h = kernel.discretise_sequence(dt)
        return A_h, Q_h, _kernel_initial_covariance(kernel), kernel.sde_params().H

    A_h, Q_h, P_h, H_h = _per_site(site_model, self.site, n_sites)
    # (S, T, d, d) → (T, S, d, d): one block per site at every step
    A_h = einx.id("s t i j -> t s i j", A_h)
    Q_h = einx.id("s t i j -> t s i j", Q_h)
    dtype = jnp.result_type(A_g, A_h)

    noise = self._noise_vector(noise_var).astype(dtype)
    init_cov = _stack_block_diag(P_g.astype(dtype), P_h.astype(dtype))
    offset = None if self.mean_fn is None else self.mean_fn(self.times)
    return LinearGaussianSSMPrior(
        transition=_stack_block_diag(A_g.astype(dtype), A_h.astype(dtype)),
        obs_model=_shared_plus_site_rows(H_g[0], H_h[:, 0]).astype(dtype),
        process_noise=_stack_block_diag(Q_g.astype(dtype), Q_h.astype(dtype)),
        obs_noise=jnp.diag(noise),
        init_mean=jnp.zeros(init_cov.shape[0], dtype=dtype),
        init_cov=init_cov,
        obs_offset=offset,
    )

def log_marginal(
    self,
    y: Float[Array, "T S"],
    noise_var: Float[Array, ""] | Float[Array, " S"],
) -> Float[Array, ""]:
    r"""Marginal log-likelihood of the observed $(t, s)$ pairs.

    $$
    \log p(y_{\mathrm{obs}} \mid \theta) = \sum_{k=1}^{T}
      \log \mathcal{N}\!\left(y_{k, o_k};\, H_{o_k} m_k^-,\,
      H_{o_k} P_k^- H_{o_k}^\top + R_{o_k o_k}\right),
    $$

    with $o_k$ the sites observed at $t_k$ (``mask[k]``), equal to the
    dense Gaussian over the observed pairs.

    Args:
        y: Observations, shaped ``(T, S)``; unobserved entries may be
            ``NaN`` and reach neither the value nor a gradient.
        noise_var: Observation noise variance, scalar or ``(S,)``.

    Returns:
        The scalar log marginal.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import pyrox_ssm as pss
        >>> kernel = pss.MaternSDE(variance=1.0, lengthscale=1.0, order=0)
        >>> mask = jnp.array([[True, False], [True, True]])
        >>> times = jnp.arange(2.0)
        >>> model = pss.SharedPlusSiteMarkovGP(kernel, kernel, times, mask)
        >>> y = jnp.array([[0.3, jnp.nan], [0.1, -0.2]])
        >>> log_marg = model.log_marginal(y, jnp.asarray(0.1))
    """
    return self.as_lgssm(noise_var).log_marginal(y, mask=self.mask)

Posterior means, and optionally variances, of the shared and site GPs.

Runs the Kalman filter and RTS smoother on as_lgssm and reads the blocks of the smoothed state mean \(\hat{x}_k = \mathbb{E}[x_k \mid y]\),

\[ \mathbb{E}[g(t_k) \mid y] = H_g \hat{x}_{g,k}, \qquad \mathbb{E}[h_s(t_k) \mid y] = H_h \hat{x}_{h,s,k}, \]

so the two sum to the posterior mean of site \(s\)'s signal, \(\mathbb{E}[g(t_k) + h_s(t_k) \mid y] = H[s] \hat{x}_k\). With return_var=True the marginal variances come from the same smoothed state covariance \(\hat{P}_k\),

The two parts are correlated a posteriori (one observation informs both), so their variances do not add to the variance of \(g + h_s\), \(H[s] \hat{P}_k H[s]^\top\). The RTS smoother solves against the predicted state covariance, so a kernel of exactly zero variance (a singular block) gives NaN here; log_marginal is unaffected.
